# CRO Strategy Playbook

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Playbook for CRO strategy across ecom builds.

## Funnel stages + benchmarks

| Stage | Benchmark (median DTC) | Top quartile |
|-------|------------------------|--------------|
| Visitor → Cart | 5-8% | 12%+ |
| Cart → Checkout | 40-50% | 65%+ |
| Checkout → Purchase | 65-75% | 85%+ |
| First Purchase → Repeat | 25-35% | 50%+ |
| Subscriber retention (90d) | 55-65% | 80%+ |

## Lift mandate
40%+ relative improvement on baseline per surface tested.

## Test prioritization (ICE)
- **Impact (1-10):** Estimated revenue lift if winning
- **Confidence (1-10):** How sure are we this beats control? Decoder bank confidence boost.
- **Ease (1-10):** Implementation effort (10 = same-day, 1 = multi-week)
- **Score = I × C × E** (max 1000)
- Tests below 200 don't run

## Sequencing rules
- 1-2 tests live per project per week
- Don't run >3 tests on same surface simultaneously (cross-contamination)
- Holdout cohort for top tests (90/10 split, 8-week minimum)
- Statistical significance gate: 95% confidence + MDE met + 2-week run minimum

## Surface priority order (default)
1. PDP hero (highest leverage on first-touch)
2. Cart drawer mechanics
3. Checkout flow (steps, express, address)
4. Post-purchase upsell
5. Subscription toggle
6. Email signup discount
7. Listing filters
8. FAQ structure

## Per-niche adjustments
- Apparel: fit-finder UX often beats hero (size-uncertainty is #1 objection)
- Supplements: trust signals dominate (third-party testing > everything)
- Beauty: shade-finder + ingredient transparency
- Home: configurator UX, room-context photography
- Tech: spec-table positioning, comparison-with-competitors

## Playbook patterns

### Pattern 1: Above-fold trust trio
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day return policy
Place above primary CTA. 8-15% lift on visitor→cart in skeptical niches.

### Pattern 2: Cart drawer free-shipping bar
- Threshold $50-80 (median)
- Progress bar with celebration on complete
- 12-18% AOV lift typical

### Pattern 3: Checkout express-first
- Shop Pay / Apple Pay / PayPal above the form on mobile
- Reduce mobile checkout abandonment 15-25%

### Pattern 4: Post-purchase one-click upsell
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single-click add (no re-payment)
- 8-15% AOV lift

### Pattern 5: Subscription default
- Default-select subscribe vs. one-time on PDP
- Caveat: only if churn-prevention strong
- 25-40% subscription rate lift

## Lessons captured
- Cross-project lessons append to `memory/patterns/good/cro-lessons-cross-project.md`
- Validated patterns promote to `cro-decoded-patterns.md`
- Failed patterns demote to `patterns/avoid/`

# Scope Split Enforcement

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Reject overlapping work between spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence.

## The four lines

| Specialist | Owns | Forbidden territory |
|------------|------|---------------------|
| spark | Above-fold copy: hero headline/subhead/badge, primary CTA, PDP hero block | Below-fold sections, mechanics, cart, checkout, body, FAQ |
| ecom-cro | Below-fold mechanics: variants, bundles, cart, checkout, upsell, subscription, post-purchase, abandon triggers | Copy text, hero, marketing pages, brand voice |
| merch | On-page copy: PDP body, bullets, FAQ, size guide, cart microcopy, checkout reassurance, post-purchase confirmation, subscription page, objections | Hero, mechanics, A/B prioritization, lifecycle email |
| sequence | Lifecycle email: welcome, cart abandon, browse abandon, post-purchase, win-back, subscription nurture | On-page copy, mechanics, hero, transactional one-offs |

## PR review heuristic

When a PR arrives, identify the author and verify changes match scope:

### Spark PR check
- Touches `app/page.tsx` hero block? OK
- Touches `app/products/[handle]/page.tsx` hero zone? OK
- Touches `components/pdp-body.tsx`? **REJECT — merch.**
- Touches `components/cart-drawer.tsx` mechanics? **REJECT — ecom-cro.**
- Touches `lib/email/welcome.ts`? **REJECT — sequence.**

### Ecom-CRO PR check
- Touches `components/cart-drawer.tsx` mechanic logic? OK
- Touches `lib/cart/cart-state.ts`? OK
- Touches text content in cart drawer (literal strings)? **REJECT — merch.**
- Touches hero copy? **REJECT — spark.**
- Touches email send logic? Trigger config OK; email content **REJECT — sequence.**

### Merch PR check
- Touches `content/products/*.md` (description content)? OK
- Touches `components/pdp-body.tsx` (text only)? OK
- Touches PDP hero copy? **REJECT — spark.**
- Touches mechanic logic in `lib/cart/`? **REJECT — ecom-cro.**
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/`? **REJECT — sequence.**

### Sequence PR check
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/welcome.ts`? OK
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/cart-abandon.ts`? OK
- Touches `lib/email/transactional/order-confirmation.ts`? **REJECT — quill / postmark.**
- Touches PDP body? **REJECT — merch.**

## Edge case decisions

### Cart microcopy with mechanic implication
"Add $12 more for free shipping"
- Mechanic (threshold logic, progress bar): ecom-cro
- Text content: merch
- Both ship parallel; catalyst ratifies integration

### Hero CTA copy with mechanic
"Shop the bundle" (bundle exists)
- CTA copy: spark
- Bundle pricing logic: ecom-cro
- Bundle eligibility rules: ecom-cro

### Lifecycle email referencing PDP language
- Email content + cadence: sequence
- May reference merch's PDP language for consistency
- Don't copy-paste — reference

## Violation log

Append to `memory/patterns/avoid/cro-scope-violations.md`:

```markdown
## 2026-04-30 — spark
- Severity: minor (8 lines)
- File: components/pdp-body.tsx
- Issue: spark wrote benefit bullets (merch territory)
- Decision: split PR, re-dispatch to merch
- Specialist response: acknowledged
```

## Repeat-offender protocol
- 2+ violations in 30 days from same specialist → escalate to cadence (HR)
- Cadence schedules retraining cycle
- Tutor delivers scope-clarification training

## When in doubt
- File path test: which `components/*` directory does the change live in?
- Verb test: is the change a "what" (copy text) or "how" (mechanic logic)?
- Layer test: above-fold (spark) / below-fold UI mechanic (ecom-cro) / below-fold text (merch) / inbox (sequence)?

# A/B Test Prioritization

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** ICE-scored test roadmap + statistical significance gates.

## ICE Scoring

For every proposed test:

### Impact (1-10)
- 10: Above-fold PDP / hero (every visitor sees)
- 8: Cart drawer (every cart-creator)
- 7: Checkout step
- 6: Post-purchase upsell
- 5: Subscription toggle
- 4: FAQ rewrite
- 3: Listing filter UX
- 2: Footer CTAs
- 1: Account-page tweak

### Confidence (1-10)
- 10: Pattern observed in 8+ decoder brands and validated in past tests
- 8: Pattern in 5+ decoder brands
- 6: Pattern in 3+ decoder brands
- 4: Speculative; based on niche audit
- 2: Untested hypothesis

### Ease (1-10)
- 10: Same-day implementation
- 8: 2-3 day spec + ship
- 6: 1 week
- 4: 2 weeks
- 2: Multi-week effort

### Score = I × C × E (max 1000)

| Score | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| 600+ | Run this week |
| 300-600 | Queue next 2 weeks |
| 200-300 | Queue when bandwidth |
| <200 | Don't run |

## Statistical Significance Gates

Every test must hit ALL gates before declaring winner:

### Gate 1: Run length
- Minimum 14 days
- Captures full week cycle (weekday/weekend behavior)

### Gate 2: Sample size / MDE
- Compute MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) for desired confidence
- Default: 95% confidence, 80% power
- For 5% baseline conversion + 10% MDE → ~22,000 visitors per variant
- Tools: Optimizely calculator, Evan Miller's calculator

### Gate 3: P-value < 0.05
- Two-sided test
- Bayesian alternative: 95% probability variant beats control

### Gate 4: No SRM (Sample Ratio Mismatch)
- Verify 50/50 split actually delivered ~50/50 traffic
- If skewed >5%, investigate instrumentation

### Gate 5: Effect size meaningful
- Lift must be ≥10% (don't ship 2% wins; not worth coordination cost)

## Test design rules

### Single-variable tests
- Default. Easy to attribute.

### Multi-variable tests
- Allowed for above-fold A/B/C variants from spark (3 variants of headline)
- Each variant must be a complete spec (not a/b/c on individual elements)

### Holdouts
- For top tests: 90/10 split
- Holdout cohort sees control for 8+ weeks even after winner declared
- Measures long-term retention impact (winner may lose at week 12)

### Sequential testing
- Allowed ONLY when test feeds next test (e.g., hero variant → bundle picker variant)
- Otherwise run parallel on independent surfaces

## Lift attribution

After test completion:
- Compute lift % vs control
- Verify gates 1-5
- Attribute to specialist (spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence)
- Update `cro-decoded-patterns.md` with validated win
- Notify Echo + Yash via weekly CRO report

## Weekly cadence
- Monday: review prior week's results, declare winners/losers
- Tuesday: ship new variants (specialists)
- Wednesday: deploy to A/B framework
- Thursday-Sunday: monitor (Orbit dashboards)
- Friday afternoon: Decoder delta + roadmap update for next week

# Hero Headline Formulas

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Niche-adapted headline formulas for ecom heroes.

## Universal rules
- ≤8 words
- Outcome-first
- Specific number when possible
- Active voice
- No banned words (leverage / synergy / innovative / seamless / robust / cutting-edge / next-gen / best-in-class)

## Per-niche formulas

### Apparel
- **Pain → Solution:** "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- **Outcome + Material:** "Sleep-soft tees built to last."
- **Time-bound:** "Pack one, wear three days."
- **Anti-positioning:** "Not your grandfather's wool."

### Beauty
- **Outcome + Time:** "Glowing skin in 14 days."
- **Inclusive:** "60+ shades. One radical formula."
- **Ingredient-led:** "Hyaluronic acid, finally done right."
- **Result-vs-feature:** "Concealer that doesn't crease."

### Supplements
- **Specific benefit + Time:** "Energy in 5 minutes. No crash."
- **Quantified outcome:** "30 days to a stronger gut."
- **Trust-led:** "Third-party tested. Doctor formulated."
- **Anti-positioning:** "What your multivitamin missed."

### CPG (food/drink)
- **Sensory + Outcome:** "Cravings handled. Macros locked."
- **Indulgence-permission:** "Soda your gut will thank you for."
- **Number-led:** "20g protein. 4g sugar. Done."

### Home
- **Outcome + Time:** "Better sleep starts tonight."
- **Material-led:** "Organic cotton, made to outlast."
- **Anti-fast:** "Furniture that'll outlive your lease."

### Tech / connected
- **Outcome + Mechanism:** "Sleep deeper. Recover faster."
- **Spec-led benefit:** "Pod-tech sleep. Measurable proof."
- **Anti-tracker:** "More than a tracker. A sleep coach."

### Pet
- **Concern + Solution:** "Real food. Real ingredients. Tail-wagging proof."
- **Personalization:** "Your dog's perfect plate, delivered."

### Subscription / personal care
- **Convenience-led:** "Razors at your door. Half the price."
- **Anti-friction:** "Skincare without the guesswork."

## Subhead formulas
Pattern: **Pain acknowledgment + Solution mechanism + Proof hint**

≤25 words, 1-2 sentences.

Example:
- Headline: "Stop wearing scratchy wool. Start with merino."
- Subhead: "Hand-knit merino tees, 30-day comfort guarantee. Soft enough to sleep in. Worn by 200,000+."

## CTA formulas
≤4 words. Action verb + benefit.

| Niche | Low-friction | Standard | Commitment |
|-------|--------------|----------|------------|
| Apparel | "Try a tee" | "Shop merino" | "Add to bag" |
| Beauty | "See shades" | "Shop now" | "Get yours" |
| Supplements | "Start free" | "Try 30 days" | "Subscribe + save" |
| Subscription | "Join free" | "Get started" | "Subscribe" |

## Badge formulas
≤3 words. Announcement / category / status.

- "New collection"
- "Best seller"
- "Limited drop"
- "Just dropped"
- "Now subscription"

# CTA Copy Variants

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Above-fold CTA copy generation.

## Universal rules
- ≤4 words
- Action verb first
- Benefit clear
- 3 sub-variants per primary CTA (low-friction / standard / commitment)

## Action verb library
- Start, Shop, Try, Get, Add, Build, Join, See, Browse, Pick, Choose, Find, Discover, Unlock, Save, Subscribe, Order, Reserve, Claim

## Avoid
- "Learn more" — too vague
- "Click here" — anti-pattern
- "Get started" — overused (use only when product-led signup)
- "Submit" — clinical
- "Sign up" — friction-prime

## Three-variant pattern (per dispatch)

### Low-friction
- Optimize for clicks (commitment can come later)
- Example: "Try free", "See shades", "Browse drops"

### Standard
- Optimize for ratio of click + intent
- Example: "Shop merino", "Get the kit", "Find your shade"

### Commitment
- Optimize for high-intent shoppers ready to buy
- Example: "Add to bag", "Subscribe + save 20%", "Order now"

- "Add to Cart" (universal)
- "Get Yours" (commitment-led)

### Subscription toggle CTA
- "Subscribe + save 20%"
- "Lock in 15% off"
- "Set + forget"

### Variant trigger CTAs
- "Choose color"
- "Pick size"
- "Select bundle"

- Shop Pay
- Apple Pay
- Google Pay
- PayPal

- Primary: commitment-prime ("Shop now")
- Secondary: low-friction ("See lookbook", "Watch video", "Read story")

Trust-prime under CTA:
- "Free shipping over $50"
- "30-day returns, no questions"
- "No subscription required"

# CRO Strategy Playbook

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Playbook for CRO strategy across ecom builds.

## Funnel stages + benchmarks

| Stage | Benchmark (median DTC) | Top quartile |
|-------|------------------------|--------------|
| Visitor → Cart | 5-8% | 12%+ |
| Cart → Checkout | 40-50% | 65%+ |
| Checkout → Purchase | 65-75% | 85%+ |
| First Purchase → Repeat | 25-35% | 50%+ |
| Subscriber retention (90d) | 55-65% | 80%+ |

## Lift mandate
40%+ relative improvement on baseline per surface tested.

## Test prioritization (ICE)
- **Impact (1-10):** Estimated revenue lift if winning
- **Confidence (1-10):** How sure are we this beats control? Decoder bank confidence boost.
- **Ease (1-10):** Implementation effort (10 = same-day, 1 = multi-week)
- **Score = I × C × E** (max 1000)
- Tests below 200 don't run

## Sequencing rules
- 1-2 tests live per project per week
- Don't run >3 tests on same surface simultaneously (cross-contamination)
- Holdout cohort for top tests (90/10 split, 8-week minimum)
- Statistical significance gate: 95% confidence + MDE met + 2-week run minimum

## Surface priority order (default)
1. PDP hero (highest leverage on first-touch)
2. Cart drawer mechanics
3. Checkout flow (steps, express, address)
4. Post-purchase upsell
5. Subscription toggle
6. Email signup discount
7. Listing filters
8. FAQ structure

## Per-niche adjustments
- Apparel: fit-finder UX often beats hero (size-uncertainty is #1 objection)
- Supplements: trust signals dominate (third-party testing > everything)
- Beauty: shade-finder + ingredient transparency
- Home: configurator UX, room-context photography
- Tech: spec-table positioning, comparison-with-competitors

## Playbook patterns

### Pattern 1: Above-fold trust trio
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day return policy
Place above primary CTA. 8-15% lift on visitor→cart in skeptical niches.

### Pattern 2: Cart drawer free-shipping bar
- Threshold $50-80 (median)
- Progress bar with celebration on complete
- 12-18% AOV lift typical

### Pattern 3: Checkout express-first
- Shop Pay / Apple Pay / PayPal above the form on mobile
- Reduce mobile checkout abandonment 15-25%

### Pattern 4: Post-purchase one-click upsell
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single-click add (no re-payment)
- 8-15% AOV lift

### Pattern 5: Subscription default
- Default-select subscribe vs. one-time on PDP
- Caveat: only if churn-prevention strong
- 25-40% subscription rate lift

## Lessons captured
- Cross-project lessons append to `memory/patterns/good/cro-lessons-cross-project.md`
- Validated patterns promote to `cro-decoded-patterns.md`
- Failed patterns demote to `patterns/avoid/`

# Scope Split Enforcement

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** Reject overlapping work between spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence.

## The four lines

| Specialist | Owns | Forbidden territory |
|------------|------|---------------------|
| spark | Above-fold copy: hero headline/subhead/badge, primary CTA, PDP hero block | Below-fold sections, mechanics, cart, checkout, body, FAQ |
| ecom-cro | Below-fold mechanics: variants, bundles, cart, checkout, upsell, subscription, post-purchase, abandon triggers | Copy text, hero, marketing pages, brand voice |
| merch | On-page copy: PDP body, bullets, FAQ, size guide, cart microcopy, checkout reassurance, post-purchase confirmation, subscription page, objections | Hero, mechanics, A/B prioritization, lifecycle email |
| sequence | Lifecycle email: welcome, cart abandon, browse abandon, post-purchase, win-back, subscription nurture | On-page copy, mechanics, hero, transactional one-offs |

## PR review heuristic

When a PR arrives, identify the author and verify changes match scope:

### Spark PR check
- Touches `app/page.tsx` hero block? OK
- Touches `app/products/[handle]/page.tsx` hero zone? OK
- Touches `components/pdp-body.tsx`? **REJECT — merch.**
- Touches `components/cart-drawer.tsx` mechanics? **REJECT — ecom-cro.**
- Touches `lib/email/welcome.ts`? **REJECT — sequence.**

### Ecom-CRO PR check
- Touches `components/cart-drawer.tsx` mechanic logic? OK
- Touches `lib/cart/cart-state.ts`? OK
- Touches text content in cart drawer (literal strings)? **REJECT — merch.**
- Touches hero copy? **REJECT — spark.**
- Touches email send logic? Trigger config OK; email content **REJECT — sequence.**

### Merch PR check
- Touches `content/products/*.md` (description content)? OK
- Touches `components/pdp-body.tsx` (text only)? OK
- Touches PDP hero copy? **REJECT — spark.**
- Touches mechanic logic in `lib/cart/`? **REJECT — ecom-cro.**
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/`? **REJECT — sequence.**

### Sequence PR check
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/welcome.ts`? OK
- Touches `lib/email/sequences/cart-abandon.ts`? OK
- Touches `lib/email/transactional/order-confirmation.ts`? **REJECT — quill / postmark.**
- Touches PDP body? **REJECT — merch.**

## Edge case decisions

### Cart microcopy with mechanic implication
"Add $12 more for free shipping"
- Mechanic (threshold logic, progress bar): ecom-cro
- Text content: merch
- Both ship parallel; catalyst ratifies integration

### Hero CTA copy with mechanic
"Shop the bundle" (bundle exists)
- CTA copy: spark
- Bundle pricing logic: ecom-cro
- Bundle eligibility rules: ecom-cro

### Lifecycle email referencing PDP language
- Email content + cadence: sequence
- May reference merch's PDP language for consistency
- Don't copy-paste — reference

## Violation log

Append to `memory/patterns/avoid/cro-scope-violations.md`:

```markdown
## 2026-04-30 — spark
- Severity: minor (8 lines)
- File: components/pdp-body.tsx
- Issue: spark wrote benefit bullets (merch territory)
- Decision: split PR, re-dispatch to merch
- Specialist response: acknowledged
```

## Repeat-offender protocol
- 2+ violations in 30 days from same specialist → escalate to cadence (HR)
- Cadence schedules retraining cycle
- Tutor delivers scope-clarification training

## When in doubt
- File path test: which `components/*` directory does the change live in?
- Verb test: is the change a "what" (copy text) or "how" (mechanic logic)?
- Layer test: above-fold (spark) / below-fold UI mechanic (ecom-cro) / below-fold text (merch) / inbox (sequence)?

# A/B Test Prioritization

**Owner:** catalyst
**Scope:** ICE-scored test roadmap + statistical significance gates.

## ICE Scoring

For every proposed test:

### Impact (1-10)
- 10: Above-fold PDP / hero (every visitor sees)
- 8: Cart drawer (every cart-creator)
- 7: Checkout step
- 6: Post-purchase upsell
- 5: Subscription toggle
- 4: FAQ rewrite
- 3: Listing filter UX
- 2: Footer CTAs
- 1: Account-page tweak

### Confidence (1-10)
- 10: Pattern observed in 8+ decoder brands and validated in past tests
- 8: Pattern in 5+ decoder brands
- 6: Pattern in 3+ decoder brands
- 4: Speculative; based on niche audit
- 2: Untested hypothesis

### Ease (1-10)
- 10: Same-day implementation
- 8: 2-3 day spec + ship
- 6: 1 week
- 4: 2 weeks
- 2: Multi-week effort

### Score = I × C × E (max 1000)

| Score | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| 600+ | Run this week |
| 300-600 | Queue next 2 weeks |
| 200-300 | Queue when bandwidth |
| <200 | Don't run |

## Statistical Significance Gates

Every test must hit ALL gates before declaring winner:

### Gate 1: Run length
- Minimum 14 days
- Captures full week cycle (weekday/weekend behavior)

### Gate 2: Sample size / MDE
- Compute MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) for desired confidence
- Default: 95% confidence, 80% power
- For 5% baseline conversion + 10% MDE → ~22,000 visitors per variant
- Tools: Optimizely calculator, Evan Miller's calculator

### Gate 3: P-value < 0.05
- Two-sided test
- Bayesian alternative: 95% probability variant beats control

### Gate 4: No SRM (Sample Ratio Mismatch)
- Verify 50/50 split actually delivered ~50/50 traffic
- If skewed >5%, investigate instrumentation

### Gate 5: Effect size meaningful
- Lift must be ≥10% (don't ship 2% wins; not worth coordination cost)

## Test design rules

### Single-variable tests
- Default. Easy to attribute.

### Multi-variable tests
- Allowed for above-fold A/B/C variants from spark (3 variants of headline)
- Each variant must be a complete spec (not a/b/c on individual elements)

### Holdouts
- For top tests: 90/10 split
- Holdout cohort sees control for 8+ weeks even after winner declared
- Measures long-term retention impact (winner may lose at week 12)

### Sequential testing
- Allowed ONLY when test feeds next test (e.g., hero variant → bundle picker variant)
- Otherwise run parallel on independent surfaces

## Lift attribution

After test completion:
- Compute lift % vs control
- Verify gates 1-5
- Attribute to specialist (spark / ecom-cro / merch / sequence)
- Update `cro-decoded-patterns.md` with validated win
- Notify Echo + Yash via weekly CRO report

## Weekly cadence
- Monday: review prior week's results, declare winners/losers
- Tuesday: ship new variants (specialists)
- Wednesday: deploy to A/B framework
- Thursday-Sunday: monitor (Orbit dashboards)
- Friday afternoon: Decoder delta + roadmap update for next week

# Above-Fold Conversion Psychology

**Owner:** spark
**Scope:** Psychology behind above-fold copy decisions.

## The 5-second rule
Visitor decides whether to stay or bounce in 5 seconds. Above-fold copy has to:
1. Tell them what this is (recognition)
2. Tell them what they get (outcome)
3. Reassure them they're in the right place (proof)

## Cognitive load
- Headline: 1 idea
- Subhead: 1 expansion + 1 proof hint
- CTA: 1 next step
- Trust signal: 1 reassurance

If above-fold tries to convey >4 ideas, conversion drops.

## F-pattern + Z-pattern reading
- Desktop hero: F-pattern (top-left to right, then sweep down-left)
- Place headline top-left
- Place CTA below or top-right
- Place imagery on right side (visual weight)

- Mobile hero: Z-pattern is moot (single column)
- Stack: image → headline → subhead → CTA → trust signals
- Sticky CTA on long pages

## Specificity > generality
- "Save time" → 0% lift
- "Save 10 hours/week" → 8-15% lift (tested across decoder bank)
- "Better skin" → 0% lift
- "Glowing skin in 14 days" → 12-18% lift

## Outcome > feature
- Feature: "AI-powered scoring engine"
- Outcome: "Find your best candidates in seconds"
- Outcomes consistently outperform features 20-40% on first-touch

## Risk reversal
Place close to CTA:
- "30-day returns, no questions"
- "Free shipping over $50"
- "Cancel anytime"
- "No credit card required" (for SaaS — not ecom)

## Social proof types (descending efficacy)
1. Specific user testimonial w/ photo + name + outcome
2. Specific metric ("Used by 200,000+")
3. Logos of recognizable customers
4. Press mentions
5. Star rating + review count
6. Generic "Loved by thousands" (low value, used as default)

For first-time-visitor heroes: type 2 or 5 work best. Type 1 testimonials work better below fold.

## Skepticism in skeptical niches
- Supplements / health / wellness: trust signals dominate
- Place 3rd-party testing badge above CTA
- "Doctor formulated" or specific certifications
- Founder photo if founder is credentialed

## Above-fold trust trio (decoder-validated pattern)
Below CTA:
- Reviews stars + count
- Free shipping threshold
- 30-day returns

Drives 8-15% visitor→cart lift in apparel/beauty/CPG.

## Anti-patterns
- Hero video that auto-plays sound (instant bounce)
- Carousel hero with multiple slides (CTR drops on slides 2+; pick one)
- Long headline (>8 words eye-skips)
- Generic CTA ("Learn more")
- No specific number anywhere
- Trust signal placement below fold (too late)

## Niche intensity matrix
| Niche | Above-fold density | Notes |
|-------|--------------------|------|
| Apparel | High | Visual + headline + trust |
| Beauty | High | Visual-led, shade-finder prime |
| Supplements | Medium | Trust dominates over visual |
| Tech | Low | Spec-table + outcome, minimal visual |
| Home | Medium-High | Lifestyle photography + outcome |
| Subscription | Medium | Convenience-led, friction-removal |

# Cart + Checkout Mechanics

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Below-fold cart + checkout mechanic specs.

## Cart drawer mechanics

### Trigger
- Auto-open on add-to-cart (default)
- Manual click on cart icon (always available)
- Never auto-open during active typing in another field

### State machine
- closed → opening (animation) → open → closing → closed
- During opening: backdrop fades in 200ms
- Open state: drawer slides in 320ms ease-out

### Components inside drawer
1. Header: "Your Cart (N items)" + close X
2. Free-shipping progress bar (if applicable)
3. Line items (scrollable)
4. Promo code field (collapsed by default)
5. Subtotal + tax + shipping breakdown
6. Express checkout buttons (above primary CTA on mobile)
7. Primary checkout CTA (sticky bottom mobile)
8. Trust badges row

### Line item interactions
- Quantity stepper: +/- buttons, debounced 200ms
- Remove: optimistic UI (immediate disappear), undo toast 5s
- Save-for-later (if logged in)
- Variant edit: opens bottom sheet

### Free-shipping progress bar
- Threshold: typically $50-80 (decoder-validated per niche)
- Progress %: (cart_subtotal / threshold) × 100
- Visual: filled bar with current % + remaining $X
- On completion: brief confetti + "Free shipping unlocked!" pulse
- Copy slot: merch fills "$X away from free shipping" / "Free shipping unlocked"

### Upsell row
- Show 1-3 recommended products
- Eligibility: not-already-in-cart, in-stock, related-by-tag
- Click → add without dismissing drawer
- Position: above subtotal (decoder pattern: 12% AOV lift)

## Checkout flow

### Step count
- Single-page checkout (default — best for mobile)
- Multi-step only for high-AOV / complex flows (e.g., custom configurations)

### Step order (single-page)
1. Email + contact (with returning-customer detection)
2. Shipping address (with autocomplete)
3. Shipping method
4. Payment (Shop Pay default + cards + BNPL)
5. Review

### Express checkout
- Position: above the form on mobile, above email on desktop
- Order: Shop Pay > Apple Pay > Google Pay > PayPal
- Mobile: 15-25% checkout abandonment reduction

### Address autocomplete
- Google Places API or Shopify-native
- Type 3 chars → suggestions appear
- Tap suggestion → auto-fills street, city, state, zip

### Field optimization
- Combine first + last name (single field) on mobile
- Postal code → numeric keyboard
- Phone → tel keyboard
- Card number → numeric + auto-detect type

### Order bump
- Pre-purchase one-click add (above payment)
- Single eligible product (high-margin, complementary)
- Click → add to cart, no re-confirm

### Returning customer
- Detect via email
- Pre-fill shipping address
- Show "Welcome back, {{firstName}}" microcopy slot

## Post-purchase upsell

### One-click eligibility
- Same payment method on file
- 30-min eligibility window
- Single eligible product
- Click → charge, no checkout re-flow

### Decline UX
- "No thanks" button → continue to thank-you
- Don't repeat upsell on next visit
- Track decline reason if survey opt-in

## Edge cases
- Sold-out item in cart: dim + "remove only" action
- Max-quantity hit: stepper disabled + tooltip slot for merch
- Subscription item: frequency display + "edit subscription" link slot
- Bundle ineligibility: hide upsell row, fall back to recommendations
- Shipping unavailable: error state with redirect to supported countries

## Coordination
- Elio: receives state machine + interaction map → produces visual spec
- Merch: receives copy slot list → fills text content
- Sequence: receives abandon trigger conditions

# Upsell + Bundle Patterns

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Upsell, bundle, and order-bump mechanics.

## Bundle types

### Fixed bundle
- Pre-defined product set at discounted price
- Example: "Starter Kit (3 items, save 15%)"
- Pricing logic: bundle_price = sum(item_prices) × (1 - discount)
- UX: single PDP for the bundle, all items fixed

### Build-your-own bundle
- Customer picks N items from M-eligible pool, fixed total
- Example: "Build your 5-pack — any 5 sodas, $30"
- Pricing logic: total fixed; items unconstrained within pool
- UX: bundle picker on PDP or dedicated bundle page

### Tiered bundle
- Discount escalates with quantity
- "Buy 2, save 10%; buy 3+, save 15%; buy 5+, save 20%"
- Pricing logic: count_in_cart determines discount
- UX: progress display on PDP + cart

### Mix-and-match
- "Any 3 from collection X, save 15%"
- Pricing logic: tag-based eligibility, discount applied at cart level
- UX: callout on collection page + cart-level confirmation

## Order bump (pre-purchase)

### Position
- Above payment step in checkout (single-page)
- Above order review (multi-step)

### Eligibility logic
- Single product
- High-margin (don't bump cheap items)
- Complementary to cart (e.g., socks with shoes; not duplicate)
- In stock
- Not already in cart

### UX
- Single-click add (no re-confirm)
- Optimistic UI (line item appears immediately)
- "Added!" micro-confirmation
- Decline = ignore (no required interaction)

### Conversion math
- Typical bump conversion: 15-30% of viewers
- AOV lift: 5-10% across orders that see bump

## Post-purchase upsell

### Page placement
- After payment confirmation, before final thank-you
- One full page or modal

### One-click eligibility
- Same payment method on file
- 30-min eligibility window (Shopify limit; pattern varies by platform)
- Single product (don't show multiple — choice paralysis)
- Higher-AOV product than cart (upsell ladder)

### Decline UX
- "No thanks, take me to my order" → thank-you page
- Don't show same upsell on repeat visits

### Conversion math
- Typical post-purchase upsell conversion: 10-25%
- AOV lift: 8-15%

## Cart upsell row

### Position
- Inside cart drawer/page, between line items and subtotal
- Single row, 1-3 product recommendations

### Eligibility
- Not in cart
- Related-by-tag or "frequently bought together"
- In stock

### UX
- Compact card (image + title + price + "+" button)
- Click "+" → add to cart, no dismiss
- Updates free-shipping progress + subtotal in real-time

### Conversion math
- 8-15% of cart sessions add upsell row
- AOV lift: 4-8%

## Subscription upsell

### PDP toggle
- "One-time" vs "Subscribe & save 20%"
- Default: one-time (less commitment)
- Default-subscribe variant: 25-40% subscription rate lift, but only if churn-prevention strong

### Frequency picker
- 1mo / 2mo / 3mo / 6mo (per niche)
- Default: most popular for niche (decoder-validated)

### Skip / pause / cancel
- All self-serve (no email-required)
- Pause offer at cancel UX (Athletic Greens pattern: "skip a month" beats cancel 35% of attempts)

## Bundle math display
- Always show savings: "Bundle: $90 (save $15 vs. individual)"
- Use strikethrough for "individual price"
- Pre-calculate; never make the customer do math

## Anti-patterns
- Don't upsell items already in cart
- Don't bundle low-margin (kills profit per order)
- Don't show >3 cart-row upsells (decision fatigue)
- Don't auto-add bumps (ethics + chargebacks)
- Don't hide bundle savings — always display

## Decoder-validated patterns
- Athletic Greens: subscription default + pause-vs-cancel
- Magic Spoon: build-your-own 4-pack
- Liquid IV: tiered bundle (10/20/30 stick packs)
- Bombas: 4-pack discount on socks (commodity bundle)
- Olipop: variety pack as PDP

# Subscription Mechanics

**Owner:** ecom-cro
**Scope:** Subscription UX from PDP toggle through churn-prevention.

## PDP subscription toggle

### Default state
- One-time (default) — lower commitment, broader funnel
- Subscribe-default — only if niche has high churn-prevention or cart-friction is the bottleneck

### Display
- Two-option toggle: "One-time" / "Subscribe & save N%"
- Discount % visible in toggle (15-25% typical)
- Frequency picker appears when "Subscribe" selected
- Microcopy slot for merch: "Skip or cancel anytime"

### Frequency options
- Per-niche default:
  - Supplements: 1mo (most), 2mo, 3mo
  - CPG / food: 2 weeks, 1mo
  - Personal care: 1mo, 2mo, 3mo
  - Pet food: 2 weeks, 1mo (large bag)
- Default to most-popular frequency

## Subscription onboarding

### Welcome flow
- Email 1 (sequence): welcome + first-shipment ETA + skip/swap reminder
- In-app: first-shipment tracker, edit-subscription link
- Educational content: how to skip, how to swap, how to cancel

### First-shipment delight
- Branded packaging (Vega owns; sequence references)
- Insert card with "manage your subscription" QR
- First-month freebie or upgrade (decoder pattern: 8-12% retention lift)

## Mid-cycle engagement

### Pre-shipment notification
- 3 days before shipment: "Your next shipment is on its way"
- CTA: "Skip / swap / pause" (single-tap from email or in-app)

### Auto-pause-on-skip
- If customer skips 1+ time, offer pause: "Pause for 30/60/90 days?"
- Reduce churn vs full cancellation

## Cancellation UX (churn-prevention)

### Multi-step cancellation flow
1. "Why are you canceling?" → reason picker
2. Based on reason, offer save:
   - "Too much product" → reduce frequency
   - "Don't need right now" → pause (Athletic Greens pattern)
   - "Too expensive" → discount on next month
   - "Not the right fit" → swap to similar product
3. If still canceling: confirm with reduced-frequency offer
4. Final confirm: "Cancel subscription"

### Decoder-validated saves
- Athletic Greens: pause beats cancel 35% of attempts
- Hims: discount on next month beats cancel 20%
- Curology: swap-to-similar saves 15%

### Win-back trigger
- After cancellation: trigger win-back sequence (sequence owns)
- Day 30: "We miss you" + 20% off
- Day 60: "Last call — 25% off"
- Day 90: stop, respect unsubscribe

## Subscription account portal

### Required actions (self-serve)
- Skip next shipment
- Reschedule next shipment
- Swap product
- Change frequency
- Update payment method
- Update shipping address
- Pause (1/2/3 month)
- Cancel (with save flow)

### Anti-patterns
- Email-required to cancel — illegal in CA + EU per consumer law
- Hidden cancel link — same legal issue
- Unable to skip — drives cancellation instead

## Subscription analytics (Orbit owns; ecom-cro consumes)
- Active subscribers
- Churn rate (monthly + annualized)
- Average subscription lifetime (months)
- Skip rate per cycle
- Pause vs cancel ratio
- Win-back rate

# PDP Body Structure

**Owner:** merch
**Scope:** Mandatory PDP body order + writing patterns.

## Mandatory order
1. Benefits-first paragraphs (2-3, ≤60 words each)
2. Benefit bullets (3-5)
3. Objection-handling section (3-5 objections)
4. Spec table

**NEVER lead with feature list.** This is the #1 anti-pattern.

## Section 1: Benefits paragraphs

### Pattern
- 2-3 short paragraphs
- Outcome-focused

# Objection Handling Frameworks

**Owner:** merch
**Scope:** Niche-typical objection patterns + frameworks for addressing.

## Universal framework
1. Acknowledge the concern (don't dismiss)
2. Provide the specific reassurance (number, policy, mechanism)
3. Risk reversal (return policy, guarantee, free trial)

## Per-niche objection libraries

### Apparel
| Objection | Answer pattern |
|-----------|----------------|
| Will it fit? | Size guide + true-to-size note + free returns |
| Will it shrink? | Care instructions + "no shrinkage" claim if true |
| Will it itch / scratch? | Material spec (micron count) + comfort guarantee |
| What if I don't like the color? | Free returns within 30 days |
| Returns process? | "Return free within 30 days, instant refund" |

### Beauty
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Will it work for my skin type? | "Tested for [types]" + ingredient list |
| Allergic reactions? | Allergen-free claim + patch-test recommendation |
| Cruelty-free? | Certification (Leaping Bunny etc.) |
| Returns on opened products? | Policy ("opened, full refund within X days") |
| Right shade for me? | Shade-finder quiz / free shade match |

### Supplements
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Is it safe? | Third-party testing + manufacturer info |
| Drug interactions? | "Consult doctor if on medications" |
| How fast does it work? | "Most users notice [effect] in [timeframe]" |
| Money-back guarantee? | "30-day full refund, no questions" |
| Subscription cancellation? | "Cancel anytime in your account, no fees" |

### CPG (food/drink)
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Taste? | "Loved by N% of reviewers" + flavor profile |
| Allergens? | Full allergen list |
| Shelf life? | Months/years + freshness guarantee |
| Storage? | Room temp / refrigerated |

### Tech / connected
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Setup difficulty? | "Set up in N minutes" + step count |
| Compatibility? | Device list + compatibility checker |
| Data privacy? | Privacy policy + on-device claim if applicable |
| Warranty? | Length + claim process |
| Returns? | 30/60/100-day policy |

### Pet
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Picky pet? | "Money-back if pet refuses" |
| Right plan size? | Custom-plan calculator |
| Allergies? | Ingredient list + allergen-free options |
| Vet-recommended? | Vet endorsements + qualifications |

### Subscription / personal care
| Objection | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Commitment fear? | "Cancel anytime, no fees" |
| Right plan for me? | Quiz / consultation |
| Auto-renew? | "Reminder before renewal, easy skip" |
| Returns on unopened? | Policy |

## Risk reversal staples
- 30-day money-back guarantee
- Free shipping over $X
- Free returns
- Cancel anytime
- "If you don't love it, ship it back"
- First month free / risk-free trial

## Placement
- Top 3 objections inline in PDP body (per pdp-body-structure.md)
- Remaining objections in FAQ section
- Critical ones (returns, allergies) repeated in cart + checkout reassurance copy

## Voice
- Confident, not defensive
- Specific numbers (30 days, not "soon")
- Plain language
- Quill voice scorecard 8/9

## Anti-patterns
- "We're confident you'll love it" — generic
- "Most customers are happy" — vague
- "Email us if there's an issue" — high-friction
- Hiding cancellation behind email-required process — illegal in CA/EU

# Cart + Checkout Microcopy

**Owner:** merch
**Scope:** Microcopy that fills ecom-cro's mechanic slots.

## Cart drawer microcopy

### Header
- "Your Cart (N items)"
- "Cart" + count badge
- Close button: "✕" or "Close"

### Free-shipping bar
| State | Copy |
|-------|------|
| Below threshold | "$X away from free shipping" |
| Met threshold | "Free shipping unlocked!" |
| Over threshold (default state) | "Free shipping included" |

### Line item
- Quantity stepper labels: "−" "+"
- Remove: "Remove" or trash icon w/ "Remove" tooltip
- Variant detail: "Color: Navy / Size: M"
- Save for later: "Save for later"

### Upsell row
- Header: "Frequently bought together" / "You may also like"
- Add button: "Add" or "+"

### Subtotal block
- "Subtotal: $X"
- "Shipping: calculated at checkout"
- "Tax: calculated at checkout"
- Promo code field: "Have a promo code?" → expand input

### Express checkout buttons
- Native labels (Shop Pay / Apple Pay / PayPal — don't customize per platform rules)

### Primary CTA
- "Checkout" (default)
- "Secure Checkout" (trust-prime)
- "Continue to Payment" (multi-step)

### Trust badges row
- "Secure Checkout"
- "30-Day Returns"
- "Free Shipping over $50"

## Checkout microcopy

### Email step
- Label: "Email"
- Placeholder: "you@email.com"
- Returning-customer banner: "Welcome back, {{firstName}}! [Login for faster checkout]"
- Marketing opt-in: "Email me about new products and sales" (un-checked default — GDPR)

### Address autocomplete
- "Start typing your address..."
- Suggestion list label: "Suggestions"

### Shipping method
- Per-method label: "Standard (5-7 business days) — Free"
- "Express (2-3 days) — $9"
- "Overnight — $25"

### Payment
- "Payment information"
- Trust microcopy: "Encrypted and secure"

### Order summary
- "Order Summary"
- Line items same as cart
- "Subtotal" / "Shipping" / "Tax" / "Total"

### Confirm CTA
- "Place Order" (clear, commitment)
- "Pay $X" (price-anchored)
- "Complete Purchase"

### Errors
- Card declined: "Card was declined. Try a different card or contact your bank."
- Address invalid: "We couldn't verify this address. Double-check zip code."
- Out of stock during checkout: "Sorry, [product] just sold out. We've removed it from your cart."

## Post-purchase microcopy

### Confirmation page header
- "Order confirmed!" / "Thanks, {{firstName}}!" / "You're all set."

### Order details
- "Order #12345"
- "We'll send a tracking number to {{email}} once it ships."

### Subscription opt-in (if applicable)
- "Want to save 20% by subscribing? [Switch to Subscribe & Save]"

### Referral CTA
- "Love it? Share $10 off — get $10 back. [Get your link]"

### Account creation prompt
- "Create an account to track your order"
- "Save your info for next time — takes 30 seconds"

### Recommended next products
- "You might also like"
- "Top picks for you"

## Microcopy character limits
- Cart drawer header: ≤30 chars
- Free-shipping bar: ≤50 chars
- Trust badge label: ≤20 chars
- Primary CTA: ≤25 chars
- Error message: ≤80 chars
- Confirmation header: ≤40 chars

## Voice
- All microcopy passes quill voice scorecard 8/9
- No banned words
- Specific over generic ("$12 away" not "almost there")
- Active voice
- Confident, not apologetic

## Anti-patterns
- "Oops, something went wrong" — generic, no info
- "Please try again" — passive, no action
- "Add some products to your cart" — empty state should be more specific
- Apologetic tone for normal flows ("Sorry to bother you...")
- ALL CAPS labels (accessibility issue)

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - CTA: "Get yours"

- Subject: "Getting the most out of your [product]"

- CTA: none (or "Watch the guide")

- Subject: "How are you liking [product]?"
- Goal: review request
- Content: simple review form + photo upload
- CTA: "Leave a review (takes 60s)"

- Subject: "Time for a refill?"
- Goal: replenishment / cross-sell
- Content: replenishment reminder + complementary product
- CTA: "Reorder"

### Email 5 — Day 60
- Subject: "Share $10, get $10"
- Goal: referral activation
- Content: referral program + share link
- CTA: "Get your link"

### Email 1 — Day 60 of inactivity
- Subject: "We miss you, {{firstName}}"
- Goal: soft re-engagement
- Content: brand update + new arrivals
- CTA: "See what's new"

### Email 2 — Day 90
- Subject: "Here's 20% off — come back"
- Goal: incentive
- Content: discount code + top products
- CTA: "Take 20% off"

### Email 3 — Day 120
- Subject: "Last call: 25% off"
- Goal: final attempt
- Content: 25% code + 7-day expiration + unsubscribe respect
- CTA: "Use 25% off"

## Subscription nurture

### Pre-renewal (3 days before next shipment)
- Subject: "Your shipment ships in 3 days"
- Content: shipment preview + skip/swap link
- CTA: "Manage subscription"

### Post-renewal
- Subject: "On its way!"
- Content: tracking + content engagement
- CTA: "Track shipment"

### Mid-cycle engagement (between shipments)
- Subject: "Tips for getting the most from your subscription"
- Content: educational + community

### Churn-prevention (cancel-flow trigger)
- Subject: "Before you cancel — could we offer a pause?"
- Content: pause options + frequency reduction
- CTA: "Pause instead"

### Win-back from cancel
- Subject: "30 days off, on us"
- Content: re-activation incentive
- CTA: "Re-subscribe"

## Voice
- All emails pass quill scorecard
- Subject lines ≤50 chars
- Single primary CTA per email
- Plain-text version included

# Cart Abandon Recovery Playbook

**Owner:** sequence
**Scope:** Recovery sequence specifics for cart abandon.

## Trigger conditions (set by ecom-cro, fired by sequence)
- Cart dismissed (drawer closed without checkout)
- 60 minutes elapsed
- Cart value > $30 (don't waste effort on low-value carts)
- Customer email captured (signed up or began checkout)
- Not purchased since trigger
- No prior abandon email in last 7 days

## 3-email cadence

### Email 1 — 1 hour
**Goal:** soft reminder, preserve margin
**No incentive.** Just a reminder.

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| From | "{{brand}}" or "{{brandFounder}}" |
| Subject variants | "Forget something?" / "Your cart's still warm" / "Pick up where you left off" |
| Preview text | "Your cart's saved. Check out before stock changes." |
| Hero | Cart preview (item images + names) |
| Body | Soft reminder. No discount. |
| CTA | "Resume checkout" |
| Footer | Unsubscribe + brand info |

### Email 2 — 24 hours
**Goal:** incentive trigger (conditional)
**Discount IF cart value > $40, else free shipping IF cart > $80, else no discount.**

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Subject variants | "10% off — for the next 24h" / "{{firstName}}, here's a nudge" / "Save on what you almost bought" |
| Preview text | "10% off your cart. Code expires in 24h." |
| Hero | Discount banner + cart preview |
| Body | Discount code + 24h countdown + cart contents |
| CTA | "Apply discount + checkout" |

### Email 3 — 72 hours
**Goal:** final attempt
**Higher discount, alternatives shown, soft urgency.**

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| Subject variants | "Last call: 15% off" / "Final reminder" / "Don't miss out" |
| Preview text | "15% off — final reminder." |
| Hero | 15% discount banner |
| Body | 15% code + cart preview + top 3 alternatives + "we'll release stock back" soft urgency |
| CTA | "Take 15% off" |

## Recovery rate targets
- Email 1: 2-4% recovery
- Email 2: 4-8% recovery
- Email 3: 1-3% recovery
- **Total sequence: 8-15% recovered carts**
- Top decoder benchmarks: 15-22%

## Discount escalation rules
- Never start with discount on email 1 (preserves margin + brand)
- Email 2: 10% if cart > $40, free ship if cart > $80, none if < $40
- Email 3: 15%, time-bound
- Don't go above 20% on cart-abandon (becomes habit-forming)

## Personalization
- {{firstName}} in subject (small lift)
- {{cartItems}} as preview content
- {{cartTotal}} for context
- Don't over-personalize (creepy zone)

## Send-time optimization
- Email 1: send any time (1h after trigger)
- Email 2: send Tue-Thu 10am local (best open rates)
- Email 3: send during business hours

## Decoder-validated patterns
- Bombas: 1h reminder no discount, 24h 15% off, 72h 20% off — recovers ~12% carts
- Chubbies: humorous voice, single email at 1h with $5 off — ~8% recovery
- Allbirds: 1h reminder, 24h "you have great taste" + free returns reminder — ~10% recovery

## Cross-sequence interaction
- If user added to cart again before sequence completes: pause sequence, restart trigger
- If user purchased: terminate sequence
- If unsubscribed: terminate
- If 7-day window elapsed without conversion: end sequence (don't re-trigger for 30d)

## Coordination
- Trigger logic: ecom-cro
- Email content: sequence
- Voice ratification: quill
- Brand kit: vega
- Email infra: postmark (when hired)

# Subscription Nurture Patterns

**Owner:** sequence
**Scope:** Email sequences across subscription lifecycle.

## Subscription lifecycle stages

1. **Pre-renewal** — 3 days before next shipment
2. **Renewal** — shipment processed
3. **Post-shipment** — tracking + delight
4. **Mid-cycle** — between shipments, educational
5. **Cancel intent** — churn-prevention trigger
6. **Win-back** — post-cancellation

## Pre-renewal email (3 days before shipment)

### Goal
Notify + give skip/swap option (reduces churn 12-18%).

### Content
- Subject: "Your next shipment ships in 3 days"
- Hero: shipment preview (product + variant + frequency)
- Body: "We'll charge {{paymentMethod}} on {{date}}. Need to skip or swap? Update by {{cutoffDate}}."
- CTAs:
  - Primary: "Manage subscription"
  - Secondary inline links: "Skip this shipment" / "Swap product" / "Pause"

### Anti-pattern
- Don't bury skip/swap in account portal links — surface them in the email itself

## Post-renewal / shipped email

### Goal
Confirm + tracking + delight.

### Content
- Subject: "On its way! 📦"
- Body: tracking number + ETA
- Cross-sell: complementary products (without being pushy)
- CTA: "Track shipment"

## Mid-cycle engagement

### Goal
Keep brand top-of-mind between shipments. Reduce surprise-charge cancels.

### Cadence
- Subscription frequency = monthly: 1 mid-cycle email
- Frequency = bimonthly: 1-2 mid-cycle
- Frequency = quarterly: 2-3 mid-cycle

### Content patterns
- Educational: "5 ways to get more from your [product]"
- Community: "How customers are using [product]"
- Behind-the-scenes: brand story / new product preview
- User-generated content / reviews

### CTA
- Soft: "See more tips" / "Browse community posts"
- Avoid: aggressive cross-sell

## Churn-prevention sequence (cancel-intent trigger)

### Trigger
User clicks "Cancel" button in account portal.

### In-flow vs email
This typically happens in-app, but follow-up email reinforces the save offer.

### Email 1 (immediate post-cancel-attempt, if save offer accepted)
- Subject: "You're paused, not gone"
- Body: confirm pause duration + when subscription resumes + "any time, easy to update"

### Email 2 (immediate post-cancel-confirm, if save not accepted)
- Subject: "We're sorry to see you go"
- Body: "We've cancelled. Final shipment {{date}}. Re-subscribe anytime."
- Soft win-back hint: "If you change your mind, here's 20% off your first month back."

### Save-offer emails (sent if user clicks save)
- "Your subscription is paused for 30 days"
- "Frequency reduced to every 2 months"

## Win-back from cancel

### Trigger
30, 60, 90 days post-cancellation.

### Email 1 — Day 30
- Subject: "30 days off, on us"
- Body: re-activation incentive + soft "we updated [product]"
- CTA: "Re-subscribe"

### Email 2 — Day 60
- Subject: "Here's 20% off — come back"
- Body: discount + new arrivals
- CTA: "Use 20% off"

### Email 3 — Day 90
- Subject: "Last call"
- Body: 25% off + 7-day expiration
- CTA: "Use 25% off"

After 90: stop. Respect unsubscribe. Don't drift into re-engagement-spam zone.

## Subscription-specific copy notes

### Pause vs cancel framing
- Always offer pause as default save option
- Athletic Greens pattern: "Skip a month" before "Cancel"
- 35% of cancel-attempts convert to pause

### Frequency reduction
- "Most subscribers find every-2-months works better"
- Lower-frequency = lower-churn (counterintuitive)

### Discount-on-renewal
- Avoid — trains customers to threaten cancel for discounts
- Only deploy strategically (e.g., year-end retention push)

## Targets
- Pre-renewal email open: 45%+
- Mid-cycle open: 25%+
- Win-back recovery: 5-12%
- Cancel→pause rate: 30%+

## Coordination
- Trigger logic: ecom-cro
- Email content: sequence
- Subscription portal UX: ecom-cro
- Voice: quill

# Niche Audit Protocol

**Owner:** decoder
**Scope:** On-demand competitive audit when catalyst / elio / spark / merch needs niche-specific intel for a project.

## Trigger
- Request from catalyst (CRO strategy phase)
- Request from elio (about to design new ecom surface in unfamiliar niche)
- Request from spark / merch (need copy formula intel for niche)

## Workflow

### Step 1 — Niche brief
Receive from requester:
- Niche name
- Specific surface focus (PDP / cart / hero / etc.) OR "general"
- Project context (which Boldteq client / build)
- Deadline

### Step 2 — Identify top 10
- WebSearch: "top DTC brands [niche]" + "[niche] direct-to-consumer leaders"
- Cross-reference SimilarWeb traffic rankings
- Cross-reference decoder priors (don't re-teardown brands already in library)
- Confirm 10 brand list before audit

### Step 3 — Abbreviated teardown per brand (60 min each)
- Capture only requested dimensions (or all 8 if "general")
- Mobile + desktop both
- 10 brands × 60 min = ~10 hours total

### Step 4 — Synthesize cross-brand patterns
- File: `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/niche-audits/[niche]-[YYYY-MM-DD].md`
- Structure:
  1. Niche overview (3-paragraph summary)
  2. Dominant patterns (observed in 5+ brands)
  3. Divergent patterns (observed in 2-4 brands — risky to assume)
  4. White-space opportunities (no brand doing X — Boldteq client could)
  5. Per-dimension table: hero / PDP / cart / checkout / post-purchase / mobile / motion / copy
  6. Top-3 niche-specific insights for the requester
  7. Brand-evidence index

### Step 5 — Hand off
- Notify requester via Polyglot delegation event
- Cross-link from `cro-decoded-patterns.md` if patterns hit 3-brand threshold

## Niche-specific dimensions

### Apparel
- Fit-finder UX
- Size guide structure
- Returns policy prominence
- Material specs depth

### Beauty
- Shade-finder / ingredient-finder
- Trust signals (cruelty-free / dermat-tested)
- UGC integration

### Supplements
- Third-party testing badges
- Doctor / clinical proof
- Subscription default rate
- Allergen/interaction warnings

### CPG (food/drink)
- Flavor / variety pack patterns
- Allergen disclosure
- Subscription-vs-one-time default

### Tech / connected
- Spec table positioning
- Compatibility checker
- Data privacy callouts
- Setup-time claims

### Home
- Lifestyle photography density
- Configurator UX
- Bulky-item shipping copy

### Pet
- Plan calculator
- Vet endorsements
- Picky-pet guarantee

### Subscription / personal care
- Cancel friction (or absence)
- Pause/skip prominence
- Onboarding quiz

## Time budget
- Standard niche audit: 8-12 hours total
- Express audit (5 brands, 3 dimensions): 4-6 hours

# Pattern Extraction Rubric

**Owner:** decoder
**Scope:** What qualifies as a "pattern" worth recording — and when to promote from teardown library to validated playbook.

## Pattern qualification criteria

A teardown observation qualifies as a pattern if:
1. **Recurring** — observed in ≥1 brand currently, with clear repeatability potential
2. **Specific** — concrete enough to copy (visual + behavior + copy formula)
3. **Causal hypothesis** — plausible reason it converts (psychology / friction reduction / trust)
4. **Measurable** — could be A/B tested

If it fails any of these, it's an observation, not a pattern. Note in teardown but don't tag as pattern.

## Pattern naming convention
- Format: `[surface]-[mechanic]-[descriptor]`
- Examples: `pdp-trust-trio`, `cart-free-shipping-bar`, `checkout-express-first-mobile`, `subscription-pause-vs-cancel-save`

## Promotion thresholds (teardown → cro-decoded-patterns.md)

| Pattern occurrences | Status | Action |
|---------------------|--------|--------|
| 1 brand | Single observation | Note in teardown only |
| 2 brands | Possible pattern | Tag `provisional` in teardown |
| 3 brands | Validated pattern | PROMOTE to `cro-decoded-patterns.md` |
| 5+ brands | Strong pattern | Bump confidence score in playbook |
| 8+ brands + tested | Canonical | Top recommendation tier |

## Pattern entry format (in `cro-decoded-patterns.md`)

```markdown
### [pattern-id]: [short name]

**Surface:** [pdp / cart / checkout / post-purchase / subscription / email]
**Confidence:** [provisional / validated / strong / canonical]
**Brand evidence:** [brand1, brand2, brand3, ...]
**Niches observed:** [apparel, beauty, ...]

**WHEN to use:** [conditions where this pattern fits]
**WHY it converts:** [psychology / friction / trust hypothesis]
**STRUCTURE:** [layout / component tree / interaction]
**SPEC:** [exact dimensions / states / responsive notes]
**COPY FORMULA:** [if pattern includes copy]
**EXAMPLES:** [3+ brand-cited concrete examples]
**ANTI-PATTERN:** [what looks similar but breaks]
**TYPICAL LIFT:** [from decoder bank / validated tests]
**REFERENCES:** [teardown entries cited]
```

## Demotion criteria (validated → invalidated)

If catalyst-confirmed test result invalidates a pattern:
- 1 invalidating test in same niche → bump confidence DOWN one tier
- 2 invalidating tests → demote to `~/.claude/memory/patterns/avoid/invalidated-cro-patterns.md`
- Move to avoid library with `INVALIDATED YYYY-MM-DD` timestamp + test_id

## Avoid bias
- Don't pattern-extract from articles or "best practices" lists
- Patterns must come from live brand observation
- Re-verify any teardown >12 months old before citing

## Quality gates per teardown
- Mira scorecard: ≥3 patterns extracted (otherwise re-run teardown)
- Cross-reference check: did this pattern hit 3-brand threshold this run?
- Diversity check: not all observations from same brand (single-brand teardown can't promote anything)

# Ecom PDP Design Protocol

**Owner:** elio
**Scope:** End-to-end PDP design protocol for Stack B/C ecom builds.

## Pre-design gate
- ≥3 decoder teardowns in matching niche must exist (else dispatch decoder for niche audit)
- Project `design-vision.md` + brand-kit reviewed
- Token system bootstrapped by token (no hex in spec)

## Design surface zones (top to bottom)

### Zone 1 — Hero block (above fold)
- Image gallery (left desktop, full-width mobile)
- Variant selector (color swatches / size buttons / bundle picker)
- Price block (regular / compare-at strikethrough / subscription discount toggle)
- Stock indicator (in-stock / low-stock / sold-out)
- Primary CTA — Add to Cart (sticky on mobile when scrolled past)
- Trust trio (reviews stars + count, free-shipping promise, returns policy)
- Subscription toggle if applicable

### Zone 2 — Reviews module
- Star average + total count + breakdown
- Filter (all / 5-star / 4-star / 3-star / lower)
- Sort (most recent / most helpful / most critical)
- Verified-purchase badge
- Photo / video reviews UGC

### Zone 3 — Body content (merch-owned)
- Benefits paragraphs (2-3, ≤60 words each)
- Benefit bullets (3-5, outcome-bolded)
- Objection-handling (3-5 Q+A)
- Spec table

### Zone 4 — UGC gallery
- Instagram / TikTok integration
- 6-12 images grid

### Zone 5 — FAQ (merch-owned, accordion)

### Zone 6 — Cross-sell rail
- "You may also like" / "Frequently bought together"
- 4-8 product cards

## Mobile-first specs (mandatory)
- Sticky ATC bar with offset for cart drawer
- Image gallery: swipe gesture + dot indicators
- Variant selector: tap-to-expand bottom sheet
- Touch targets ≥48px
- Reviews: collapsed-by-default per accordion

## Performance budgets
- LCP ≤2.5s (hero image priority hint, dimensions reserved, AVIF/WebP, CDN)
- CLS ≤0.1 (image dimensions reserved, ATC button reserved, sticky elements have placeholders)
- Total bundle ≤200KB JS for PDP route

## Accessibility
- All interactive elements keyboard-navigable
- Variant selector has visible focus + ARIA states
- Image gallery has alt text + lightbox keyboard nav
- Reviews have proper heading hierarchy
- WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on all token combinations

## Slot map for handoff

### Copy slots → spark
- Hero CTA copy variants (3)
- Subscription toggle CTA
- Variant trigger CTAs

### Copy slots → merch
- Body paragraphs / bullets / objection-handling / spec table
- Reviews module labels
- FAQ copy
- Trust microcopy below CTA
- Cross-sell rail header

### Mechanic slots → ecom-cro
- Variant selector logic (in-stock / out-of-stock / availability)
- ATC drawer trigger
- Subscription toggle logic + frequency picker
- Stock-indicator threshold logic
- Cross-sell eligibility query

### Component slots → figma-synth
- ProductCard (cross-sell)
- VariantSelector
- AddToCartCTA
- PriceBlock
- ReviewStars
- TrustBadge
- SubscriptionToggle

### Token requests → token
- Brand-aware accent for sale badge
- Subscription-CTA distinct from primary CTA color
- Trust-trio icon stroke

## Output deliverable
- `project/design/specs/pdp.md` — full spec including all zones + slot map
- Hand off JSON to vega for ratification
- Once vega approves: hand to spark (copy), merch (copy), ecom-cro (mechanics), figma-synth (Code Connect), token (any new tokens), pod-frontend (implementation)

# Cart + Checkout Design Protocol

**Owner:** elio
**Scope:** Cart drawer + checkout flow design for Stack B/C ecom.

## Cart drawer design

### Default choice
- Drawer (overlay slide-in) > full cart page

# Ecom Motion + Interaction Protocol

**Owner:** elio
**Scope:** Micro-interactions + motion patterns for ecom storefronts.

## Universal rules
- All durations from token system (`--duration-instant` 100ms / `--duration-fast` 200ms / `--duration-base` 300ms / `--duration-slow` 500ms)
- All easings from token (`--easing-out` for entrances, `--easing-in-out` for transitions, `--easing-spring` for delightful)
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: replace transitions with instant state changes; keep critical feedback (loading, errors)
- Mobile-first: all interactions tested on touch device

## PDP motion patterns

### Variant swatch tap response
- Hover (desktop): 200ms scale-up 1.05 + shadow
- Active tap: 100ms scale-down 0.95
- Selected state: persistent ring 2px + checkmark badge
- Disabled (out of stock): 50% opacity + diagonal strikethrough overlay

### Image zoom
- Desktop hover: cursor-zoom + 1.5-2x zoom in tile, follow cursor
- Mobile pinch: native pinch-zoom up to 3x
- Tap (mobile): open lightbox, swipe between images

### Image gallery swipe
- Mobile native horizontal scroll-snap with dot indicators
- Desktop thumbnails on left/below
- Selected thumb shows ring 2px

### Sticky ATC reveal (mobile)
- Trigger: scroll past in-page ATC button
- Animation: slide up from bottom 320ms ease-out
- Hide on scroll back to in-page ATC
- Reserve bottom space for sticky element via padding-bottom

### Add-to-cart click feedback
- Optimistic: button shows checkmark instantly
- Cart icon badge increments with subtle bounce
- Cart drawer auto-opens after 300ms delay
- Failure: revert checkmark, show inline error toast

## Cart drawer motion

### Open
- Backdrop fade-in 200ms
- Drawer slide-in 320ms cubic-bezier easing
- Trap focus on first interactive element

### Close
- Drawer slide-out 280ms
- Backdrop fade-out 200ms
- Return focus to triggering element

### Line item remove
- Optimistic: line item slides out 200ms + crossfade to undo toast
- Undo toast: 5-second auto-dismiss with progress bar
- Re-add on undo: line item slides back in

### Free-shipping bar progress
- Smooth fill animation 400ms ease-out when subtotal changes
- On threshold met: brief 600ms confetti or pulse on bar

## Checkout motion

### Step transitions (multi-step)
- Slide left between steps 280ms
- Per-step content fade 200ms

### Field validation
- Error state: red ring fade-in 200ms
- Success state: green check fade-in 300ms
- Inline error message: slide down 200ms

### Express checkout button shimmer
- Subtle gradient shimmer on first paint to indicate interactive

## Post-purchase motion

### Confirmation hero
- Staggered fade-in: header 100ms / order details 200ms / next-steps 300ms

### Confetti / delight (light touch)
- Reserved for first-purchase or milestone (fifth order, etc.)
- 1.5s max duration
- Skip if `prefers-reduced-motion`

## Quick-view modal
- Open: backdrop fade 200ms + modal scale-up from 0.95 to 1, 280ms ease-out
- Close: reverse
- Trap focus

## Exit-intent modal (use sparingly)
- Trigger: mouse leaves top edge (desktop) or scroll-up gesture (mobile)
- Once per session max
- Modal fade + scale-up 280ms
- Easy dismiss (X + ESC + click outside)
- Don't trigger if user already in cart or checkout

## Loading states
- Skeleton on async fetches (PDP gallery, reviews, related products)
- Spinner only for short waits (<2s)
- Token-defined timing for consistency

## Anti-patterns
- Auto-play hero video with sound
- Carousel hero with auto-advance
- Bouncing CTAs (gimmicky)
- Animated price tickers (untrustworthy)
- Long animations (>800ms) that delay interaction
- Motion without `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback

## Coordination
- ecom-cro provides state machine; elio specs the visual + motion of each transition
- Token defines timing tokens; elio references
- Pod frontend implements; figma-synth captures motion in Code Connect example

# Mobile Ecom Design Protocol

**Owner:** elio
**Scope:** Mobile-first design rules for ecom storefronts. Mobile = 60-70% of ecom traffic.

## Mobile-first mandate
- Every spec starts at 375px viewport
- Then expands to 768px (tablet) and 1280px+ (desktop)
- Never desktop-first then "responsive down"

## Touch target ≥48px
- All buttons, links, swatches, qty steppers
- Minimum spacing 8px between adjacent targets
- Auto-reject any spec with smaller targets

## Bottom-nav pattern (apparel / beauty / DTC)
- 4-5 icons: Home / Shop / Cart / Account / Search
- Sticky bottom
- 56px height + safe-area-inset-bottom
- Active state with token-defined accent

## Sticky elements priority
- Sticky ATC on PDP (highest priority)
- Sticky checkout CTA in cart drawer
- Sticky bottom-nav (if used)
- NEVER stack 3+ sticky elements (cumulative height blocks content)

## Thumb-zone CTA placement
- Primary CTAs in bottom 1/3 of screen
- Secondary actions in middle
- Header for navigation only

## Mobile cart drawer
- Full-height (100vh)
- Slide from right
- Sticky checkout CTA at bottom
- Trust badges row above CTA

## Mobile checkout
- Express checkout above form (Shop Pay / Apple Pay / Google Pay / PayPal)
- Combined first+last name field
- Numeric keyboards on postal / phone / card-number
- Address autocomplete on focus (3-char trigger)
- One-page format default (multi-step only for high-AOV configurable)

## Mobile size guide
- Modal bottom-sheet (not full-page nav-out)
- Tab structure if multiple measurement systems (US / UK / EU)
- Image diagram with measurement points
- Easy dismiss (X + swipe-down)

## Mobile filter UX (listing)
- Bottom-sheet drawer triggered by "Filter" button
- Apply button at bottom (sticky)
- Filter chips on listing for active filters (tap to remove)
- Sort separate from filter (top-right of listing)

## Mobile image gallery
- Native scroll-snap horizontal scroll
- Dot indicators below
- Pinch-zoom + tap-to-lightbox

## Mobile variant selector
- Tap-to-expand bottom sheet for size pickers
- Color swatches inline (compact size, ≥48px when 4+ swatches)
- Bundle picker as separate full-screen flow if 3+ variant axes

## Mobile reviews
- Collapsed accordion by default
- Expand to inline scroll
- Filter / sort in bottom sheet

## Mobile FAQ
- Accordion (single-expand or multi-expand per pattern)
- Collapse by default
- Smooth height transition

## Mobile performance budgets
- LCP ≤2.0s (stricter than desktop 2.5s)
- CLS ≤0.05
- Total page weight ≤500KB on PDP
- Image optimization: AVIF + WebP + responsive srcset
- Defer non-critical JS

## Mobile gestures
- Swipe gallery
- Pinch zoom
- Pull-to-refresh on listing pages
- Swipe-to-remove on cart line items (with undo)
- Long-press image for save/share menu

## Mobile keyboard handling
- Sticky elements adjust for keyboard open
- Form fields scroll into view on focus
- Submit button visible above keyboard

## Mobile error states
- Inline below field (don't push form down — animate above)
- Toast for global errors (top of screen)
- Network-loss banner at top with retry CTA

## Mobile loading
- Skeleton for product grid (matches card geometry)
- Spinner only for ≤2s waits
- Optimistic UI for ATC / qty changes

## Anti-patterns
- Touch targets <48px
- Hover-only interactions (no touch fallback)
- Auto-play video with sound
- Pop-ups that block scroll
- Forms that don't surface keyboard-correct types
- Sticky stacks ≥3 elements
- Mobile-as-afterthought ("mobile not yet specced" = auto-reject)

## Output
- All elio specs include explicit mobile breakdown
- Performance audit mandatory before vega ratification

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- test: /test — Intelligent Test Runner
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
