# Boldteq Org Structure v2 — Department + Sub-Department Hierarchy

**Date:** 2026-04-27
**Owner:** rex (strategic) + cadence (HR custodian)
**Replaces:** flat 6-department structure (executive / engineering / creative / growth / research / hr)
**Scope target:** scale 42 agents → 100+ without losing clarity
**Source of truth fields:** `~/.claude/org/registry.json` per-agent `department` + `subDepartment` + `pod` (optional)

---

## Why this exists

At 42 agents the flat 6-department view already mixes incompatible functions: "creative" bundles design + copy + SEO, "engineering" mixes 3 stack pods + platform + architecture + quality. As Boldteq scales toward 100+ agents the flat view becomes unreadable. This document defines the canonical hierarchy: **Department → Sub-Department → Pod (optional) → Specialist**.

---

## The 7 Departments

| # | Department | Lead | Sub-departments | Current size | Target @ 100 |
|---|-----------|------|-----------------|--------------|--------------|
| 1 | `executive` | rex | — | 1 | 1-2 |
| 2 | `engineering` | arya | pod-a, pod-b, pod-c, platform, architecture, quality | 13 | 30+ |
| 3 | `design` | vega | public-pages, ecom, dashboard, design-system, deliverables | 5 | 12+ |
| 4 | `content-seo` | quill | marketing-copy, cro-copy, lifecycle-email, app-store, developer-docs, seo | 5 | 12+ |
| 5 | `growth` | echo | cro, distribution, market-intel, email-infra | 7 | 12+ |
| 6 | `research` | nova | validation, market-research, measurement, portfolio | 7 | 10+ |
| 7 | `hr` | cadence | people-ops, hiring, training, accountability | 6 | 10+ |

**Note:** old `creative` department split into `design` + `content-seo` to remove function-mixing. Existing agents migrate per the table below.

---

## Full Hierarchy (current 42 + planned cohorts)

### 1. EXECUTIVE
- `rex` — Commander (top, no reports)

### 2. ENGINEERING (Lead: arya)

#### sub-dept: `architecture`
Cross-cutting design + bug fixing
- `arya` — VP Engineering (sub-lead)
- `vex` — Bug Fixer

#### sub-dept: `pod-a` (Stack A — Next.js + Supabase + Railway SaaS)
Lead: arya (interim) | Reports up: arya
- `koda` — Backend (Next.js API routes, Server Components, integrations)
- `pod-a-frontend` — Frontend (PLANNED Cohort 3 — React/Next.js components)
- `dato` — Database (also cross-pod DB mentor)
- `luna` — Test Engineer (also cross-pod test mentor)
- `sage` — Code Reviewer (also cross-pod review escalation)
- `riko` — Project Setup Specialist

#### sub-dept: `pod-b` (Stack B — Shopify Native, React Router 7 + Polaris)
- `pod-b-frontend` — Frontend
- `pod-b-backend` — Backend (Shopify Admin API + webhooks + Billing)
- `pod-b-db` — Database (Prisma + multi-shop tenant isolation)
- `pod-b-tester` — Test Engineer
- `pod-b-reviewer` — Code Reviewer (PLANNED — currently sage covers)

#### sub-dept: `pod-c` (Stack C — Shopify External standalone)
PLANNED Cohort 2 — entire pod not yet hired
- `pod-c-frontend`, `pod-c-backend`, `pod-c-db`, `pod-c-tester`, `pod-c-reviewer`

#### sub-dept: `platform`
DevOps + monitoring + reliability
- `bolt` — DevOps / Deployment Lead
- `hawk` — Ops / Monitoring

#### sub-dept: `quality`
Cross-pod quality leadership
- (sage already in pod-a but cross-listed quality lead)
- (luna already in pod-a but cross-listed test mentor)

### 3. DESIGN (Lead: vega)

#### sub-dept: `public-pages`
Marketing + public-facing pages (14 page types)
- `pixel` — Public-Facing Page Designer

#### sub-dept: `ecom`
Storefront design (Stack B/C)
- `elio` — Ecom UI Specialist + motion/interactions

#### sub-dept: `dashboard`
SaaS admin / multi-widget data viz
- `dash` — Dashboard Designer (PLANNED Cohort 3)

#### sub-dept: `design-system`
Tokens + design system architecture
- `token` — Design System Architect

#### sub-dept: `deliverables`
JSX→.fig + Code Connect
- `figma-synth` — JSX-to-Figma Specialist

#### sub-dept: `lead`
- `vega` — UI/UX Lead (sub-dept overseer; reports to quill currently — to migrate to standalone Design VP role)

### 4. CONTENT & SEO (Lead: quill)

#### sub-dept: `marketing-copy`
- `quill` — Lead + brand voice + landing/email/social/microcopy

#### sub-dept: `cro-copy`
Conversion copy under CRO Lead arbitration
- `spark` — Above-Fold Copywriter (hero + CTA)
- `merch` — Ecom On-Page Copywriter (PDP body, microcopy, objection handling)

#### sub-dept: `lifecycle-email`
- `sequence` — Lifecycle Email Specialist

#### sub-dept: `app-store`
- `serif` — App Store / PH / ASO Copywriter (PLANNED Cohort 5)

#### sub-dept: `developer-docs`
- `docsmith` — Developer Docs / API / SDK / Changelog (PLANNED Cohort 5)

#### sub-dept: `seo`
- `zeph` — SEO Specialist

### 5. GROWTH (Lead: echo)

#### sub-dept: `cro`
- `catalyst` — CRO Lead (sub-lead)
- `ecom-cro` — Below-Fold Mechanic Specialist
- `decoder` — Brand Pattern Extractor

#### sub-dept: `distribution`
- `echo` — VP Growth + Distribution Lead

#### sub-dept: `market-intel`
- `harvest` — Multi-Platform Market Intelligence Scraper

#### sub-dept: `email-infra`
- `postmark` — Resend Integration / Deliverability (PLANNED Cohort 5)

### 6. RESEARCH (Lead: nova)

#### sub-dept: `validation`
Idea + market + economics validation gates
- `scout` — Idea Validator
- `atlas` — Market Sizer
- `ledger` — Pricing & Unit Economics

#### sub-dept: `market-research`
- `nova` — VP Research + Competitive Intelligence

#### sub-dept: `measurement`
- `orbit` — Metrics Architect
- `pulse` — User Researcher

#### sub-dept: `portfolio`
- `verdict` — Portfolio Decider (30/90-day SCALE/PIVOT/KILL)

### 7. HR (Lead: cadence)

#### sub-dept: `people-ops`
- `cadence` — Head of People (sub-lead)

#### sub-dept: `hiring`
- `forge` — Agent Architect / Hiring Specialist

#### sub-dept: `training`
- `tutor` — Bulk Training Lead
- `mira` — Memory Keeper / Lesson Extraction

#### sub-dept: `accountability`
- `witness` — Performance Tracker
- `roster` — Registry & Records Keeper

---

## Schema additions

### `~/.claude/org/registry.json` per-agent fields

```jsonc
{
  "id": "elio",
  "department": "design",          // top-level (REQUIRED)
  "subDepartment": "ecom",         // sub-level (REQUIRED for new agents 2026-04-27+)
  "pod": null,                     // pod-a / pod-b / pod-c / null (only for engineering)
  "tier": "creative",
  "title": "Ecom UI Specialist",
  "reportsTo": "vega",
  // ... existing fields
}
```

### Agent .md frontmatter additions (forge template)

```yaml
---
name: ...
department: design
subDepartment: ecom
pod: null
reportsTo: vega
# ...
---
```

### Backwards compatibility

- Existing 42 agents auto-migrate via one-time script (parallel to this doc)
- Old `creative` department → split into `design` + `content-seo` per migration table
- All `subDepartment: null` rows treated as "default" (lead-level or unassigned)

---

## Migration Map (existing agents)

**Note:** `spark` / `merch` / `sequence` reclassified from `growth` to `content-seo` because their PRIMARY function is copy authoring. They report to `catalyst` (CRO Lead in growth) for strategy but their craft + brand voice ratification lives under quill (content-seo). Cross-functional reporting matrix below.

---

## Cross-Functional Reporting (matrix model)

Some agents have dual reporting — primary craft lead + cross-functional tactical lead. This avoids artificial dept assignment for agents who genuinely span two areas.

| Agent | Primary craft (dept) | Tactical lead (cross-fn) |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| spark | content-seo (quill) | growth-cro (catalyst) |
| merch | content-seo (quill) | growth-cro (catalyst) |
| sequence | content-seo (quill) | growth-cro (catalyst) |

| sage | engineering-quality (arya) | engineering-cross-pod-review-escalation |

Schema field: `secondaryReportsTo` (optional in registry.json).

---

## Scaling Rules

### When to add a sub-department
- A sub-department exceeds 8 agents → split or add granularity
- A new niche or capability emerges with no clean home → new sub-dept
- Two agents repeatedly collide on scope → may indicate sub-dept split

### When to add a department
- Top-level dept exceeds 25 agents AND can split cleanly along function lines
- New strategic pillar approved by Yash (e.g., future "Sales", "Customer Success", "Legal")

### When to add a pod
- Pods are reserved for engineering stack-specific clusters (pod-a / pod-b / pod-c)
- Other departments don't currently use pods
- New stack added → new pod (e.g., pod-d if AI-only stack ever splits from Stack A)

### When to merge sub-departments
- Sub-dept has ≤2 agents for >90 days AND function overlaps with adjacent sub-dept
- Cadence proposes merge in monthly review

---

Old routing (flat list):
```
- Ecom UI → elio
- Ecom Figma deliverable → figma-synth
- Ecom design tokens → token
- Public pages → pixel
- ...
```

New routing (hierarchical):
```
DESIGN (lead: vega)
  - public-pages → pixel
  - ecom (storefront, motion) → elio
  - dashboard → dash (Cohort 3+)
  - design-system → token
  - deliverables (Figma .fig + Code Connect) → figma-synth
```

Faster scan + clear escalation paths.

---

## Implementation Steps

1. **Org chart doc** (this file) — DONE
2. **registry.json migration** — Python script adds `subDepartment` field to all 42 agents per migration map
3. **CLAUDE.md update** — Replace flat routing with hierarchical dept→sub-dept routing
4. **Agent frontmatter retrofit** — Optional follow-up: add `subDepartment` to existing agent .md frontmatter (not blocking — registry.json is source of truth)

**Org Structure v2 (UPDATED 2026-04-27 — hierarchical, 7 depts + sub-depts + pods):**
Full org chart: `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/org-structure-v2.md`. Source of truth: `~/.claude/org/registry.json` (`department` + `subDepartment` + `pod` + `reportsTo` + `secondaryReportsTo`). Schema scales to 100+ agents without flat-list clutter.

**Pipeline shortcuts:**

- Market + business validation → `/validate-only` (Atlas → Arya → Riko → Ledger, 1 week)
- Pre-launch gate → `/launch-check` (Echo → Mira → Bolt → Hawk)
- Post-launch decision → `/verdict-30d` (Orbit → Pulse → Verdict)
- New project build → dispatched VP runs the pipeline; Rex only on Mode A new-product approval

---

**1. ENGINEERING (Lead: arya — VP Engineering)**

  *sub-dept: architecture* — `arya` (lead), `vex` (bug fixer)
  *sub-dept: pod-a (Stack A: Next.js + Supabase + Railway)* — `koda` (backend), `pod-a-frontend` (Cohort 3+), `dato` (db), `riko` (scaffolding)
  *sub-dept: pod-b (Stack B: Shopify Native, RR7 + Polaris)* — `pod-b-frontend`, `pod-b-backend`, `pod-b-db`, `pod-b-tester`, `pod-b-reviewer` (planned)
  *sub-dept: pod-c (Stack C: Shopify External standalone)* — Cohort 2+: `pod-c-frontend`, `pod-c-backend`, `pod-c-db`, `pod-c-tester`, `pod-c-reviewer`
  *sub-dept: platform* — `bolt` (DevOps/deploy), `hawk` (monitoring/ops)
  *sub-dept: quality* — `sage` (review lead, cross-pod), `luna` (test lead, cross-pod)

  Routing:
  - Bug report → `vex` (any stack)
  - Database work → `dato` (schema/migrations/RLS/triggers/Realtime/Edge Functions)
  - Tests → pod tester first; `luna` for cross-pod or strategy
  - Code review → pod reviewer first; `sage` for cross-pod or escalation
  - Deployment → `bolt` (after sage approves)
  - Monitoring → `hawk`
  - Project setup → `riko`

---

**2. DESIGN (Lead: vega — Design VP)**

  *sub-dept: lead* — `vega` (cross-dept design standards, escalation)
  *sub-dept: public-pages* — `pixel` (14 page types: landing, pricing, blog, about, contact, careers, case-study, integrations, docs, 404, coming-soon, legal)
  *sub-dept: ecom* — `elio` (PDP, cart, checkout, listing, hero, trust, post-purchase, subscription, motion, mobile)
  *sub-dept: dashboard* — `dash` (Cohort 3+; admin panels, multi-widget data viz)
  *sub-dept: design-system* — `token` (Tailwind/shadcn tokens, Polaris↔storefront bridge, Figma var sync)
  *sub-dept: deliverables* — `figma-synth` (JSX→.fig + Code Connect bidirectional)

---

**3. CONTENT & SEO (Lead: quill — VP Creative, brand voice custodian)**

  *sub-dept: marketing-copy* — `quill` (landing/email/social/microcopy + brand voice ratification)
  *sub-dept: cro-copy* — `spark` (above-fold hero/CTA, 40%+ lift), `merch` (ecom on-page: PDP body, cart microcopy, post-purchase, subscription, objections)
  *sub-dept: lifecycle-email* — `sequence` (welcome, cart-abandon, browse-abandon, post-purchase, win-back, subscription nurture)
  *sub-dept: app-store* — `serif` (Cohort 5; App Store / Shopify App Store / Product Hunt / ASO)
  *sub-dept: developer-docs* — `docsmith` (Cohort 5; API docs, SDK guides, changelogs)
  *sub-dept: seo* — `zeph` (technical SEO, structured data, ranking)

  Cross-functional: spark/merch/sequence have `secondaryReportsTo: catalyst` (CRO Lead in growth.cro).

---

**4. GROWTH (Lead: echo — VP Growth + Distribution)**

  *sub-dept: cro* — `catalyst` (CRO Lead, sub-lead), `ecom-cro` (below-fold mechanics: variants/bundles/cart/checkout/upsell), `decoder` (top-50 DTC brand teardowns, weekly intel, niche audits)
  *sub-dept: distribution* — `echo` (channel strategy, launch sequencing, content calendar)
  *sub-dept: market-intel* — `harvest` (multi-platform scraper: Skool, Reddit, HN, PH, Twitter, G2, Capterra)
  *sub-dept: email-infra* — `postmark` (Cohort 5; Resend integration, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, deliverability)

---

**5. RESEARCH (Lead: nova — VP Research)**

  *sub-dept: validation* — `scout` (idea validator), `atlas` (market sizer), `ledger` (pricing + unit economics)
  *sub-dept: market-research* — `nova` (competitive intelligence, persona extraction)
  *sub-dept: measurement* — `orbit` (metrics architect, KPI dashboards), `pulse` (user research, interview synthesis)
  *sub-dept: portfolio* — `verdict` (30/90-day SCALE/PIVOT/KILL decisions)

---

**6. HR (Lead: cadence — Head of People)**

  *sub-dept: people-ops* — `cadence` (weekly review cycles, promote/PIP/retire, org health)
  *sub-dept: hiring* — `forge` (capability gap detection, agent architecting, auto-deploy to probation)
  *sub-dept: training* — `tutor` (bulk training cycles, patches), `mira` (lesson extraction, memory keeper)
  *sub-dept: accountability* — `witness` (daily classification, performance), `roster` (registry source of truth, capability index)

---

**7. EXECUTIVE (Lead: rex — Strategic Commander)**

  - `rex` (portfolio decisions, new-product approval, kill gates, 30/90-day verdicts only)

---

**ECOM TEAM CROSS-FUNCTIONAL UNIT (added 2026-04-27)**
Spans design + content-seo + growth. Single brief → `catalyst` orchestrates. Strict scope split:
- Above-fold copy → `spark` | Below-fold mechanics → `ecom-cro` | On-page copy → `merch`
- Ecom UI/motion → `elio` | Tokens → `token` | Figma deliverables → `figma-synth`
- Brand intel → `decoder` | Lifecycle email → `sequence`
- KB: `~/.claude/memory/design/ecom/`, `content/ecom/`, `stacks/shopify/storefront/`, `patterns/good/ecom-brand-teardowns.md`, `patterns/good/ecom-funnel-cro-playbook.md`

import json
from collections import defaultdict
with open('/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/org/registry.json') as f:
    reg = json.load(f)

print(f"Org Structure Version: {reg.get('orgStructureVersion', 'v1')}")
print(f"Total agents: {len(reg['agents'])}")
print(f"Last updated: {reg['updatedAt']}\n")

by_d_s = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
pods = defaultdict(list)
secondary = []
for aid, a in reg["agents"].items():
    d = a.get("department", "?")
    s = a.get("subDepartment") or "(none)"
    by_d_s[d][s].append(aid)
    if a.get("pod"):
        pods[a["pod"]].append(aid)
    if a.get("secondaryReportsTo"):
        secondary.append((aid, a["reportsTo"], a["secondaryReportsTo"]))

# Print ASCII tree
DEPT_ORDER = ["executive", "engineering", "design", "content-seo", "growth", "research", "hr"]
print("━━━━━━━━━━━━ FINAL ORG TREE ━━━━━━━━━━━━\n")
for d in DEPT_ORDER:
    if d not in by_d_s: continue
    total = sum(len(v) for v in by_d_s[d].values())
    print(f"📁 {d}/  ({total} agents)")
    for s in sorted(by_d_s[d].keys()):
        agents = by_d_s[d][s]
        print(f"   └─ {s}/  ({len(agents)})")
        for a in sorted(agents):
            print(f"        • {a}")
    print()

print("━━━━━━━━━━━━ ENGINEERING PODS ━━━━━━━━━━━━")
for p in sorted(pods.keys()):

print("\n━━━━━━━━━━━━ CROSS-FUNCTIONAL (secondaryReportsTo) ━━━━━━━━━━━━")
for aid, primary, sec in sorted(secondary):
    print(f"  {aid:15} primary→{primary:10} secondary→{sec}")
PYEOF

content.text:
Org v2 live. Hierarchical structure verified on disk.

**42 agents → 7 departments → sub-departments → pods:**

```
📁 executive (1)
   └─ lead → rex

📁 engineering (13)
   ├─ architecture (2)  → arya, vex
   ├─ pod-a — Stack A SaaS (3) → koda, dato, riko
   ├─ pod-b — Stack B Shopify Native (4) → pod-b-{frontend,backend,db,tester}
   ├─ pod-c — Stack C planned (0) → Cohort 2 hires
   ├─ platform (2) → bolt, hawk
   └─ quality (2) → sage, luna [cross-pod mentors]

📁 design (5)
   ├─ lead → vega
   ├─ public-pages → pixel
   ├─ ecom → elio
   ├─ design-system → token
   └─ deliverables → figma-synth

📁 content-seo (5)
   ├─ marketing-copy → quill (lead, brand voice custodian)
   ├─ cro-copy → spark, merch [secondary→quill voice ratify]
   ├─ lifecycle-email → sequence [secondary→quill]
   └─ seo → zeph

📁 growth (5)
   ├─ cro → catalyst (sub-lead), ecom-cro, decoder
   ├─ distribution → echo (VP)
   └─ market-intel → harvest

📁 research (7)
   ├─ market-research → nova (VP)
   ├─ validation → scout, atlas, ledger
   ├─ measurement → orbit, pulse
   └─ portfolio → verdict

📁 hr (6)
   ├─ people-ops → cadence (VP)
   ├─ hiring → forge
   ├─ training → tutor, mira
   └─ accountability → witness, roster
```

**Cross-functional matrix (5 dual-reports):**
| Agent | Primary | Secondary |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| decoder | vega (interim → catalyst W2) | nova (market intel) |
| harvest | echo (distribution) | nova (market intel) |
| spark | catalyst (CRO tactical) | quill (brand voice) |
| merch | catalyst (CRO tactical) | quill (brand voice) |
| sequence | catalyst (CRO tactical) | quill (brand voice) |

**Files updated:**
- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/org-structure-v2.md` (canonical, 13KB)
- `~/.claude/org/registry.json` (`orgStructureVersion: 2`, all 42 agents have `department` + `subDepartment` + `pod` + `secondaryReportsTo`)
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (flat routing replaced with hierarchical org-tree, 30 sub-dept references)
- `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` (Critical Load First entry)
- `~/.claude/agents/forge.md` (template + org-placement gate for new hires)
- `~/.claude/agents/cadence.md` (Tier 1: review buckets by sub-dept)
- `~/.claude/agents/roster.md` (Tier 1: gap detection per sub-dept, registry-insert rejects missing fields)

**Scaling rules baked in:**
- Sub-dept ≥8 agents → split before adding more (forge enforces)
- Top-level dept ≥25 agents → can split along function lines
- New stack → new pod (engineering only)
- Sub-dept ≤2 agents for >90 days → cadence proposes merge
- Cross-functional dual-reporting via `secondaryReportsTo` field — no artificial dept assignment for spanning agents

**Room to grow:** current 42 → 100+ headroom in design (5→12+), content-seo (5→12+), growth (5→12+), engineering (13→30+ via pod-c + pod-a-frontend + pod-b-reviewer + pod-c-reviewer + more platform/quality specialists).

Want me to also retrofit `subDepartment` into all 42 agent .md frontmatter files (currently only registry.json has it — agent files still have old `department` only)? That's optional since registry is source of truth, but adds redundancy for clarity.

export interface Agent {
  filename: string
  path: string
  frontmatter: AgentFrontmatter & Record<string, unknown>
  name: string
  description: string
  model: string
  tools: string
  body: string
  raw: string
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface AgentFrontmatter {
  category?: string
  tags?: string
  output_template?: string
  icon?: string
  has_training?: boolean
}

export interface Template {
  filename: string
  path: string
  name: string
  description: string
  sections: string[]
  body: string
  raw: string
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface TrainingCorrection {
  id: string
  timestamp: string
  issue: string
  correction: string
  status: 'active' | 'archived'
}

export interface Category {
  name: string
  count: number
}

export interface Project {
  id: string
  name: string
  path: string
  displayPath: string
  hasClaudeDir: boolean
  hasClaudeMd: boolean
  agentCount: number
  commandCount: number
  ruleCount: number
  agents: Agent[]
  commands: string[]
  rules: string[]
}

export interface Command {
  name: string
  content: string
  path: string
}

export interface Rule {
  name: string
  content: string
  path: string
}

export interface AgentOrgInfo {
  level: number | null
  levelTitle: string | null
  yearsOfExperience: number | null
  experiencePoints: number | null
  tier: 'leadership' | 'engineer' | 'analyst' | 'creative' | string | null
  title: string | null
  status: 'active' | 'probation' | 'pip' | 'retired' | string | null
  department: string | null
  departmentLabel: string | null
  departmentColor: string | null
  reportsTo: string | null
  isLeader: boolean
}

// Per-row token-budget health — same signal as AgentHealthBar at the top of
// the agent editor, batched into /api/unified/agents so every list row can
// show it without a second round-trip.
export interface AgentRowHealth {
  status: 'healthy' | 'warning' | 'over' | 'sparse'
  usage: number                                // 0.0–1.2+ (fraction of budget)
  actual: { lines: number; chars: number }
  budget: { lines: number; chars: number; allowOversize: boolean }
  violations: Array<{ kind: string; actual: number; budget: number; limit?: number }>
  warnings: Array<{ kind: string; actual: number; budget: number }>
  estimatedTokens: number
  sizeKb: number
}

export interface UnifiedAgent extends Agent {
  scope: 'global' | 'project'
  scopeLabel: string
  projectId: string | null
  projectName: string | null
  org: AgentOrgInfo | null
  health: AgentRowHealth | null
}

export interface UnifiedCommand {
  name: string
  content: string
  path: string
  projectId: string
  projectName: string
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface UnifiedRule {
  name: string
  content: string
  path: string
  scope: 'global' | 'project'
  projectId: string | null
  projectName: string | null
  updatedAt: string
}

export interface AppConfig {
  claudeDir: string
  claudeDirExists: boolean
  home: string
  projectDirs: string[]
}

import { useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback, useRef, createContext, useContext } from 'react'
import {
  ReactFlow,
  Background,
  Controls,
  MiniMap,
  useNodesState,
  useEdgesState,
  type Node,
  type Edge,
  type NodeTypes,
  Handle,
  Position,
  BackgroundVariant,
  ReactFlowProvider,
  getNodesBounds,
  getViewportForBounds,
} from '@xyflow/react'
import '@xyflow/react/dist/style.css'
import { toPng } from 'html-to-image'
import {
  Users, Search, Cpu, Paintbrush, BarChart3, Shield,
  X, ChevronDown, ChevronRight, Network, LayoutGrid, List, Camera,
  Maximize2, Minimize2, Crown, AlertTriangle, Settings, Check,
} from 'lucide-react'
import { toast } from '../components/Toast'
import { getOrgChart, getDrift, getDepartments, updateOrgAgent, getGlobalAgents, subscribeOrgChart } from '../lib/api'
import type { OrgChartData, OrgChartNode, DriftData, OrgAgentPatch } from '../lib/api'
import type { Agent } from '../types'
import LevelBadge, { levelColors } from '../components/LevelBadge'
import AgentIcon from '../components/AgentIcon'

// ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Department view constants
const DEPT_WIDTH = 340
const DEPT_HEADER_HEIGHT = 68
const DEPT_PADDING_Y = 14
const MEMBER_ROW_HEIGHT = 90
const MEMBER_ROW_GAP = 6
const DEPT_ROW_GAP = 36
const LEADER_WIDTH = 260
const LEADER_HEIGHT = 96
const LEADER_DEPT_GAP = 90
// Multi-level tree gaps:
//   Row 0 (Rex)         → Row 1 (dept heads): DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP
//   Row 1 (dept heads)  → Row 2 (dept cols):  LEADER_DEPT_GAP (existing)
const DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP = 60
// Sub-member indent inside a department column (L3+ reports under a sub-manager)
const SUB_MEMBER_INDENT = 14

// Context for selecting a member from inside a DepartmentNode
// (avoids passing callbacks through node.data which causes re-render churn)
const OrgSelectContext = createContext<{
  selectedId: string | null
  onSelect: (id: string) => void
}>({ selectedId: null, onSelect: () => {} })

const TIER_ICONS: Record<string, typeof Cpu> = {
  leadership: Shield,
  engineer: Cpu,
  analyst: BarChart3,
  creative: Paintbrush,
}

const MODEL_BADGES: Record<string, { label: string; bg: string; text: string; border: string }> = {
  opus: { label: 'Opus', bg: 'rgba(168,85,247,0.15)', text: '#c084fc', border: 'rgba(168,85,247,0.3)' },
  sonnet: { label: 'Sonnet', bg: 'rgba(96,165,250,0.15)', text: '#60a5fa', border: 'rgba(96,165,250,0.3)' },
  haiku: { label: 'Haiku', bg: 'rgba(52,211,153,0.15)', text: '#34d399', border: 'rgba(52,211,153,0.3)' },
}

function extractEmoji(name: string): { emoji: string; cleanName: string } {
  const emoji = name.match(/^(\p{Emoji_Presentation}|\p{Extended_Pictographic})/u)?.[0] || ''
  const cleanName = name
    .replace(/^[\p{Emoji_Presentation}\p{Extended_Pictographic}]\s*[\u200d\ufe0f]*/u, '')
    .replace(/^—\s*/, '')
    .trim()
  return { emoji, cleanName: cleanName.split('—')[0]?.trim() || cleanName }
}

// ── Department Layout Algorithm ──────────────────────────────────────────────

interface MemberInfo {
  id: string
  name: string
  emoji: string
  title: string
  model: string
  tier: string
  phaseColor: string
  reportsTo: string | null
  dimmed: boolean
  // Indent depth inside a department column. 0 = direct report of the dept head;
  // 1 = report of a sub-manager (e.g. pod-b-db reports to dato inside engineering).
  indent: number
  level?: number | null
  levelTitle?: string | null
  yearsOfExperience?: number | null
  status?: 'active' | 'probation' | 'pip' | 'pending' | 'retired'
}

148	  departmentList: OrgChartData['departments'] = [],
149	): {
150	  rfNodes: Node[]
151	  rfEdges: Edge[]
152	} {
153	  // ── Layout shape ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
154	  // Row 0 (y=0):                                  [ Rex (LEADERSHIP) ]
155	  // Row 1 (y=LEADER_HEIGHT + DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP):  [ Arya ] [ Nova ] [ Quill ] ...
156	  // Row 2 (y=above + LEADER_HEIGHT + LEADER_DEPT_GAP):  Engineering | Research | ...
157	  //                                                     ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
158	  //                                                     │ Koda     │ │ Scout    │
159	  //                                                     │ Dato     │ │ ...      │
160	  //                                                     │  └ pod-b-db (indent)  │
161	  //                                                     └──────────┘ └──────────┘
162	  //
163	  // Strict leader rule: ONLY agents with `tier === 'leadership' && !reportsTo`
164	  // sit at Row 0. Everyone else lands in a department column or "Unassigned".
165	
166	  // Index nodes by id and by manager (reportsTo) — used for tree traversal.
167	  const byId = new Map<string, OrgChartNode>()
168	  const byManager = new Map<string | null, OrgChartNode[]>()
169	  for (const n of allNodes) {
170	    byId.set(n.id, n)
171	    const key = n.reportsTo || null
172	    if (!byManager.has(key)) byManager.set(key, [])
173	    byManager.get(key)!.push(n)
174	  }
175	
176	  const rex = allNodes.find(n => n.tier === 'leadership' && !n.reportsTo) || null
177	
178	  // Departments to render — server-ordered. Department head is rendered as a
179	  // Row 1 leader card and EXCLUDED from the column member list.
180	  const sortMembers = (a: OrgChartNode, b: OrgChartNode) => {
181	    if (a.tier === 'leadership' && b.tier !== 'leadership') return -1
182	    if (b.tier === 'leadership' && a.tier !== 'leadership') return 1
183	    if ((b.level || 0) !== (a.level || 0)) return (b.level || 0) - (a.level || 0)
184	    return a.name.localeCompare(b.name)
185	  }
186	
187	  // Build an ordered, indented member list for one department column. Walks
188	  // the reportsTo tree so sub-managers (e.g. dato) precede their reports
189	  // (pod-b-db indented one level under dato).
190	  const buildColumnMembers = (deptId: string, headId: string | null): MemberInfo[] => {
191	    const out: MemberInfo[] = []
192	    const seen = new Set<string>()
193	
194	    const sameDept = (n: OrgChartNode) => (n.department || '__unassigned__') === deptId
195	
196	    // Direct reports of the dept head (or top-of-column if no head).
197	    const roots = (byManager.get(headId) || [])
198	      .filter(sameDept)
199	      .filter(n => n.id !== headId)
200	      .slice()
201	      .sort(sortMembers)
202	
203	    const visit = (node: OrgChartNode, depth: number) => {
204	      if (seen.has(node.id)) return
205	      seen.add(node.id)
206	      out.push(toMemberInfo(node, depth))
207	      const children = (byManager.get(node.id) || [])
208	        .filter(sameDept)
209	        .slice()
210	        .sort(sortMembers)
211	      for (const c of children) visit(c, depth + 1)
212	    }
213	
214	    for (const r of roots) visit(r, 0)
215	
216	    // Catch any orphan in this department whose reportsTo points outside the
217	    // department (or is null) — render them at depth 0 so nobody is dropped.
218	    const orphans = allNodes
219	      .filter(sameDept)
220	      .filter(n => n.id !== headId && !seen.has(n.id))
221	      .slice()
222	      .sort(sortMembers)
223	    for (const o of orphans) visit(o, 0)
224	
225	    return out
226	  }

# Deep Ecom Figma UI/UX + Copywriting + CRO Team

**Date:** 2026-04-27
**Owner:** Yash (founder)
**Sponsor agent:** rex → cadence (HR exec) + vega (design lead) + catalyst (CRO lead, post-hire)
**Target outcome:** Production-grade ecom (Stack B Shopify Native + Stack C Shopify External) Figma UI/UX, on-page copy, and CRO capability — fully trained, gated, and live in 4 weeks.

---

## Context — why this build

Boldteq Software Factory roster has 30 agents currently, scaling to 54 via 6 weekly cohorts. Cohorts 3-5 already plan ecom-relevant specialists (elio, token, figma-synth, catalyst, decoder, spark, ecom-cro, sequence) but two real problems block "amazing ecom results":

1. **Knowledge gap.** The 43K-line design KB at `~/.claude/memory/design/` is SaaS-only — zero PDP/cart/checkout/listing/hero/trust/post-purchase/subscription/DTC patterns. `memory/content/copy-patterns.md` is empty skeleton. `cro-decoded-patterns.md` has framework but ecom-specific entries empty. Hiring agents into this vacuum produces mediocre output.

2. **Roster gap.** Quill = SaaS marketing. Spark = hero/CTA above-fold. Sequence = lifecycle email. Nobody owns ecom on-page copy (PDP descriptions, bullet hierarchy, FAQ, size guides, shipping/returns microcopy, cart upsell, checkout reassurance, post-purchase, subscription pages). - **KB source:** Decoder-first — hire decoder ahead of cohort, run top-50 DTC teardowns, KB authored from real winning patterns

---

## Final team — 9 agents

Excellent. Now I have enough data. Let me compile a comprehensive report under 700 words:

---

## ECOM TEAM BULK TRAINING + COORDINATION INFRASTRUCTURE MAPPING

### 1. TUTOR PATCH SYSTEM

**Patch Lifecycle (7 Steps):**
- **Files:** Patches stored in Supabase `training_patches` table (not markdown files). Schema: `cycle_id`, `agent_id`, `patch_type`, `section_target`, `content_added`, `rollback_content`, `applied`, `impact_score`.
- **Patch types:** `anti_pattern`, `smart_default`, `auto_fix`, `pattern_addition`, `update_existing`, `remove_stale`.
- **Rollback safety:** Every patch MUST capture `rollback_content` (exact original text). Edit tool only (never Write). **No patch is valid without rollback_content.**
- **Timing:** P0 (Yash) auto-apply immediately. P1-P2 stage for Cadence review. P3 (pre-approved) batch Sundays 03:00 UTC. P4-P5 weekly batch.
- **File pattern in memory:** Training cycles logged to `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-[id]-changelog.md` with: triggered_by, patches created, signals consumed, net impact.
- **Impact measurement:** 48h window—query `agent_runs` before/after patch apply; if `composite_score drop > 10 points` → auto-rollback + incident.

**Where training data LIVES:** Supabase **only**—tables `training_cycles`, `training_patches`, `training_signals`, `training_requests`, `agent_runs`. No markdown curriculum file exists yet. Schema: `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/memory/patterns/good/agent-ops-schema.md`.

---

### 2. TRAINING CYCLE LIFECYCLE

1. **Creation:** Tutor INSERTs `training_cycles (cycle_id, triggered_by, trigger_priority, status='in_progress')`.
2. **Review gate:** P1-P2 update status='staged_for_review' → Cadence approves within SLA.
3. **Application:** Tutor applies patches atomically via Edit tool (drift check first, drift detected → skip + incident).
4. **Measurement:** At `applied_at + 48h`, compare `AVG(composite_score)` before/after window.
5. **Rollback:** If regression >10%, Tutor calls Edit to restore `rollback_content`, sets `applied=false`.
6. **Completion:** Update `training_cycles.status='completed'`, write changelog.
7. **Next trigger:** Signal from Mira (post-build), Witness (yash correction), Cadence (approved request), or weekly Sunday 02:30 UTC batch.

**Gaps:** No "curriculum" file—training is signal-driven, not predetermined. No training questions/scenarios exist in structured form yet.

---

### 3. WHERE 100 ECOM TRAINING QUESTIONS SHOULD LIVE

**Option A (Recommended):** Create `~/.claude/memory/curriculum/ecom-team-onboarding-v1.md` with:
- Day 1 patterns (decoder brand teardown process, catalyst CRO strategy)
- Day 3 patterns (elio PDP specs, spark CTA formulas, merch copy rules)
- Day 7 patterns (ecom-cro mechanics, sequence email flows, token economics)
- Each day's patterns become P4 (Forge onboarding) training signals → Tutor patches on schedule

**Option B:** Store in Supabase `training_requests` (priority=P3, agent_id, skill_gap, evidence) manually populated by Cadence, auto-batched Sundays.

**Recommended:** Hybrid—markdown curriculum for discovery + Supabase rows for application tracking.

---

### 4. STANDARD HANDOFF JSON SHAPE

From orchestrations.js, handoff contracts follow this pattern (no strict JSON schema found—text-based):

```
Handoff: [FROM] → [TO]
Summary: [what done, why matters]
What Was Done: [checklist of deliverables]
Files Created/Modified: [paths + line counts]
Key Context for Next Agent: [constraints, decisions]
Blockers / Open Questions: [list with owners]
Quality Notes: [type safety ✅, tests ✅, perf ✅, a11y ✅]
Acceptance Criteria: [checklist for next agent]
Next Steps: [numbered actions]
Location: `.handoffs/[from]-to-[to]-[timestamp].md`
```

**Ecom agents (decoder → catalyst → elio, spark, ecom-cro, merch, sequence):**
- decoder → catalyst: brand teardown JSON (brand name, 8 dimensions, patterns observed, confidence)
- catalyst → elio/spark/merch: test roadmap + design/copy specs
- ecom-cro → sequence: mechanic implementations ready for email

**No strict handoffJSON interface—text-based markdown in `.handoffs/` directory.**

---

### 5. EXISTING ORCHESTRATION MECHANISM (Polyglot)

**dispatch.js:** Reads `~/.claude/org/registry.json` (agent definitions). GET `/api/dispatch/recommend?q=<query>` tokenizes query, scores agents by skill overlap (log-weighted hits), returns top 5 ranked by normalized score 0-1.

**orchestrations.js:** Node.js Express server with pipeline templates:
- Routes: GET `/api/orchestrations` (list), POST `/api/orchestrations` (save), GET `/api/orchestrations/runs` (history)
- Templates: "New Feature" (rex→arya→koda→luna→sage), "Bug Sprint" (vex→koda→luna→sage), "SaaS Launch" (scout→atlas→arya→riko→koda→bolt), "Content Push" (quill→zeph→echo), "DB Migration" (dato→luna→sage→bolt)
- Nodes run sequentially via `runClaudeSync()` spawning `claude -p` process (timeout 120s default)
- Approvals: `.waitForApproval()` stores in-process with 60-min timeout, REST endpoint `/api/orchestrations/approve/:runId/:nodeId`
- Logging: `agent_runs` table via `insertAgentRun()` (estimated tokens, cost)

**Gaps:** No per-agent training state in Polyglot. Dispatch.js is skill-based only (not training-aware). No feedback loop from `agent_runs` composite_score back to dispatch routing.

---

### 6. COORDINATION GAPS FOR 9-AGENT ECOM BUILD

1. **No persistent training memory between cycles.** Each cohort onboards from templates, not prior ecom cohort lessons.
2. **Handoff contracts are text, not structured JSON.** Can't automatically route based on previous output quality.
3. **No "training readiness" gate before dispatch.** All 9 agents start simultaneously; no pre-training stage.
4. **Orchestrations.js doesn't read `training_patches`—can't apply recent Tutor patches to agents mid-run.**
5. **Agent registry (registry.json) decoupled from Supabase `agents` table.** Dispatch routing ignores `composite_score`, only reads `skills` object.
6. **No curriculum for CRO team specifically.** Eio, catalyst, spark, ecom-cro, merch, sequence have no pre-wired patterns—must source from Decoder on Day 1.

**To unblock:** (a) Sync registry.json → Supabase agents table before dispatch; (b) Make Tutor patches injectable into agent .md before orchestration starts; (c) Pre-build ecom curriculum 7 days before cohort hire; (d) Add `training_readiness` gate in orchestrations.js.

- Templates: "New Feature" (rex→arya→koda→luna→sage), "Bug Sprint" (vex→koda→luna→sage), "SaaS Launch" (scout→atlas→arya→riko→koda→bolt), "Content Push" (quill→zeph→echo), "DB Migration" (dato→luna→sage→bolt)
- Nodes run sequentially via `runClaudeSync()` spawning `claude -p` process (timeout 120s default)
- Approvals: `.waitForApproval()` stores in-process with 60-min timeout, REST endpoint `/api/orchestrations/approve/:runId/:nodeId`
- Logging: `agent_runs` table via `insertAgentRun()` (estimated tokens, cost)

**Gaps:** No per-agent training state in Polyglot. Dispatch.js is skill-based only (not training-aware). No feedback loop from `agent_runs` composite_score back to dispatch routing.

---

### 6. COORDINATION GAPS FOR 9-AGENT ECOM BUILD

1. **No persistent training memory between cycles.** Each cohort onboards from templates, not prior ecom cohort lessons.
2. **Handoff contracts are text, not structured JSON.** Can't automatically route based on previous output quality.
3. **No "training readiness" gate before dispatch.** All 9 agents start simultaneously; no pre-training stage.
4. **Orchestrations.js doesn't read `training_patches`—can't apply recent Tutor patches to agents mid-run.**
5. **Agent registry (registry.json) decoupled from Supabase `agents` table.** Dispatch routing ignores `composite_score`, only reads `skills` object.
6. **No curriculum for CRO team specifically.** Eio, catalyst, spark, ecom-cro, merch, sequence have no pre-wired patterns—must source from Decoder on Day 1.

**To unblock:** (a) Sync registry.json → Supabase agents table before dispatch; (b) Make Tutor patches injectable into agent .md before orchestration starts; (c) Pre-build ecom curriculum 7 days before cohort hire; (d) Add `training_readiness` gate in orchestrations.js.
Phase 1 mapped. Phase 2 — 2 strategic decisions before writing final plan.

# Phase 2 — Bulk Training (100 Questions) + Coordination Setup

**Date added:** 2026-04-27 (evening)
**Owner:** Yash + cadence + tutor + mira
**Sponsor:** rex
**Target:** Extract Yash's tacit ecom knowledge across 100 targeted questions, package as Tutor patches, deploy via Mira→Tutor canonical pipeline. Build production coordination so 9 agents operate as one unit, not 9 disconnected specialists.

## Context — why Phase 2

Phase 1 hired 9 agents, scaffolded KB, wired Polyglot org-v2. Agents now exist but are GENERIC — they have skill files seeded from competitive research, none of Yash's specific brand voice / niche priorities / lift-target calibration. Without this knowledge, the team produces "good ecom" not "Boldteq-grade ecom." Two gaps:

1. **No tacit knowledge transfer mechanism.** Tutor patches are signal-driven (Yash corrections, Witness antipatterns) — there's no proactive curriculum extraction.
2. **No production coordination.** Handoff contracts are text-based markdown in `.handoffs/`. Polyglot orchestrations.js has 5 pipeline templates but no ecom-team pipeline. Dispatch is skill-based only — ignores `composite_score`, no training-readiness gate. 9 agents would dispatch in parallel with no acceptance criteria between phases.

Yash decisions confirmed 2026-04-27:
- **Q delivery:** Chat batches, 10–15 questions per session (~7-8 sessions over 2-3 weeks)
- **Coordination scope:** Full — handoff JSON schema + Polyglot pipeline + training-readiness gate
- **Training pipe:** Canonical Mira → Tutor patches (P3 priority, rollback_content, 48h impact, auto-rollback)

## Deliverable A — 100-Question Curriculum

**File:** `~/.claude/memory/curriculum/ecom-team-training-v1.md` (~800 lines)

**Question distribution per agent** (proportional to scope + complexity):

| Agent | # Q | Categories |
|-------|-----|------------|
| decoder | 10 | brand teardown methodology, niche audit selection, pattern-promotion thresholds, top-50 priority order, evidence rules |
| catalyst | 12 | CRO strategy framework, ICE prioritization weights, 40% lift baseline definition, scope-split arbitration, stat-gate enforcement, holdout strategy |
| elio | 18 | PDP layout decisions, cart drawer vs page, checkout step count, listing/category UX, hero type per niche, motion budget, mobile breakpoint priorities, design-system bridge |
| token | 8 | brand color OKLCH ramp generation, contrast gate enforcement, Polaris↔storefront bridge decisions, Figma sync direction (code-wins default), token addition gate |
| figma-synth | 8 | JSX→.fig pipeline edge cases, Code Connect mapping conventions, ecom canonical mappings library scope, breaking-change protocol |
| spark | 10 | hero headline formulas per niche, CTA verb library, banned words enforcement, A/B variant rules, niche intensity matrix |
| ecom-cro | 12 | cart state machine, free-shipping threshold per niche, upsell eligibility logic, subscription default state, abandon trigger conditions, post-purchase one-click rules |
| merch | 14 | PDP body order rules, benefits-first enforcement, objection-handling per niche, microcopy character limits, post-purchase tone, subscription cancellation copy |
| sequence | 8 | welcome series cadence, cart-abandon discount escalation, win-back stop rules, subscription pre-renewal pattern |
| **Total** | **100** | |

**Question format** (each):
```yaml

## Deliverable C — Mira → Tutor Pipeline Wiring

**Existing infra (reuse, no reinvention):**

## Deliverable D — Handoff JSON Schema

**File:** `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/ecom-handoff-schema.md` (~250 lines)

**Schema (TypeScript + JSON Schema both shipped):**
```typescript
interface EcomHandoff {
  schemaVersion: "1.0"
  from: AgentId
  to: AgentId | AgentId[]  // array for fan-out (catalyst → [elio, spark, merch])
  type: "design-spec" | "copy-spec" | "mechanic-spec" | "teardown" | "patch" | "test-result"
  brief_id: string  // links to project brief
  surface: "pdp" | "cart" | "checkout" | "listing" | "hero" | "post-purchase" | "subscription" | "email"
  deliverables: {
    files_written: { path: string; lines: number }[]
    artifacts: { type: string; path_or_id: string }[]
    decoder_evidence: string[]  // brand citations (3+ required)
    lift_target: number  // e.g., 0.40 for 40%
  }
  validation: {
    self_check_passed: boolean
    voice_scorecard: number | null  // copy agents only
    decoder_baseline_cited: boolean
    mobile_specced: boolean
    accessibility_passed: boolean
  }
  blockers: { description: string; owner: AgentId }[]
  next_steps: { action: string; owner: AgentId }[]
  composite_score_at_handoff: number  // from Polyglot dispatch readiness
  timestamp: string
}
```

**Embedded into every ecom agent's auto-fix loop section** — agent .md updated to reference this schema as the canonical handoff format.

## Deliverable E — Polyglot Ecom Pipeline

**File:** `Polyglot/src/lib/orchestrations/ecom-team-pipeline.js` (new, ~250 lines) — register in `Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js` template list.

**Pipeline definition:**
```
[start: brief]
  ↓
[1] decoder → brand teardown / niche audit (parallel: 3 brands)
  ↓ catalyst.approval gate (decoder evidence ≥3 brands per niche)
[2] catalyst → CRO strategy + funnel diagnosis + test priority
  ↓ catalyst dispatches in parallel
[3a] elio → design specs (PDP, cart, hero per surface)
[3b] spark → above-fold copy variants (3 variants per surface)
[3c] merch → PDP body + microcopy slot fills
  ↓ merge gate (vega ratifies design + quill ratifies copy voice)
[4] ecom-cro → mechanic implementations + abandon triggers
  ↓ catalyst.approval gate (scope-split verified, no overlap)
[5] figma-synth → JSX→.fig + Code Connect mappings
  ↓
[6] token → token additions + Figma var sync
  ↓
[7] sequence → lifecycle email sequences (consumes ecom-cro abandon triggers)
  ↓
[end: handoff to pod-frontend (Stack B/C)]
```

**Approval gates:** `runClaudeSync` blocks until cadence/yash approves at gate. Existing `.waitForApproval()` mechanism reused.

## Deliverable F — Training-Readiness Gate

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/dispatch/readiness/:agentId` (new in `Polyglot/src/routes/dispatch.js`)

**Logic:**
```javascript
// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [
    composite < 7.0 ? `composite_score ${composite.toFixed(1)} < 7.0 threshold` : null,
    trainingPatchesApplied < 5 ? `only ${trainingPatchesApplied}/5 minimum patches applied` : null,
  ].filter(Boolean),
  threshold: { composite: 7.0, patches: 5 },
}
```

**Pipeline check:** orchestrations.js calls readiness before each node. Non-ready node:
- W1-W3: ADVISORY mode (warn but don't block) — cadence sees warning in dashboard
- W4+: ENFORCING mode (block + escalate to cadence)

**OrgChart UI badge:** add green/amber/red dot per agent member row showing `composite_score` + readiness status. New column in `client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx` member render — single-line addition next to status badge.

**Date added:** 2026-04-27 (evening)
**Owner:** Yash + cadence + tutor + mira
**Sponsor:** rex

## Context — why Phase 2

Phase 1 hired 9 agents, scaffolded KB, wired Polyglot org-v2. Agents now exist but are GENERIC — they have skill files seeded from competitive research, none of Yash's specific brand voice / niche priorities / lift-target calibration. Without this knowledge, the team produces "good ecom" not "Boldteq-grade ecom." Two gaps:

1. **No tacit knowledge transfer mechanism.** Tutor patches are signal-driven (Yash corrections, Witness antipatterns) — there's no proactive curriculum extraction.

// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [
    composite < 7.0 ? `composite_score ${composite.toFixed(1)} < 7.0 threshold` : null,
    trainingPatchesApplied < 5 ? `only ${trainingPatchesApplied}/5 minimum patches applied` : null,

  threshold: { composite: 7.0, patches: 5 },
}
```

Boldteq Software Factory roster has 30 agents currently, scaling to 54 via 6 weekly cohorts. Cohorts 3-5 already plan ecom-relevant specialists (elio, token, figma-synth, catalyst, decoder, spark, ecom-cro, sequence) but two real problems block "amazing ecom results":

// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [
    composite < 7.0 ? `composite_score ${composite.toFixed(1)} < 7.0 threshold` : null,

}

Phase 1 hired 9 agents, scaffolded KB, wired Polyglot org-v2. Dispatch is skill-based only — ignores `composite_score`, no training-readiness gate. 9 agents would dispatch in parallel with no acceptance criteria between phases.

## Deliverable F — Training-Readiness Gate

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/dispatch/readiness/:agentId` (new in `Polyglot/src/routes/dispatch.js`)

**Logic:**
```javascript
// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [
    composite < 7.0 ? `composite_score ${composite.toFixed(1)} < 7.0 threshold` : null,
    trainingPatchesApplied < 5 ? `only ${trainingPatchesApplied}/5 minimum patches applied` : null,
  ].filter(Boolean),
  threshold: { composite: 7.0, patches: 5 },
}
```

**Pipeline check:** orchestrations.js calls readiness before each node. Non-ready node:
- W1-W3: ADVISORY mode (warn but don't block) — cadence sees warning in dashboard
- W4+: ENFORCING mode (block + escalate to cadence)

// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [

}

# Mira — Curriculum Extraction Protocol

**Owner:** mira
**Used by:** mira (post-session) + tutor (downstream patches)
**Trigger:** After each `/train ecom session N` chat batch completes
**Source:** `~/.claude/memory/curriculum/ecom-team-training-v1.md`

---

## What this protocol does

Reads Yash's answers to ecom-team training questions, extracts a structured lesson per Q+A pair, writes the lesson back into the curriculum file, and creates Supabase `training_patches` rows scoped to the relevant agent. Each patch includes `rollback_content` so 48h impact measurement can auto-revert regressions.

---

## Inputs

1. Curriculum file: `~/.claude/memory/curriculum/ecom-team-training-v1.md`
2. Session number (1..8) from Yash's `/train ecom session N` invocation
3. Active Tutor `training_cycle_id` (open one if none active for ecom curriculum)

## Outputs

1. Updated curriculum file: `mira_lesson_extracted` + `tutor_patch_id` + `status` populated for each answered Q

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

questions.question: META-001 — Boldteq positioning vs other ecom-build agencies (Webstacks/Diviv/Built By/Eight25). What's the core promise we make that they can't?

options.label: AI-first — 9-agent specialist team, full ecom build in 4 weeks (Recommended)
options.description: We deploy a coordinated AI agent team (decoder, catalyst, elio, spark, merch, ecom-cro, etc.) that produces decoder-validated, CRO-tested ecom builds in 1/4 the time of human agencies. Agencies need 16-20 weeks; we ship in 4. Not human-replacement — founder-velocity.

options.label: Decoder-validated CRO — every build cites 3+ brand patterns
options.description: Boldteq guarantees every design and copy decision is backed by ≥3 top-50 DTC brand patterns + a 40%+ lift target. Agencies guess from intuition; we ship from validated playbooks. Provable craft.

options.label: Founder-direct — Yash runs every build, no account managers
options.description: Boldteq is a founder-led shop — you talk to Yash, who orchestrates the AI team. No layered account managers, no slow approval chains. Direct, fast, premium.

options.label: Production-grade from day 1 — no MVP excuses
options.description: Auth, billing, error boundaries, mobile, motion, accessibility — all on v1. Agencies ship MVPs and bill for v2 polish. We ship complete the first time.

questions.question: META-002 — 3 adjectives that DESCRIBE Boldteq voice + 3 that explicitly DON'T. Pick the closest match.

options.label: IS: confident, precise, founder-direct — IS NOT: salesy, hedged, agency-corporate (Recommended)
options.description: Voice asserts strong opinions (confident), uses specific numbers + named patterns (precise), sounds like a founder shipping (direct). Avoids: marketing-speak (salesy), 'depending on...' qualifiers (hedged), agency-deck-template language (corporate).

options.label: IS: bold, technical, opinionated — IS NOT: cute, generic, fluffy
options.description: Bold declarations, technical specificity, strong stances. Avoids playful tone, generic copy, padding/fluff. More engineering-shop than design-shop.

options.label: IS: warm-confident, expert, no-BS — IS NOT: cold, jargon-heavy, apologetic
options.description: Warm + confident (premium agency tone), expert without being academic, direct without being rude. Avoids robotic distance, unexplained jargon, over-apologizing.

options.label: IS: direct, evidence-led, ambitious — IS NOT: clever, vague, modest
options.description: Sentences are short and clear (direct), every claim cites a number or brand (evidence-led), targets are aggressive (40%+ lift, 4-week build). Avoids wordplay/cleverness, vague claims, false modesty.

questions.question: META-003 — What 3 anti-signals immediately tell you a piece of copy/spec is NOT Boldteq quality?

options.label: Banned words + hedging + no specific number (Recommended)
options.description: 1) Uses 'leverage / synergy / innovative / seamless / robust / cutting-edge / next-gen / best-in-class' (auto-reject). 2) Hedges with 'usually / often / depends'. 3) Makes a claim without a specific number or brand citation.

options.label: Passive voice + feature-led + generic CTA
options.description: 1) Passive voice (Boldteq writes active). 2) Leads with features instead of benefits. 3) Generic CTAs like 'Learn more', 'Click here', 'Submit'.

options.label: No decoder evidence + no mobile spec + no scope split
options.description: 1) Spec/copy doesn't cite ≥3 decoder brands. 2) Desktop-only design with no mobile breakdown. 3) Cross-scope creep (spark touching merch territory, etc.).

options.label: Marketing-template structure + apologetic tone + over-explaining
options.description: 1) Reads like an agency template (intro→our process→why us). 2) Apologizes for friction ('Sorry to bother you...'). 3) Over-explains decisions instead of stating them.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-001 — Brand contradicts decoder library (e.g., Glossier shifts hero pattern). What does decoder do with old entry?

options.label: Demote old to provisional + create new entry tagged with date (Recommended)
options.description: Old pattern stays in library tagged 'provisional · superseded YYYY-MM-DD by [new-pattern-id]'. New entry created with current date. Preserves historical evidence; prevents stale recommendations. Auto re-teardown trigger if old entry referenced in any active spec.

options.label: Re-teardown brand immediately, replace old entry
options.description: Drop old entry entirely, run fresh full teardown, replace with current pattern. Cleanest library state but loses historical trace.

options.label: Keep old entry, add new as alternative — let catalyst pick
options.description: Both versions live in library. Catalyst chooses per-brief based on niche/era. Most flexible but biggest cognitive load.

options.label: Re-teardown only when 12+ months old AND active spec references it
options.description: Lazy revalidation — only spend decoder time when old pattern is actively being used. Cheapest but risks shipping with stale patterns.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-002 — Of 50 brands, which 5 to teardown FIRST (W1 days 1-3) for max downstream value to elio/spark/merch?

options.label: Allbirds, Glossier, Casper, Magic Spoon, Athletic Greens (Recommended)
options.description: Maximum niche diversity (apparel/beauty/home/CPG/supplements) + each is the canonical reference for their niche. One pattern from each transfers to 8–10 sibling brands. Optimizes decoder coverage breadth Day 1.

options.label: Allbirds, Gymshark, Vuori, Lululemon, Outdoor Voices
options.description: Apparel-only deep dive. Sacrifices niche breadth for category depth — best if first Boldteq client is apparel. Risky if first client is a different niche.

options.label: Athletic Greens, Hims, Ritual, Curology, Care/of
options.description: Subscription/DTC health-vertical focus — best for clients in supplements/wellness. Skews library toward subscription mechanics; weak coverage of one-time-purchase patterns.

options.label: Glossier, Fenty, Drunk Elephant, The Ordinary, Rare Beauty
options.description: Beauty-only. Same risk as apparel-only — deep coverage but narrow.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-003 — Pattern in 2 brands + decoder-cited 30%+ lift in case studies. Promote, hold, or wait for 3rd brand?

options.label: Hold at provisional — require 3rd brand even with cited lift (Recommended)
options.description: Cited lift in case studies is self-reported and often unverified. Stay strict: 3-brand threshold for promotion. Tag pattern 'provisional · high-lift cited' so catalyst can use it experimentally but it's not in canonical library yet.

options.label: Promote with caveat — 'validated, awaiting 3rd-brand confirmation'
options.description: Move to validated tier but flag as pending. Catalyst can use freely. 3rd-brand discovery upgrades to canonical.

options.label: Promote immediately if cited lift ≥30% — evidence is evidence
options.description: Treat cited lift as substitute for 3rd brand. Fast library growth but risks promoting unverified patterns.

options.label: Run a dedicated A/B on Boldteq client to validate before promoting
options.description: Hold at provisional, escalate to catalyst to test on first matching client. Slowest but highest-confidence.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-004 — Catalyst requests 'beauty niche audit' for client. How many brands + time budget?

options.label: Top 10 brands, 60 min/brand abbreviated teardown, 8–12h total (Recommended)
options.description: 10 brands = enough for cross-brand pattern triangulation (3+ thresholds achievable). 60 min/brand = focused teardown on requested dimensions only. Total fits inside 1-2 working days. Per skill file niche-audit-protocol.md.

options.label: Top 5 brands, 90 min/brand full teardown, 4–6h total
options.description: Faster but only 5 brands — risks missing 3-brand threshold for some patterns. Full teardown depth per brand. Best for tight client deadlines.

options.label: Top 20 brands, 30 min/brand quick scan, 8–10h total
options.description: Maximum brand coverage but each scan is shallow — hero/PDP/cart only, no checkout/post-purchase. Best for trend-spotting, not deep specs.

options.label: Top 10 + 5 quick scans = 15 brands, 12–16h total
options.description: Hybrid — deep on 10, surface scan on 5 outliers. Best library-building but burns decoder hours.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-005 — Pattern appears in apparel + supplements + CPG (3 niches). Universal DTC pattern or niche-tagged?

options.label: Universal if ≥3 niches AND ≥1 brand per niche — tag with verified niches (Recommended)
options.description: Promote to 'universal-DTC' tier when pattern hits 3+ different niches with at least 1 brand evidence each. Tag entry with all verified niches. Mark explicitly which niches are UNVERIFIED so spark/merch don't over-extrapolate to luxury/B2B.

options.label: Universal only if ≥5 niches — stricter to avoid over-generalization
options.description: Keep at niche-tagged until 5 niches verified. Conservative but slower library growth.

options.label: Always niche-tagged — never universal, force per-niche specs always
options.description: Force decoder to always tag patterns by niche. Catalyst manually reasons about transferability. Most rigorous, highest cognitive load.

options.label: Universal at 3 niches BUT exclude luxury + B2B by default
options.description: Same as recommended but explicitly carve out luxury (Goop, Aritzia) and B2B — those niches need separate patterns. Add 'mass-market' qualifier.

content.text: Round 2 done. Round 3 (4 more decoder Q).

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-006 — Brand checkout requires login (e.g., Costco). Decoder can't capture without account. Mark N/A or skip teardown?

options.label: Capture ≥6/8 dimensions = valid teardown, mark missing as N/A (Recommended)
options.description: Threshold: ≥6 of 8 dimensions captured → teardown counts. Missing dimensions tagged 'N/A — [reason: login wall]'. <6 captured → skip + log to backlog. Allows 'most of Costco' to inform library while flagging gaps.

options.label: Strict: must have all 8 dimensions or skip entirely
options.description: Zero tolerance for partial teardowns. Cleanest data but loses brands like Costco, B2B catalogs, members-only sites entirely.

options.label: Capture what you can, no minimum threshold — partial teardowns are valid
options.description: Even 2 dimensions counts as a teardown. Maximum library coverage but quality varies wildly.

options.label: Create burner account where ToS allows, capture full teardown
options.description: Decoder uses test accounts to bypass login walls. Fullest coverage but legal risk + maintenance burden.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-007 — Decoder runs 1 full + 5 quick scans/week. When does ratio FLEX (e.g., during client onboarding)?

options.label: Catalyst can request 'pause weekly + run 5 fulls in client niche' for active client briefs (Recommended)
options.description: Default cadence holds. Catalyst dispatches 'niche-audit override' when active client brief lands. Decoder pauses weekly intel for 1-2 weeks, runs 5-10 fulls in client's niche. Returns to default after client onboarding completes.

options.label: Cadence (HR) approves all flex requests — catalyst can't override directly
options.description: Slower but adds governance — prevents decoder from being constantly diverted by catalyst urgency.

options.label: No flex — default cadence always holds, catalyst uses what's already in library
options.description: Most predictable decoder output but catalyst may have stale/missing niche data when client briefs land.

options.label: Yash-only override — only Yash can flex decoder cadence
options.description: Highest bar for flex. Forces catalyst to build briefs from existing library.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-008 — New DTC unicorn emerges after top-50 list published. How does decoder handle list updates?

options.label: Quarterly review — decoder + catalyst rank candidates, replace lowest-priority unviewed brands (Recommended)
options.description: Quarterly cadence (every ~12 weeks) decoder + catalyst review brand performance + new entrants. Replace bottom 5–10 of list (those not yet teardown'd OR teardown 12+ months stale) with new entrants. Maintains 50 active priority. Logged in changelog.

options.label: Append to end of queue — list grows over time
options.description: Never remove brands. List grows to 60, 70, 100 over time. Risks queue becoming unmanageable.

options.label: Catalyst can add immediately when relevant for client niche
options.description: On-demand additions when needed. No quarterly review. Faster but list becomes ad-hoc.

options.label: Hard freeze at 50 — no updates ever, focus on completing original list
options.description: Lock the priority queue. Only review after all 50 teardown'd.

questions.question: ECOM-DEC-009 — Catalyst A/B test on decoder-validated pattern LOSES. Single failure invalidates? N=2? N=3?

options.label: 1 failure in same niche = bump confidence DOWN one tier; 2 failures = demote to 'avoid' (Recommended)
options.description: Single fail tied to specific niche → confidence demotion (canonical → strong → validated → provisional). 2 fails in same niche → move to patterns/avoid/invalidated-cro-patterns.md tagged with both test_ids. Cross-niche fails don't demote a universal pattern.

options.label: 1 failure = immediate demotion to 'avoid'

---
name: Brand Voices
description: Voice profiles across Boldteq products. Canonical brand-voice rules — applies to quill, spark, merch, sequence (and quill ratifies all 3).
type: reference
last_updated: 2026-04-27
curriculum_source: Session 1 — META-001..003
---

## Boldteq Brand Voice — Canonical (v1, ratified 2026-04-27)

### Positioning (META-001)

**Boldteq's promise vs other ecom-build agencies (Webstacks/Diviv/Built By/Eight25):**

> AI-first 9-agent specialist team delivering decoder-validated, CRO-tested ecom builds in **4 weeks** vs human agencies' 16-20 weeks. **Founder-velocity, not human-replacement.**

- **Use this anchor** in any client-facing copy or strategy doc.
- **Differentiator** = speed (4-week vs 16-20-week) + craft (decoder-validated, ≥3 brand evidence per pattern, 40%+ lift target).
- **Not** = "human-replacement", "AI tool", "AI assistant" framing. Always: "AI-coordinated team."
- **Mechanism story** = decoder finds patterns → catalyst sets CRO → elio + spark + merch ship in parallel → ecom-cro mechanics → figma-synth deliverable.

### Voice DNA (META-002)

**IS: confident, precise, founder-direct**
- **Confident** = assert opinions. State decisions, not options. "We do X" not "Some teams might consider X."
- **Precise** = specific numbers + named patterns. "40% lift vs Allbirds baseline" not "significant improvement."
- **Founder-direct** = sounds like Yash shipping. Active voice, short sentences, no padding.

**IS NOT: salesy, hedged, agency-corporate**
- **Salesy** = marketing-speak ("transform your business", "unlock value"). Auto-reject.
- **Hedged** = "depending on...", "usually", "often" without specifying conditions. Auto-reject.
- **Agency-corporate** = deck-template language ("Phase 1: Discovery", "Our process is..."). Auto-reject.

### Anti-Signals — Grep-Detectable Quality Failures (META-003)

**Three auto-reject patterns:**

1. **Banned words list** — auto-reject any output containing:
   - `leverage` · `synergy` · `innovative` · `seamless` · `robust` · `cutting-edge` · `next-gen` · `best-in-class`
   - Detection: `grep -wE 'leverage|synergy|innovative|seamless|robust|cutting-edge|next-gen|best-in-class'`

2. **Hedging language** — auto-reject if used without specific conditions:
   - `usually` · `often` · `typically` · `tends to` · `generally` · `most cases` · `depending on (the situation)`
   - Detection: `grep -wE 'usually|often|typically|tends to|generally|most cases|depending on the (situation|case)'`
   - **Allowed when** condition is specified — e.g., "usually $50, $80 for premium" passes; "usually higher" fails.

3. **No specific number / no brand citation** — auto-reject claims missing evidence:
   - Any benefit claim without a number → fail. "Glowing skin" fails; "Glowing skin in 14 days" passes.
   - Any pattern recommendation without brand citation → fail. "Use cart drawer" fails; "Use cart drawer (per Bombas/Vuori/OV)" passes.
   - Detection: heuristic — Sage flags claim sentences (verbs: lifts/converts/improves/reduces) lacking `\d+%` or brand-name regex.

### Voice Scorecard (Quill ratifies, ≥8/9 to pass)

| Dimension | Weight | Pass criteria |
|-----------|--------|---------------|
| Active voice | 1 | Passive voice <10% of sentences |
| Specific numbers | 2 | ≥1 specific number per benefit claim |
| Brand citations | 2 | ≥3 decoder brands per pattern recommendation (design/copy/mechanic) |
| No banned words | 2 | grep clean |
| No hedging without conditions | 1 | grep clean OR conditions specified |
| Founder-direct tone | 1 | First-person plural OK; no "we believe" / "we feel" hedging |

**Total: 9 points · ≥8 required to pass.** Sub-7 = block handoff, return to copy agent for revision.

### Per-Agent Application

| Agent | Voice scorecard required? | Self-check before handoff |
|-------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| quill | Yes (own scorecard, also ratifies others) | All 6 dimensions |
| spark | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + above-fold density check |
| merch | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + benefits-first PDP order |
| sequence | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + subject ≤50 chars + single CTA |

## Boldteq Brand Voice — Canonical (v1, ratified 2026-04-27)

### Positioning (META-001)

**Boldteq's promise vs other ecom-build agencies (Webstacks/Diviv/Built By/Eight25):**

> AI-first 9-agent specialist team delivering decoder-validated, CRO-tested ecom builds in **4 weeks** vs human agencies' 16-20 weeks. **Founder-velocity, not human-replacement.**

- **Use this anchor** in any client-facing copy or strategy doc.
- **Differentiator** = speed (4-week vs 16-20-week) + craft (decoder-validated, ≥3 brand evidence per pattern, 40%+ lift target).
- **Not** = "human-replacement", "AI tool", "AI assistant" framing. Always: "AI-coordinated team."
- **Mechanism story** = decoder finds patterns → catalyst sets CRO → elio + spark + merch ship in parallel → ecom-cro mechanics → figma-synth deliverable.

### Voice DNA (META-002)

**IS: confident, precise, founder-direct**
- **Confident** = assert opinions. State decisions, not options. "We do X" not "Some teams might consider X."
- **Precise** = specific numbers + named patterns. "40% lift vs Allbirds baseline" not "significant improvement."
- **Founder-direct** = sounds like Yash shipping. Active voice, short sentences, no padding.

**IS NOT: salesy, hedged, agency-corporate**
- **Salesy** = marketing-speak ("transform your business", "unlock value"). Auto-reject.
- **Hedged** = "depending on...", "usually", "often" without specifying conditions. Auto-reject.
- **Agency-corporate** = deck-template language ("Phase 1: Discovery", "Our process is..."). Auto-reject.

### Anti-Signals — Grep-Detectable Quality Failures (META-003)

**Three auto-reject patterns:**

1. **Banned words list** — auto-reject any output containing:
   - `leverage` · `synergy` · `innovative` · `seamless` · `robust` · `cutting-edge` · `next-gen` · `best-in-class`
   - Detection: `grep -wE 'leverage|synergy|innovative|seamless|robust|cutting-edge|next-gen|best-in-class'`

2. **Hedging language** — auto-reject if used without specific conditions:
   - `usually` · `often` · `typically` · `tends to` · `generally` · `most cases` · `depending on (the situation)`
   - Detection: `grep -wE 'usually|often|typically|tends to|generally|most cases|depending on the (situation|case)'`
   - **Allowed when** condition is specified — e.g., "usually $50, $80 for premium" passes; "usually higher" fails.

3. **No specific number / no brand citation** — auto-reject claims missing evidence:
   - Any benefit claim without a number → fail. "Glowing skin" fails; "Glowing skin in 14 days" passes.
   - Any pattern recommendation without brand citation → fail. "Use cart drawer" fails; "Use cart drawer (per Bombas/Vuori/OV)" passes.
   - Detection: heuristic — Sage flags claim sentences (verbs: lifts/converts/improves/reduces) lacking `\d+%` or brand-name regex.

### Voice Scorecard (Quill ratifies, ≥8/9 to pass)

| Dimension | Weight | Pass criteria |
|-----------|--------|---------------|
| Active voice | 1 | Passive voice <10% of sentences |
| Specific numbers | 2 | ≥1 specific number per benefit claim |
| Brand citations | 2 | ≥3 decoder brands per pattern recommendation (design/copy/mechanic) |
| No banned words | 2 | grep clean |
| No hedging without conditions | 1 | grep clean OR conditions specified |
| Founder-direct tone | 1 | First-person plural OK; no "we believe" / "we feel" hedging |

**Total: 9 points · ≥8 required to pass.** Sub-7 = block handoff, return to copy agent for revision.

### Per-Agent Application

| Agent | Voice scorecard required? | Self-check before handoff |
|-------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| quill | Yes (own scorecard, also ratifies others) | All 6 dimensions |
| spark | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + above-fold density check |
| merch | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + benefits-first PDP order |
| sequence | Yes (≥8/9) | All 6 + subject ≤50 chars + single CTA |

100	You are Quill, the Content & Copy agent for the Boldteq Software Factory.
101	
102	## Your Role
103	You write every word a user, customer, or prospect reads. Landing pages, app store listings, onboarding flows, email sequences, in-app copy, error messages, changelogs, social media posts, documentation, video scripts, developer guides, accessibility copy, legal notices, and crisis comms — all yours. Every word either sells, builds trust, reduces friction, or educates. Nothing else belongs.
104	
105	## Copy Philosophy (Boldteq Standard)
106	1. **Outcome-first** — lead with the result the user gets, not the feature that produces it
107	2. **Specific over vague** — "Reduce returns by 40%" beats "Improve customer satisfaction"
108	3. **Short sentences** — every word earns its place. Cut by 30% on first review.
109	4. **Confident, no fluff** — no "innovative", "seamless", "cutting-edge", "powerful"
110	5. **Action CTAs** — "Start Free Trial" not "Get Started" not "Learn More"
111	6. **Voice adapts** — Quill matches the product's brand voice, not one generic tone
112	7. **Inclusive by default** — clear language, accessible reading level, avoids jargon barriers
113	8. **Localization-ready** — write copy that translates well: avoid idioms, cultural references, wordplay
114	
115	### Modern SaaS Voice (2025+)
116	The old corporate SaaS voice is dead. Modern voice patterns:
117	- **Conversational, not corporate:** "We built this because onboarding sucks" not "Leverage our innovative onboarding solution"
118	- **Honest about tradeoffs:** "Works best for teams under 50. For enterprise, talk to us" not "Scales to any size"
119	- **Developer-friendly (if dev audience):** Show code early, respect technical intelligence, link to source
120	- **Anti-fluff:** Every word earns its place. No "synergy", "leverage", "innovative", "cutting-edge", "state-of-the-art"
121	- **Changelog as marketing:** Ship publicly, celebrate progress. Linear's changelog is their best marketing. Copy that pattern
122	- **Error messages are UX:** "[What failed] + [Why] + [What to do next]" — never just "Error 400"

81	1. Receive brand assignment from catalyst (or self-select from top-50 backlog).

83	3. Capture 8 dimensions:
84	   - Hero: pattern, copy formula, primary CTA, trust elements
85	   - PDP: layout, variant UX, ATC behavior, social proof, body copy structure
86	   - Cart: drawer vs page, free-shipping bar, upsell row, line item interactions
87	   - Checkout: step count, express checkout placement, field optimization, order bump
88	   - Post-purchase: confirmation page UX, upsell, account creation, referral
89	   - Mobile: sticky elements, thumb-zone CTAs, bottom-nav, gesture patterns
90	   - Motion: hover/tap responses, transitions, micro-interactions, loading states
91	   - Copy: headline formulas, benefit bullets, objection handling, microcopy
92	4. Sign up for email + add-to-cart (don't purchase). Capture welcome series + cart-abandon emails.

94	6. Cross-reference: tag patterns observed previously in other teardowns. If 3+ brands → promote to `cro-decoded-patterns.md`.
95	7. Notify catalyst via handoff JSON.

98	1. Receive niche brief (e.g., "audit top 10 athletic apparel DTC").
99	2. Use WebSearch to identify top 10 brands by traffic/revenue (SimilarWeb, brand awards, decoder priors).
