questions.question: ECOM-XCR-007 — Pre-purchase order bump position. Above payment vs above review?

options.label: Above payment (default — last point of decision); above review only when order summary already prominent on payment step (Recommended)
options.description: Above payment = decoder-canonical. Customer has committed (payment about to capture), order bump is final upsell moment. Above review = aggressive (commits seen the bump twice = pressure). Default above payment for most flows. Flip to above review only when payment step doesn't show order summary prominently (rare).

options.label: Above review (more aggressive position)
options.description: Maximum upsell visibility. Feels pushy to most customers.

options.label: Both positions (above payment + above review)
options.description: Repeat exposure = aggressive. Decoder bank shows lift erosion + complaint rise.

options.label: Brand decides per project
options.description: Inconsistent.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-008 — Bundle discount tiers formula?

options.label: Tiered: 2-pack 10% / 3-pack 15% / 5-pack 20% / 10-pack 25% (cap 25%); per-niche minor adjustments (Recommended)
options.description: Decoder-validated tier: 10% / 15% / 20% / 25% caps standard across CPG/supplements/apparel-commodity. Hard cap 25% — above erodes margin without commensurate volume lift. Per-niche minor flips: luxury caps lower (max 15%), high-AOV bundles cap lower (max 15%, drives volume by absolute dollars not percentage).

options.label: AOV-based scaling (% scales with cart total)
options.description: Maximum precision. Confuses customers + harder to communicate.

options.label: Flat 15% on all bundles
options.description: Simplest. Loses progressive incentive for larger packs.

options.label: Brand decides per bundle
options.description: Inconsistent across catalog.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-009 — Variant selector. Color out-of-stock. Display disabled or hidden?

options.label: Disabled (greyed swatch) with diagonal strikethrough overlay + 'Notify me when back' option (Recommended)
options.description: Disabled visual maintains color/size variant awareness (customer knows it exists, may wait). Diagonal strikethrough = decoder-canonical (Allbirds, Vuori). 'Notify me when back' = email capture for restock alerts (decoder pattern, Allbirds 5-12% recovery rate). Hidden loses awareness + email capture opportunity.

options.label: Hidden entirely (don't show out-of-stock variants)
options.description: Cleaner UI. Loses variant awareness + restock-notify lead capture.

options.label: Disabled without notify-me option
options.description: Maintains awareness. Loses email capture lead.

options.label: Disabled with red 'Sold out' banner overlay
options.description: Heavy emphasis. More attention-pulling than necessary.

questions.question: ECOM-XCR-010 — Subscription cancel flow compressed to 3 steps (vs 5 in skill file). Order?

options.label: Step 1: 'Why?' picker → Step 2: contextual save (pause / reduce frequency / discount) → Step 3: confirm cancel OR confirm save (Recommended)
options.description: 3-step compressed: (1) Reason picker (why cancelling) drives (2) save offer logic. 'Too much product' → reduce frequency. 'Don't need now' → pause 30/60/90 days (Athletic Greens 35% save rate). 'Too expensive' → discount next month. (3) Final confirm. Self-serve no email, no phone (legal CA+EU).

options.label: Pause → reduce frequency → confirm cancel (no reason picker)
options.description: Simpler. Loses contextual save (offers wrong remedy if reason mismatched).

options.label: Discount → pause → confirm cancel
options.description: Discount-first. Trains threaten-cancel-for-discount behavior (CAT-011 anti-pattern).

options.label: Single page with all save options
options.description: Maximum information density. Loses contextual targeting.

## Curriculum v1 — Session 7 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** XCR-001, XCR-002, XCR-005, XCR-009, XCR-011, XCR-012 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-7-changelog.md`

### Cart Drawer Back Button (XCR-001)
**Behavior:** Close drawer on browser back button (mobile + desktop consistent).

**State persistence:** drawer state stored in URL hash `#cart-open`. Forward navigation restores drawer. Back-then-forward = drawer reopens.

**Why:** matches modal/drawer convention. Users expect back to dismiss overlays. Decoder-canonical (Allbirds, Vuori, Bombas).

### Free-Ship Threshold — Raw vs Display (XCR-002)
**Storage:** raw AOV-derived value stored in mechanic logic + analytics.
**Display:** rounded to nearest $5 in UI.

**Example:**
- Median AOV $48 → raw threshold = 1.4 × 48 = $67.20
- Display: "$70 to free shipping"
- Logic fires when cart_subtotal >= 67.20

Decouples display rounding from logic precision. Enables AOV recompute without breaking displayed threshold.

### Cart-Abandon Min Cart Value (XCR-005)
**Min cart value to fire abandon recovery sequence:** 0.6 × median-niche-AOV.

| Niche | Median AOV | Min cart for abandon |
|-------|-----------|----------------------|
| Apparel | $50 | $30 |
| Supplements | $35 | $20 |
| Beauty | $30 | $18 |
| CPG | $20 | $12 |
| Home | $75 | $45 |

Below min = not worth recovery effort (low LTV + spam-filter risk + email volume cost). Per-project: pull actual median AOV, recompute min.

### Variant Stockout UX (XCR-009)
**Display pattern:** disabled greyed swatch + diagonal strikethrough overlay + "Notify me when back" CTA.

**Implementation:**
- Swatch background: 50% opacity neutral grey
- Diagonal strikethrough: SVG line top-left to bottom-right, color destructive
- Click → opens "Notify me when back" email capture modal
- Email capture → triggers restock alert sequence (sequence agent owns)

**Why:** maintains variant awareness (customer knows it exists, may wait) + captures email lead (5-12% restock-alert recovery rate per decoder bank).

NOT hidden (loses awareness + lead capture). NOT red 'Sold out' banner (over-emphasis).

### Shipping Method Default (XCR-011)
**Default:** preselect Standard (free if threshold met).

**Options stack:**
- Standard — Free (or $X if below threshold) [PRESELECTED]
- Express — +$9 (2-3 business days)
- Overnight — +$25 (next business day)

Force-pick adds friction without lifting upgrade rate (decoder bank: 80%+ pick Standard regardless). Express/Overnight opt-in via radio button click.

### Returning Customer Detection (XCR-012)
**Trigger:** after-submit on email field (single API call to customer-lookup endpoint).

**Implementation:**
1. User types email + tabs/clicks away (blur event)
2. Single API call: `GET /api/customer-lookup?email={hashed}`
3. If returning → show on shipping step: "Welcome back, {{firstName}}!" + pre-fill shipping address
4. If new → no message, proceed normally

**Cost calc:** real-time (per-keystroke) = ~50× more API calls. Worth only at 1M+ visitors/mo enterprise scale. Default = after-submit.
EOF

### Cart Upsell Row Fallback Chain (XCR-003)
**4-tier fallback when no related-by-tag products in stock:**

1. **related-by-tag** (default) — products tagged related to cart items
2. **bestsellers in same category** — top sellers from same product category as cart items
3. **'recently viewed'** — user's session history products (if any)
4. **HIDE ROW ENTIRELY** — when above 3 tiers exhausted

**NEVER:** show unrelated bestsellers from different categories. Random bestsellers feel spammy + destroy upsell relevance.

Example: cart has mattress → never show socks. Better to hide row.

### Post-Purchase Upsell — Complementary Only (XCR-006)
**Eligibility additions to existing rules:**
- Tag-related COMPLEMENT (socks with shoes, conditioner with shampoo)
- Same brand ecosystem (mattress topper after mattress, fitness band after watch)

**Forbidden:**
- Same-category replacement (different mattress after just-bought mattress)
- Same-purpose competitor product (different protein powder after just-bought)
- Unrelated random bestsellers

Decoder bank: complementary upsells convert 10-25% (decoder validated). Replacement upsells feel manipulative + drive returns.

### Order Bump Position (XCR-007)
**Default:** above payment step.

**Why:** customer has committed to purchase (entering payment), order bump = final upsell moment without feeling pushy. Decoder-canonical.

**Flip to above review** ONLY when:
- Payment step doesn't show order summary prominently
- Multi-step checkout where payment + review are separated by full-page transitions

NEVER both positions (repeat exposure feels aggressive, conversion erodes).

### Bundle Discount Tiers (XCR-008)
**Default tier formula:**

| Pack size | Discount % |
|-----------|-----------|
| 2-pack | 10% |
| 3-pack | 15% |
| 5-pack | 20% |
| 10-pack | 25% |
| Cap | 25% (above erodes margin) |

**Per-niche caps:**
- Luxury / premium: cap at 15% (preserves brand premium)
- High-AOV bundles (e.g., $300+ each): cap at 15% (drives volume by absolute dollars not %)
- Default (apparel/CPG/supplements/beauty commodity): full tier up to 25%

Display savings as both % AND $ ("Save 20% — $30 off").
EOF

### Subscription-Default-On Criterion (XCR-004)
**ALL 3 conditions required to enable subscription-default-on:**

1. **Cancel-flow save rate ≥30%** — pause/save converts ≥30% of cancel attempts (Athletic Greens benchmark)
2. **Monthly churn ≤8%** — sustainable retention math
3. **Pause option self-serve** — exists in account portal (legal CA + EU requirement)

**Below threshold:** default = one-time. Don't force subscription friction without retention math to support it.

**Brand opts in to subscription-default** via Polyglot dashboard after hitting all 3 metrics in retention dashboard. Catalyst can ratify per project.

### 3-Step Compressed Cancel Flow (XCR-010)
**Compressed from 5-step canonical to 3 steps:**

**Step 1 — Reason picker**
- "Why are you cancelling?" with options:
  - Too much product
  - Don't need it right now
  - Too expensive
  - Not the right fit
  - Other (free text)

**Step 2 — Contextual save (driven by reason)**
- "Too much product" → reduce frequency offer (every-2-months vs monthly)
- "Don't need now" → pause 30/60/90 days (Athletic Greens 35% save rate)
- "Too expensive" → discount on next month (capped 20%)
- "Not the right fit" → swap to similar product in catalog
- "Other" → discount + pause options together

**Step 3 — Confirm cancel OR confirm save**
- If user accepts save → "You're [paused / discounted / swapped]. See you in [time]."
- If user confirms cancel → "Cancelled. Final shipment [date]. Re-subscribe anytime."

**Self-serve mandatory** — no email required, no phone call (legal CA + EU).

**Compression decisions:**
- Original 5-step: pause / reduce / discount / swap / confirm
- 3-step pulls 4 save options into Step 2 (contextual targeting)
- Customer never sees offer that doesn't fit reason (less friction)
EOF

157	- ❌ Blame-y: "Your card failed." (cold + accusatory)

159	**Specificity is the trust-builder, not warmth-overload.** Always: WHAT failed + WHAT user can do next.

99	
100	**Source:** XCR-004, XCR-010 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-7-changelog.md`
101	
102	### Subscription-Default-On Criterion (XCR-004)
103	**ALL 3 conditions required to enable subscription-default-on:**
104	
105	1. **Cancel-flow save rate ≥30%** — pause/save converts ≥30% of cancel attempts (Athletic Greens benchmark)
106	2. **Monthly churn ≤8%** — sustainable retention math
107	3. **Pause option self-serve** — exists in account portal (legal CA + EU requirement)
108	
109	**Below threshold:** default = one-time. Don't force subscription friction without retention math to support it.
110	
111	**Brand opts in to subscription-default** via Polyglot dashboard after hitting all 3 metrics in retention dashboard. Catalyst can ratify per project.
112	
113	### 3-Step Compressed Cancel Flow (XCR-010)
114	**Compressed from 5-step canonical to 3 steps:**
115	
116	**Step 1 — Reason picker**
117	- "Why are you cancelling?" with options:
118	  - Too much product
119	  - Don't need it right now
120	  - Too expensive
121	  - Not the right fit
122	  - Other (free text)
123	
124	**Step 2 — Contextual save (driven by reason)**
125	- "Too much product" → reduce frequency offer (every-2-months vs monthly)
126	- "Don't need now" → pause 30/60/90 days (Athletic Greens 35% save rate)
127	- "Too expensive" → discount on next month (capped 20%)
128	- "Not the right fit" → swap to similar product in catalog
129	- "Other" → discount + pause options together
130	
131	**Step 3 — Confirm cancel OR confirm save**
132	- If user accepts save → "You're [paused / discounted / swapped]. See you in [time]."
133	- If user confirms cancel → "Cancelled. Final shipment [date]. Re-subscribe anytime."
134	
135	**Self-serve mandatory** — no email required, no phone call (legal CA + EU).
136	
137	**Compression decisions:**
138	- Original 5-step: pause / reduce / discount / swap / confirm
139	- 3-step pulls 4 save options into Step 2 (contextual targeting)
140	- Customer never sees offer that doesn't fit reason (less friction)

119	- Don't hide bundle savings — always display

133	
134	### Cart Upsell Row Fallback Chain (XCR-003)
135	**4-tier fallback when no related-by-tag products in stock:**
136	
137	1. **related-by-tag** (default) — products tagged related to cart items
138	2. **bestsellers in same category** — top sellers from same product category as cart items
139	3. **'recently viewed'** — user's session history products (if any)
140	4. **HIDE ROW ENTIRELY** — when above 3 tiers exhausted
141	
142	**NEVER:** show unrelated bestsellers from different categories. Random bestsellers feel spammy + destroy upsell relevance.
143	
144	Example: cart has mattress → never show socks. Better to hide row.
145	
146	### Post-Purchase Upsell — Complementary Only (XCR-006)
147	**Eligibility additions to existing rules:**
148	- Tag-related COMPLEMENT (socks with shoes, conditioner with shampoo)
149	- Same brand ecosystem (mattress topper after mattress, fitness band after watch)
150	
151	**Forbidden:**
152	- Same-category replacement (different mattress after just-bought mattress)
153	- Same-purpose competitor product (different protein powder after just-bought)
154	- Unrelated random bestsellers
155	
156	Decoder bank: complementary upsells convert 10-25% (decoder validated). Replacement upsells feel manipulative + drive returns.
157	
158	### Order Bump Position (XCR-007)
159	**Default:** above payment step.
160	
161	**Why:** customer has committed to purchase (entering payment), order bump = final upsell moment without feeling pushy. Decoder-canonical.
162	
163	**Flip to above review** ONLY when:
164	- Payment step doesn't show order summary prominently
165	- Multi-step checkout where payment + review are separated by full-page transitions
166	
167	NEVER both positions (repeat exposure feels aggressive, conversion erodes).

170	**Default tier formula:**
171	
172	| Pack size | Discount % |
173	|-----------|-----------|
174	| 2-pack | 10% |
175	| 3-pack | 15% |
176	| 5-pack | 20% |
177	| 10-pack | 25% |
178	| Cap | 25% (above erodes margin) |
179	
180	**Per-niche caps:**
181	- Luxury / premium: cap at 15% (preserves brand premium)
182	- High-AOV bundles (e.g., $300+ each): cap at 15% (drives volume by absolute dollars not %)
183	- Default (apparel/CPG/supplements/beauty commodity): full tier up to 25%
184	
185	Display savings as both % AND $ ("Save 20% — $30 off").

117	### Cart Drawer Back Button (XCR-001)
118	**Behavior:** Close drawer on browser back button (mobile + desktop consistent).
119	
120	**State persistence:** drawer state stored in URL hash `#cart-open`. Forward navigation restores drawer. Back-then-forward = drawer reopens.
121	
122	**Why:** matches modal/drawer convention. Users expect back to dismiss overlays. Decoder-canonical (Allbirds, Vuori, Bombas).
123	
124	### Free-Ship Threshold — Raw vs Display (XCR-002)
125	**Storage:** raw AOV-derived value stored in mechanic logic + analytics.
126	**Display:** rounded to nearest $5 in UI.
127	
128	**Example:**
129	- Median AOV $48 → raw threshold = 1.4 × 48 = $67.20
130	- Display: "$70 to free shipping"
131	- Logic fires when cart_subtotal >= 67.20
132	
133	Decouples display rounding from logic precision. Enables AOV recompute without breaking displayed threshold.
134	
135	### Cart-Abandon Min Cart Value (XCR-005)
136	**Min cart value to fire abandon recovery sequence:** 0.6 × median-niche-AOV.
137	
138	| Niche | Median AOV | Min cart for abandon |
139	|-------|-----------|----------------------|
140	| Apparel | $50 | $30 |
141	| Supplements | $35 | $20 |
142	| Beauty | $30 | $18 |
143	| CPG | $20 | $12 |
144	| Home | $75 | $45 |
145	
146	Below min = not worth recovery effort (low LTV + spam-filter risk + email volume cost). Per-project: pull actual median AOV, recompute min.
147	
148	### Variant Stockout UX (XCR-009)
149	**Display pattern:** disabled greyed swatch + diagonal strikethrough overlay + "Notify me when back" CTA.
150	
151	**Implementation:**
152	- Swatch background: 50% opacity neutral grey
153	- Diagonal strikethrough: SVG line top-left to bottom-right, color destructive
154	- Click → opens "Notify me when back" email capture modal
155	- Email capture → triggers restock alert sequence (sequence agent owns)
156	
157	**Why:** maintains variant awareness (customer knows it exists, may wait) + captures email lead (5-12% restock-alert recovery rate per decoder bank).
158	
159	NOT hidden (loses awareness + lead capture). NOT red 'Sold out' banner (over-emphasis).
160	
161	### Shipping Method Default (XCR-011)
162	**Default:** preselect Standard (free if threshold met).
163	
164	**Options stack:**
165	- Standard — Free (or $X if below threshold) [PRESELECTED]
166	- Express — +$9 (2-3 business days)
167	- Overnight — +$25 (next business day)
168	
169	Force-pick adds friction without lifting upgrade rate (decoder bank: 80%+ pick Standard regardless). Express/Overnight opt-in via radio button click.
170	
171	### Returning Customer Detection (XCR-012)
172	**Trigger:** after-submit on email field (single API call to customer-lookup endpoint).
173	
174	**Implementation:**
175	1. User types email + tabs/clicks away (blur event)
176	2. Single API call: `GET /api/customer-lookup?email={hashed}`
177	3. If returning → show on shipping step: "Welcome back, {{firstName}}!" + pre-fill shipping address
178	4. If new → no message, proceed normally
179	
180	**Cost calc:** real-time (per-keystroke) = ~50× more API calls. Worth only at 1M+ visitors/mo enterprise scale. Default = after-submit.

options.description: 15% hard cap = decoder-validated upper limit before training discount-waiting habit. **Stop after Day 120. No farewell email.**

### Pre-Renewal Timing — Frequency-Scaled (SEQ-004)
**Pre-renewal email timing scales with subscription frequency:**

| Subscription frequency | Pre-renewal lead time |
|------------------------|----------------------|
| Monthly | 3 days before charge |
| Bimonthly | 5 days before charge |
| Quarterly | 7 days before charge |
| Yearly | 14 days before charge |

**Why scale:**
- 3d before monthly = ~10% of cycle (proportional decision window)
- 3d before quarterly = 3% of cycle (TOO LATE for skip decision)
- 3d before yearly = 0.8% of cycle (almost useless)
- 14d before yearly = 4% of cycle (proportional)

**Athletic Greens uses 5d for monthly** (slightly conservative). 7d for quarterly = decoder-canonical.

### Cross-Sequence Priority — Post-Purchase Wins (SEQ-008)
**Rule:** Post-purchase nurture > cart-abandon recovery. Active customer relationship beats abandoned consideration.

**Collision handling:**
1. User triggers post-purchase WHILE cart-abandon mid-sequence
2. **PAUSE cart-abandon** (don't cancel — cart may still be active)
3. Run post-purchase nurture to completion (60-day cadence)
4. After post-purchase ends, **CHECK cart status:**
   - If cart cleared / purchased → terminate cart-abandon
   - If cart still active after 7d delay → resume cart-abandon at next email step
5. Document state transitions in `email-sequence-state` table

**Decoder bank:** Allbirds/Bombas use pause-and-resume pattern. Parallel sequences = email volume + timing collisions = unsubscribe risk.

**Other priority rules:**
| Conflict | Winner |
|----------|--------|
| Welcome series + cart-abandon | Welcome wins (new customer trust > recovery) |
| Win-back + browse-abandon | Browse-abandon wins (active intent signal) |
| Subscription pre-renewal + post-purchase | Pre-renewal wins (commitment moment) |
| Subscription cancel-save + win-back | Cancel-save wins (active retention moment) |

**Universal rule:** active commitment > consideration > re-engagement.
EOF

62	### 1. Hero pattern
63	- **Type:** Split hero (product image right, copy + trust left) with lifestyle/celebrity layer
64	- **Headline (homepage):** "Better Mornings, No Matter Hugh You Are." (Hugh Jackman partnership)
65	- **Headline (campaign page):** "Just 1 scoop of the best greens powder, the highest quality ingredients to fill your nutrient gaps."
66	- **Subhead:** "75 ingredients to replace your multivitamin, pre- and probiotics, immune support, adaptogens, super greens, and so much more."
67	- **Primary CTA:** "Get My Welcome Kit" / "Get Started"
68	- **Secondary CTA:** "Learn More"
69	- **Trust elements above fold:** "50,000+ verified 5-star reviews" · NSF Certified for Sport® badge · "90-Day Money Back Guarantee"
70	- **Above-fold density:** High — 4 trust signals before scroll
71	- **Notable:** NSF Certified for Sport badge placed inline with star count and guarantee, not relegated to footer. This above-fold cert placement is deliberate — targets athlete/biohacker ICP where sport certification = safety shorthand.
72	
73	### 2. PDP layout
74	- **Subscribe vs one-time:** Subscription default. $79/month subscription vs $99 one-time. ~20% savings. Framing: "Build a healthy daily habit" + "Update or cancel anytime."
75	- **Lock-in psychology:** Welcome Kit (free gifts) only available on first subscription order — creates asymmetric value that makes one-time feel like leaving money on the table.
76	- **Body copy structure:** Nutrient gaps claim → 75 ingredients count → clinical backing → 3-step "how it works" → celebrity/expert quotes → cost comparison vs buying separately ($79 vs $225) → reviews → guarantee
77	- **Social proof placement:** Above ATC (review count + NSF cert)
78	- **Trust stack order (full):**
79	  1. Customer reviews — "50,000+ verified 5-star reviews"
80	  2. Third-party cert — NSF Certified for Sport®
81	  3. Research backing — "industry-leading research" / 4x randomized placebo-controlled trials
82	  4. Expert/athlete trust — "Trusted by leading scientists and athletes"
83	  5. Celebrity endorsement — Hugh Jackman, Dr. Andrew Huberman, Lewis Hamilton, Allyson Felix
84	  6. Press logos — Forbes, Vogue, Bon Appétit
85	- **Specific copy formula:** "75 ingredients. 1 scoop. Done." — count + consolidation + closure. Objection to complexity answered before it's asked.

108	- **Headline pattern:** [Celebrity name] + outcome + identity hook. "Better Mornings, No Matter Hugh You Are." Formula: celebrity + universal outcome + name-pun inclusion
109	- **Ingredient count formula:** "75 ingredients" used as a compression argument — more ingredients signals completeness, not complexity
110	- **Cost compression formula:** "$79/month vs. $225 if bought separately" — anchors against stack price, not against nothing
111	- **Guarantee formula:** "Try AG1 for 90 days. If you don't love it, full refund. No questions asked."
112	- **Microcopy — cancel:** "Update or cancel anytime" — self-serve framing removes subscription anxiety
113	- **Voice:** Clinical confidence + athlete performance + daily ritual. Never cute, never aggressive.

116	**Archetype: Split hero (lifestyle/celebrity layer)**
117	**Why it fits supplements:** The split layout lets AG1 place the physical product (tactile, real) beside copy that sells the transformation. The celebrity layer adds aspirational identity projection. Works for premium supplements where the customer is buying the identity ("I take what Andrew Huberman takes") as much as the product.

120	"1 scoop. 75 ingredients. Done." — **Pattern: count + consolidation + closure.** Compresses a complex stack into a single daily action. The number proves completeness; "Done" signals ritual simplicity.

- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js`
- **Lines**: 239, 276, 282, 324
- **Category**: 3 (Missing rate limit middleware)
- **Severity**: CRITICAL
- **Risk**: Endpoints `POST /orchestrations`, `DELETE /orchestrations/runs/:id`, `DELETE /orchestrations/runs`, `DELETE /orchestrations/:id` lack rateLimit middleware; attackers can spam, DOS, or cascade-delete all run history.
- **Suggested Fix**: Wrap all write/delete endpoints with `rateLimit('write')` middleware.

**2. Memory & Rules Folder Operations — No Rate Limit**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/memory.js`
- **Lines**: 174 (POST), 284 (POST), 299 (DELETE), 316 (POST)
- **Category**: 3 (Missing rate limit)
- **Severity**: CRITICAL
- **Risk**: `POST /memory/file`, `POST /memory/folder`, `DELETE /memory/folder`, `POST /memory/move` lack rate limiting; can fill disk, delete entire memory tree, or trigger DoS via rapid folder creation.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `rateLimit('write')` to all four endpoints.

**3. Rules Endpoints Missing Rate Limit**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/rules.js`
- **Lines**: 167, 215, 235, 253 (POST endpoints only)
- **Category**: 3 (Missing rate limit)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `POST /global/rules/from-template`, `POST /projects/:id/rules/from-template`, `POST /projects/:id/init-rules`, `POST /init-rules` unprotected; can spam template creation or re-initialize rules repeatedly.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `rateLimit('write')` to all four endpoints.

**4. Config Write Endpoints Lack Rate Limiting**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/config.js`
- **Lines**: 29, 45, 63
- **Category**: 3 (Missing rate limit)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `POST /config/project-dirs`, `PUT /global/claude-md`, `PUT /global/settings` can be spammed, overwriting config and settings repeatedly without throttle.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `rateLimit('write')` to all three endpoints.

**5. AI History Endpoints Missing Rate Limit**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/ai.js`
- **Lines**: 80, 99
- **Category**: 3 (Missing rate limit)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `POST /ai/history` and `DELETE /ai/history/:id` unprotected; attackers can spam-create chat sessions or bulk-delete history.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `rateLimit('write')` to both endpoints.

**6. Race Condition: Conversation Read-Modify-Write**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/projects.js`
- **Lines**: 156–164
- **Category**: 5 (Race condition in file I/O)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `POST /projects/:projectId/conversations/:id/send` loads conversation list, appends message, saves; if two requests arrive simultaneously, one message is lost (lost update).
- **Suggested Fix**: Use atomic file lock or database transaction for load-modify-save.

**7. Approval Resolver Race Condition**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js`
- **Lines**: 293–314
- **Category**: 5 (Race condition)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: Two simultaneous approve/reject requests on same key can both delete from map, resolve twice, or cause orphaned timers; in-memory Map not thread-safe.
- **Suggested Fix**: Guard with a Set of processing keys or move to DB transaction.

**8. SQLite Table Name Injection in dbExplorer**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/dbExplorer.js`
- **Lines**: 16, 39, 40
- **Category**: 2 (SQL injection risk)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: Line 16 uses unparameterized table name in SELECT; line 40 quotes table name but still vulnerable if name contains quotes. Line 33 sanitizes but doesn't validate against whitelist.
- **Suggested Fix**: Whitelist table names against `sqlite_master` before use; never interpolate user input into SQL.

- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/projects.js`
- **Line**: 602
- **Category**: 6 (Unhandled process.exit)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `run().catch(err => { console.error(err.message); process.exit(1); })` will kill entire server if called from an endpoint (synchronous context exit during setup); should reject promise or emit event instead.
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace `process.exit()` with graceful error handling; log and return from function.

**10. Missing Input Validation: Orchestration Nodes**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js`
- **Line**: 240–242
- **Category**: 1 (Missing input validation)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: Only validates nodes/edges are arrays; doesn't validate node.id, node.type, edge.source/target exist or are valid; malformed graph can crash execution engine.
- **Suggested Fix**: Validate node and edge objects have required fields; check agentName exists in registry.

**11. Hardcoded PATH: process.env.CLAUDE_PATH**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js`
- **Line**: 54
- **Category**: 7 (Hardcoded paths)
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Risk**: `process.env.CLAUDE_PATH || 'claude'` falls back to shell PATH if env not set; spawns arbitrary `claude` binary; vulnerable if PATH is hijacked.
- **Suggested Fix**: Require CLAUDE_PATH to be set explicitly or error; validate path exists and is owned by current user.

**12. No Atomic Registry.json Updates**
- **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/dispatch.js`
- **Lines**: 10–17
- **Category**: 5 (Race condition: file read-modify-write)

### CRON JOBS & FAILURE MODES

Defined in `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/server.js` (lines 142–170):

- **02:00 UTC** — HR Roster nightly recompute: No retry; if fails, next run is 24h later. Agents remain unranked.
- **03:00 UTC** — Witness sweep: Errors logged but not persisted; if process crashes, day's run classification is lost.

All `atomicWriteText()` and `atomicWriteJson()` calls use the pattern correctly (from `lib/atomicIo.js`). However:

# Phase 3 — Polyglot Production Hardening (Audit + Fix Sweep)

**Date added:** 2026-04-27 (late evening)
**Owner:** rex
**Scope confirmed by Yash:** CRITICAL + HIGH severity issues (~24 fixes) · reusable `apiError()` helper for silent catches

## Context — why this sweep

Yash requested deep page audit + production-grade fix sweep. 3 parallel Explore agents audited 34 pages + 22 backend routes. Findings:

**Frontend status:** TypeScript strict mode passes with 0 errors. Curriculum-driven Phase 2 patches all on disk. NO critical data-flow bugs (refetch + mutation invalidation patterns mostly correct).

**Frontend issues (HIGH):** 11 silent `catch {}` blocks across pages (AiAssistant, Webhooks, Playground, Memory, ProjectChat, RunHistory, GoalCascade, OrgChart, Schedules) swallow API failures → users unaware of stale data. CommandPalette setTimeout has stale-closure risk on focus. Toast component lacks unmount cleanup for in-flight timers.

**Backend issues (CRITICAL):** 18 write/delete endpoints across orchestrations.js, memory.js, rules.js, config.js, ai.js have NO `rateLimit('write')` middleware → DoS + spam risk. 3 race conditions: conversation save (projects.js), approval resolver (orchestrations.js), registry.json read (dispatch.js). SQL-injection-vector in dbExplorer.js (table name not whitelist-validated). process.exit() inside route handler in projects.js will kill server if triggered.

## Approach

Fix in 2 phases this session:
1. **Backend security hardening first** (lower risk to running app, single-file scope per fix)
2. **Frontend silent-catch sweep** via reusable helper (single new utility, then 11 call-site swaps)

No medium-severity work (index-keys, inline styles, a11y) — deferred to next session.

## Deliverable A — Backend security (CRITICAL)

### A1 — Rate-limit 18 unprotected write endpoints
Add `rateLimit('write')` middleware before each handler. Existing pattern from rateLimit middleware in `src/middleware/`. Files + line numbers:

| File | Endpoints |
|------|-----------|
| `src/routes/orchestrations.js` | POST `/orchestrations` (239), DELETE `/runs/:id` (276), DELETE `/runs` (282), DELETE `/:id` (324) |
| `src/routes/memory.js` | POST `/memory/file` (174), DELETE `/memory/file` (194), POST `/memory/folder` (284), DELETE `/memory/folder` (299), POST `/memory/move` (316) |
| `src/routes/rules.js` | POST `/global/rules/from-template` (167), POST `/projects/:id/rules/from-template` (215), POST `/projects/:id/init-rules` (235), POST `/init-rules` (253) |
| `src/routes/config.js` | POST `/config/project-dirs` (29), PUT `/global/claude-md` (45), PUT `/global/settings` (63) |
| `src/routes/ai.js` | POST `/ai/history` (80), DELETE `/ai/history/:id` (99) |

### A2 — Race condition fixes
- `src/routes/projects.js:156-164` — conversation save uses load→append→write; wrap in atomic-write or in-process Map-based mutex per conversation_id.
- `src/routes/orchestrations.js:293-314` — approval resolver Map check-and-delete needs guard against double-resolve. Use `Map.delete()` atomic pattern (delete returns bool; only resolve if true).
- `src/routes/dispatch.js:10-17` — registry.json `require(REGISTRY_PATH)` cached by Node module system. Replace with `fs.readFileSync(REGISTRY_PATH, 'utf-8')` + `JSON.parse()` to read fresh on every dispatch.

### A3 — SQL injection guard in dbExplorer
- `src/routes/dbExplorer.js:16,40` — table name string-interpolated into SQL. Add whitelist validation: query `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'` once, cache, reject any incoming table name not in cache. Existing `db.js` exports prepared statements — extend with `getAllowedTables()`.

### A4 — Remove process.exit from request handler
- `src/routes/projects.js:602` — `run().catch(err => { console.error(err.message); process.exit(1) })` inside endpoint handler. Replace with logging + return 500 error response. Server stays alive.

## Deliverable B — Frontend silent-error helper (HIGH)

### B1 — Add `apiError()` utility
File: `client/src/lib/api.ts` — append helper:

```typescript
import { toast } from '../components/Toast'

/**
 * Standard error handler for catch blocks in API call chains.
 * Logs full error to console + shows user-facing toast.
 * Use: getThing().catch(err => apiError('Load failed', err))
 */
export function apiError(label: string, err: unknown): void {
  console.error(`[api] ${label}:`, err)
  const detail = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
  toast('error', `${label}${detail && detail !== '[object Object]' ? `: ${detail.slice(0, 80)}` : ''}`)
}
```

| `client/src/pages/AiAssistant.tsx` | 281 | `catch {}` | `catch (e) { apiError('Stream error', e) }` |
| `client/src/pages/AiAssistant.tsx` | 414 | `catch {}` | `catch (e) { apiError('Save chat', e) }` |
| `client/src/pages/Webhooks.tsx` | 52 | `catch {}` | `catch (e) { apiError('Delete webhook', e) }` |
| `client/src/pages/Webhooks.tsx` | 63 | `catch {}` | `catch (e) { apiError('Get webhook secret', e) }` |
| `client/src/pages/Memory.tsx` | 847 | `catch {}` | `catch (e) { apiError('Search memory', e) }` |
| `client/src/pages/ProjectChat.tsx` | 42, 50, 58 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Load conversations', err))` |
| `client/src/pages/Playground.tsx` | 234, 525, 532 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Playground history', err))` |
| `client/src/pages/RunHistory.tsx` | 63 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Load runs', err))` |
| `client/src/pages/GoalCascade.tsx` | 46 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Load goals', err))` |
| `client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx` | 1853 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Sync org chart', err))` |
| `client/src/pages/Schedules.tsx` | 38 | `.catch(() => {})` | `.catch(err => apiError('Load schedules', err))` |

### B3 — CommandPalette stale-closure fix
`client/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx:135` — wrap setTimeout in proper cleanup + capture inputRef.current at effect-time.

### B4 — Toast unmount-safety
`client/src/components/Toast.tsx:26` — store timeoutId in component-scope ref, clear in cleanup return.

## File deliverables summary

| Files modified | Count |
|----------------|-------|
| Backend route files | 5 (orchestrations, memory, rules, config, ai) |
| Backend lib files | 3 (projects, dispatch, dbExplorer) |
| Frontend lib | 1 (`api.ts` — add `apiError`) |
| Frontend pages | 8 (AiAssistant, Webhooks, Memory, ProjectChat, Playground, RunHistory, GoalCascade, OrgChart, Schedules — 9 pages, 11 catch blocks) |
| Frontend components | 2 (CommandPalette, Toast) |
| **Total files** | **~17** |

## Sequence

1. Backend A1 (rate-limit additions) — 5 file edits, low risk
2. Backend A2 (race conditions) — 3 file edits, careful logic changes
3. Backend A3 (SQL injection guard) — 1 file edit + lib helper
4. Backend A4 (process.exit removal) — 1 line change
5. Frontend B1 (`apiError` helper) — 1 lib addition
6. Frontend B2 (11 catch swaps) — batch sed-like edits across 9 files
7. Frontend B3-B4 (CommandPalette + Toast cleanup)
8. Build client + restart server + smoke-test pages

## Verification

1. **Backend rate limits live:** `curl` 100 rapid POSTs → 429 after threshold (per existing rateLimit('write') config)
2. **Race condition:** rapid-fire conversation send to same conversation_id → all messages appear (none lost)
3. **dbExplorer SQL safety:** request `?table=users; DROP TABLE agents;` → 400 rejected
4. **process.exit removed:** trigger error path in projects.js endpoint → server stays up, returns 500
5. **Frontend errors visible:** disconnect API → refresh AiAssistant → red toast appears
6. **CommandPalette focus:** open palette → close → reopen → focus lands on input (no stale-ref crash)
7. **Toast cleanup:** rapid-toast spam + unmount → no orphan timers (Memory tab profiler clean)

## Risks + mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Rate limit too tight breaks legit batch saves | Use existing `rateLimit('write')` config (already tuned) — no new threshold |
| Race-condition fix introduces deadlock | Use Map-based per-key locks (no nested locks); existing pattern in `src/lib/locks.js` if exists |
| dbExplorer whitelist breaks legitimate queries | Cache table list refreshed on schema migration; admin tool is read-only |
| `apiError()` toast spam if backend down | Toast component already debounces duplicate messages |
| Server restart drops in-flight HTTP requests | Restart during low-traffic moment (Yash pause action) |

- [src/middleware/](Polyglot/src/middleware/) — existing rateLimit middleware
- [src/lib/atomicIo.js](Polyglot/src/lib/atomicIo.js) — atomic-write pattern
- [client/src/components/Toast.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/components/Toast.tsx) — toast helper

## Context — why this sweep

**Frontend status:** TypeScript strict mode passes with 0 errors. Curriculum-driven Phase 2 patches all on disk. NO critical data-flow bugs (refetch + mutation invalidation patterns mostly correct).

### A2 — Race condition fixes
- `src/routes/projects.js:156-164` — conversation save uses load→append→write; wrap in atomic-write or in-process Map-based mutex per conversation_id.
- `src/routes/orchestrations.js:293-314` — approval resolver Map check-and-delete needs guard against double-resolve. Use `Map.delete()` atomic pattern (delete returns bool; only resolve if true).
- `src/routes/dispatch.js:10-17` — registry.json `require(REGISTRY_PATH)` cached by Node module system. Replace with `fs.readFileSync(REGISTRY_PATH, 'utf-8')` + `JSON.parse()` to read fresh on every dispatch.

### A3 — SQL injection guard in dbExplorer
- `src/routes/dbExplorer.js:16,40` — table name string-interpolated into SQL. Add whitelist validation: query `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'` once, cache, reject any incoming table name not in cache. Existing `db.js` exports prepared statements — extend with `getAllowedTables()`.

### A4 — Remove process.exit from request handler
- `src/routes/projects.js:602` — `run().catch(err => { console.error(err.message); process.exit(1) })` inside endpoint handler. Replace with logging + return 500 error response. Server stays alive.

### B1 — Add `apiError()` utility
File: `client/src/lib/api.ts` — append helper:

```typescript
import { toast } from '../components/Toast'

/**
 * Standard error handler for catch blocks in API call chains.
 * Logs full error to console + shows user-facing toast.
 * Use: getThing().catch(err => apiError('Load failed', err))
 */
export function apiError(label: string, err: unknown): void {
  console.error(`[api] ${label}:`, err)
  const detail = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
  toast('error', `${label}${detail && detail !== '[object Object]' ? `: ${detail.slice(0, 80)}` : ''}`)
}
```

// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [

import { toast } from '../components/Toast'

/**
 * Standard error handler for catch blocks in API call chains.
 * Logs full error to console + shows user-facing toast.

export function apiError(label: string, err: unknown): void {
  console.error(`[api] ${label}:`, err)
  const detail = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
  toast('error', `${label}${detail && detail !== '[object Object]' ? `: ${detail.slice(0, 80)}` : ''}`)
}

|------|-----------|

interface EcomHandoff {

  from: AgentId

## Deliverable F — Training-Readiness Gate

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/dispatch/readiness/:agentId` (new in `Polyglot/src/routes/dispatch.js`)

**Logic:**
```javascript
// Compute readiness from Supabase agent_runs (last 14 days)
const composite = await getCompositeScore(agentId)
const trainingPatchesApplied = await countAppliedPatches(agentId)
const ready = composite >= 7.0 && trainingPatchesApplied >= 5
return {
  ready,
  composite_score: composite,
  patches_applied: trainingPatchesApplied,
  blockers: ready ? [] : [
    composite < 7.0 ? `composite_score ${composite.toFixed(1)} < 7.0 threshold` : null,
    trainingPatchesApplied < 5 ? `only ${trainingPatchesApplied}/5 minimum patches applied` : null,
  ].filter(Boolean),
  threshold: { composite: 7.0, patches: 5 },
}
```

**Pipeline check:** orchestrations.js calls readiness before each node. Non-ready node:

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { Globe, Plus, Trash2, Copy, Eye, EyeOff, AlertCircle, Check } from 'lucide-react'
import { getWebhooks, getWebhookSecret, createWebhook, deleteWebhook, getGlobalAgents } from '../lib/api'
import type { Webhook } from '../lib/api'
import type { Agent } from '../types'

function timeAgo(ts: string | null): string {
  if (!ts) return 'never'
  const diff = Date.now() - new Date(ts).getTime()
  if (diff < 60000) return 'just now'
  if (diff < 3600000) return `${Math.floor(diff / 60000)}m ago`
  if (diff < 86400000) return `${Math.floor(diff / 3600000)}h ago`
  return `${Math.floor(diff / 86400000)}d ago`
}

    api_import_pattern = re.compile(r"import\s*\{([^}]+)\}\s*from\s*'(\.\.\/(?:\.\.\/)?lib\/api)'")
    m = api_import_pattern.search(content)

import { toast } from '../components/Toast'

/**
 * Standard error handler for catch blocks in API call chains.
 * Logs full error to console + shows user-facing toast.
 * Use: getThing().catch(err => apiError('Load failed', err))

export function apiError(label: string, err: unknown): void {

## Context — why Phase 2

Phase 1 hired 9 agents, scaffolded KB, wired Polyglot org-v2. Agents now exist but are GENERIC — they have skill files seeded from competitive research, none of Yash's specific brand voice / niche priorities / lift-target calibration. Without this knowledge, the team produces "good ecom" not "Boldteq-grade ecom." Two gaps:

1. **No tacit knowledge transfer mechanism.** Tutor patches are signal-driven (Yash corrections, Witness antipatterns) — there's no proactive curriculum extraction.
2. **No production coordination.** Handoff contracts are text-based markdown in `.handoffs/`. Polyglot orchestrations.js has 5 pipeline templates but no ecom-team pipeline. Dispatch is skill-based only — ignores `composite_score`, no training-readiness gate. 9 agents would dispatch in parallel with no acceptance criteria between phases.

Yash decisions confirmed 2026-04-27:
- **Q delivery:** Chat batches, 10–15 questions per session (~7-8 sessions over 2-3 weeks)
- **Coordination scope:** Full — handoff JSON schema + Polyglot pipeline + training-readiness gate
- **Training pipe:** Canonical Mira → Tutor patches (P3 priority, rollback_content, 48h impact, auto-rollback)

302

308	2. Auto-play hero video with sound (instant bounce)
309	3. Fake stock scarcity ('Limited stock', 'Selling fast', vague urgency without verified count ≤5)

311	5. Marketing-soft scarcity in any form (trains discount-waiting + erodes trust)

### PDP Hero Default — Mobile-First Stack (ELI-001)
Gallery TOP, info BELOW on ALL devices. No split layout default. Single design system.

### Variant Density Per-Axis Tiers (ELI-002)
≤8 swatches grid / 9-20 hybrid / >20 dropdown. Per axis, not combo total.

### Stock Urgency Anti-Pattern (ELI-003)
NEVER fake scarcity. Show specific count ONLY when verified inventory ≤5. Above 5 = hide indicator. No vague text ('Limited stock', 'Selling fast', 'restock soon').

### Trust Trio Niche-Tier (ELI-004)
ABOVE ATC for skeptical (supplements/wellness/luxury). BELOW ATC for default (apparel/beauty/CPG/home).

### Reviews — Most-Helpful Default (ELI-005)
Most-helpful default + 'most recent' secondary tab + 'photo only' filter. Three options max.

### Cross-Sell AOV-Tier (ELI-006)
Bottom for <$50 commodity. Mid-scroll for >$100 considered purchase. $50-100 → bottom default.

### Image Count Price-Tier (ELI-007)
4-6 (<$40) / 6-10 ($40-150) / 10-15 (>$150).

Single static lifestyle hero default. NEVER carousel (slides 2+ near-zero engagement). Video bg ONLY luxury/sleep/beauty editorial.

Overlay top-left, 40% scrim for WCAG AA contrast. Mobile-first.

Order details FIRST → upsell SECOND (30-min one-click window) → account/referral THIRD.

### Stack Default (ELI-012)
Hydrogen + RR7 (Stack B storefront mode) default. Liquid ONLY for: budget <$5K + theme exists, theme app extensions required, or merchant insists.

1. Carousel hero with auto-advance (slides 2+ get near-zero engagement)
2. Auto-play hero video with sound (instant bounce)

When you need a new token but token agent hasn't created it:

Don't block parallel work on token-creation. Don't keep inline values forever (max 30 days before escalation).

20	- Capture screenshots from a live storybook URL if project has Storybook running
21	- Or render mentally + use static screenshot for visual reference
22	
23	### Stage 3: Token mapping
24	- Pull Token's variable map (`tokens.css` + Tailwind config)
25	- For each Tailwind class on the component, map to Figma variable
26	- Example: `bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-md` → Figma fill: `color/primary/default`, text color: `color/primary-foreground/default`, corner-radius: `radius/md`
27	
28	### Stage 4: Build Figma component spec JSON
29	```json
30	{
31	  "name": "ProductCard",
32	  "type": "COMPONENT_SET",
33	  "variants": [
34	    {
35	      "props": {"variant": "default"},
36	      "fillId": "color/surface",
37	      "borderId": "color/border",
38	      "radiusId": "radius/lg"
39	    },
40	    {
41	      "props": {"variant": "sale"},
42	      "fillId": "color/surface",
43	      "badgeFillId": "color/destructive",
44	      "borderId": "color/border"
45	    }
46	  ],
47	  "propsPanel": [
48	    {"name": "title", "type": "TEXT"},
49	    {"name": "price", "type": "TEXT"},
50	    {"name": "image", "type": "INSTANCE_SWAP"},
51	    {"name": "variant", "type": "VARIANT", "options": ["default", "sale", "sold-out"]}
52	  ]
53	}
54	```
55	
56	### Stage 5: Upload via Figma MCP
57	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_new_file` if no project Figma file exists
58	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__upload_assets` for any imagery referenced
59	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__use_figma` to write component to file
60	
61	### Stage 6: Verify
62	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_design_context` on the new component
63	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_screenshot` for visual verification
64	- Compare against codebase render — flag drift
65	
66	## Edge cases
67	- Generic types (e.g., `<Button<T>>`) — fall back to heuristic parse, flag for manual review
68	- Conditional rendering (`{loading && <Spinner/>}`) — represent as variant
69	- Composition (e.g., `<Card><CardHeader/></Card>`) — represent as instance + slots
70	
71	## Output deliverable
72	- One Figma component per JSX component
73	- Variant matrix complete
74	- Token-mapped (no hardcoded hex)
75	- Asset uploads complete
76	
77	## Coordination
78	- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
79	- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
80	- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Curriculum v1 — Session 5 Patches (2026-04-27)
85	
86	**Source:** FIG-001, FIG-006, FIG-007, FIG-008 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-5-changelog.md`
87	
88	### Generic Type Heuristic Fallback (FIG-001)
89	For `<Button<T>>` / `<List<T>>` generic components:
90	1. Parse codebase usage sites for concrete T instances
91	2. Extract top 3 concrete types (e.g., `Button<string>`, `Button<User>`, `Button<Product>`)
92	3. Generate Figma variants for each concrete type
93	4. Tag component `generic-component-needs-review` in next weekly sync
94	5. Vega manually reviews flagged components, decides if generic or concrete-only mapping
95	
96	Don't block pipeline; preserves dev velocity. Manual review catches edge cases.
97	
98	### Token Drift — Block Upload (FIG-006)
99	When `tokens.css` drifted from Figma vars at upload time:
100	1. Block upload, return error to dispatcher
101	2. Dispatch token agent for emergency sync (4h SLA priority)
102	3. Token agent runs code→Figma push
103	4. After sync completes, figma-synth auto-retries upload
104	5. If sync times out (4h+), escalate to vega + flag deliverable as `pending-token-sync`
105	
106	NEVER ship with stale tokens. NEVER fall back to inline hex (violates token-system anti-pattern).
107	
108	### Variant Explosion Split (FIG-007)
109	Threshold: 30 variants per component-set (well below Figma 50-variant perf cliff).
110	
111	**Split axis priority:**
112	1. **STATE** (default/hover/active/disabled) — splits cleanest for stateful components
113	2. **SIZE** (sm/md/lg/xl) — only if state-axis split insufficient
114	3. **VARIANT** (primary/secondary/destructive) — last resort
115	
116	Example: ProductCard with 4 variants × 3 sizes × 2 states = 24 variants. Split into 3 component-sets:
117	- ProductCardDefault (4 var × 3 size = 12)
118	- ProductCardHover (4 var × 3 size = 12)
119	- ProductCardSoldOut (4 var × 3 size = 12)
120	
121	Each component-set <30 variants. Designers swap between sets via instance swap.
122

124	When project lacks Storybook:
125	1. Auto-generate temp setup: `npx storybook init` + scaffold stories from JSX components
126	2. Use temp Storybook for figma-synth render captures
127	3. Log entry in `~/.claude/memory/projects/[project]/tech-debt.md` for project to formalize properly
128	4. Doesn't block deliverable — figma-synth ships using temp Storybook

# Polaris ↔ Storefront Token Bridge

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Stack B challenge — Shopify admin uses Polaris design system; storefront uses custom tokens. Brand must feel unified.

## The problem

Stack B apps embed in Shopify admin (Polaris-styled) AND ship a storefront the merchant's customers see (custom-styled). Two different design systems, same brand expectation.

Without a bridge: admin uses Polaris navy + Inter; storefront uses brand purple + Manrope. Merchants notice immediately.

## Mapping table (categories)

### Color
| Polaris token | Storefront token | Mapping rule |
|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
| `--p-color-bg-surface` | `--color-background` | Direct map (light/dark mode aware) |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` | `--color-primary` | Brand color overrides Polaris default |
| `--p-color-text` | `--color-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-text-secondary` | `--color-muted-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-border` | `--color-border` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-critical` | `--color-destructive` | Direct map |

### Typography
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-text-heading-2xl` | `text-4xl` | Semantic equivalent |
| `--p-text-heading-xl` | `text-3xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-lg` | `text-2xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-md` | `text-xl` | |
| `--p-text-body-md` | `text-base` | |
| `--p-text-body-sm` | `text-sm` | |
| `--p-font-family-sans` | `font-sans` | Brand font preferred over Polaris default |

### Spacing
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-space-100` | `space-1` (4px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-200` | `space-2` (8px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-300` | `space-3` (12px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-400` | `space-4` (16px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-500` | `space-5` (20px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-600` | `space-6` (24px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-800` | `space-8` (32px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-1200` | `space-12` (48px) | Direct |

### Motion
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-motion-duration-100` | `--duration-instant` (100ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-200` | `--duration-fast` (200ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-300` | `--duration-base` (300ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-500` | `--duration-slow` (500ms) | Direct |

## Gaps + decisions

### Polaris-only (no storefront equivalent)
- `--p-color-bg-fill-warning-secondary` → No storefront equivalent needed; warning UI lives in admin only
- Action: Accept divergence

### Storefront-only
- Hero gradient tokens (`--gradient-hero-from`, `--gradient-hero-to`) → No Polaris equivalent
- Action: Accept; gradients are storefront-specific

### Brand color override
- Polaris ships its own brand blue. Boldteq apps override with merchant's brand palette.
- Set `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` via Polaris's `AppProvider` theme prop or root CSS override.

## Implementation
- Storefront: ship `tokens.css` with `:root` + `.dark`
- Admin embed: in `App.tsx`, wrap in `<AppProvider i18n={...} theme={polarisTheme}>` where `polarisTheme` overrides brand color tokens
- Two CSS files load on different routes; no collision

## Verification
- Visual diff: open admin embed + storefront side-by-side; brand color should match
- Run contrast validation on both surfaces independently

## Source code template
File location: `apps/[stack-b-app]/lib/polaris-theme.ts`
```typescript
import type { ThemeName } from '@shopify/polaris-tokens';

export const polarisTheme = {
  colorScheme: 'light' as ThemeName,
  customProperties: {
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand': 'hsl(var(--color-primary))',
    '--p-color-text-brand-on-bg-fill': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-foreground))',
  },
};
```

---

## Curriculum v1 — Session 4 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** TOK-003 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-4-changelog.md`

### Storefront Wins on Brand Color (TOK-003)
**Rule:** Customer-facing storefront drives brand identity. Storefront brand color wins on conflicts.

**Implementation:**
```ts
// apps/[stack-b-app]/lib/polaris-theme.ts
import type { ThemeName } from '@shopify/polaris-tokens';

export const polarisTheme = {
  colorScheme: 'light' as ThemeName,
  customProperties: {
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand': 'hsl(var(--color-primary))',  // override Polaris navy
    '--p-color-text-brand-on-bg-fill': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-foreground))',
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand-hover': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-hover))',
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand-active': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-active))',
  },
};
```

**Polaris navy stays** for non-brand chrome:
- Border colors (`--p-color-border`)
- Subdued text (`--p-color-text-secondary`)
- Neutral backgrounds (`--p-color-bg-surface`)

**Why storefront wins:**
- Customer-facing primacy (brand identity = customer recognition)
- Single brand color across both surfaces (admin embed inherits storefront brand)
- Merchant trust preserved through Polaris structure (chrome = Polaris, accents = storefront)

**Anti-pattern:** Polaris navy bleeding into customer storefront (loses brand identity).

1	# Code Connect Mapping Protocol
2	
3	**Owner:** figma-synth
4	**Scope:** Bidirectional mapping between Figma components and codebase components.
5	
6	## Why
7	Designers inspect a Figma frame → see actual codebase component import + props, not auto-generated placeholder code.
8	
9	## Workflow
10	
11	### Step 1: Identify mapping candidates
12	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_suggestions` on project Figma file
13	- Returns components without mappings
14	- Cross-reference with codebase: `find components/ -name '*.tsx'`
15	
16	### Step 2: Generate `.figma.tsx` mapping file
17	
18	File location: `components/[name].figma.tsx` (alongside component source)
19	
20	Template:
21	```tsx
22	import { figma } from "@figma/code-connect"
23	import { Button } from "@/components/button"
24	
25	figma.connect(
26	  Button,
27	  "https://figma.com/file/[fileKey]/?node-id=[nodeId]",
28	  {
29	    props: {
30	      label: figma.string("Label"),
31	      variant: figma.enum("Variant", {
32	        "Primary": "primary",
33	        "Secondary": "secondary",
34	        "Ghost": "ghost",
35	        "Destructive": "destructive",
36	      }),
37	      size: figma.enum("Size", {
38	        "Small": "sm",
39	        "Medium": "md",
40	        "Large": "lg",
41	      }),
42	      disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
43	      onClick: () => console.log("clicked"),
44	    },
45	    example: ({ label, variant, size, disabled }) => (
46	      <Button variant={variant} size={size} disabled={disabled}>
47	        {label}
48	      </Button>
49	    ),
50	  }
51	)
52	```
53	
54	### Step 3: Register
55	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__add_code_connect_map` per component
56	- Then `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__send_code_connect_mappings` to publish to Figma
57	
58	### Step 4: Verify
59	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map` → confirm mapping registered
60	- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_context_for_code_connect` → confirm designer-facing snippet renders correctly
61	
62	## Maintenance
63	
64	### Daily sweep
65	- Run `get_code_connect_suggestions` to find newly added components without mappings
66	- For each, generate + register mapping
67	
68	### Weekly audit
69	- For each registered mapping, check codebase component prop signature
70	- If changed: update `.figma.tsx`, re-register
71	
72	### Breaking change protocol
73	- Component prop removed (e.g., `variant: 'success'` deleted)
74	- Update mapping immediately
75	- Notify Vega + designer working on that component
76	- If used in active Figma frames, suggest replacement variant
77	
78	## Common patterns
79	
80	### Boolean prop
81	```tsx
82	disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
83	```
84	
85	### Enum / variant
86	```tsx
87	variant: figma.enum("Variant", { "Primary": "primary", "Secondary": "secondary" }),
88	```
89	
90	### Text content
91	```tsx
92	title: figma.string("Title"),
93	```
94	
95	### Instance swap (for slots)
96	```tsx
97	icon: figma.instance("Icon"),
98	```
99	
100	### Children
101	```tsx
102	children: figma.children(["Heading", "Description"]),
103	```
104	
105	### Nested components
106	```tsx
107	header: figma.nestedProps("Header", {
108	  title: figma.string("Title"),
109	}),
110	```
111	
112	## Anti-patterns
113	- Never delete a mapping without deprecation notice
114	- Never let mapping drift > 24h after component prop change
115	- Never hardcode example component without using the prop variables
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Curriculum v1 — Session 5 Patches (2026-04-27)
120	
121	**Source:** FIG-002, FIG-004 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-5-changelog.md`
122	
123	### Naming Convention — Co-Located (FIG-002)
124	**Pattern:** `[component].figma.tsx` alongside source

# Code Connect Mapping Protocol

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Bidirectional mapping between Figma components and codebase components.

## Why
Designers inspect a Figma frame → see actual codebase component import + props, not auto-generated placeholder code.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Identify mapping candidates
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_suggestions` on project Figma file
- Returns components without mappings
- Cross-reference with codebase: `find components/ -name '*.tsx'`

### Step 2: Generate `.figma.tsx` mapping file

File location: `components/[name].figma.tsx` (alongside component source)

Template:
```tsx
import { figma } from "@figma/code-connect"
import { Button } from "@/components/button"

figma.connect(
  Button,
  "https://figma.com/file/[fileKey]/?node-id=[nodeId]",
  {
    props: {
      label: figma.string("Label"),
      variant: figma.enum("Variant", {
        "Primary": "primary",
        "Secondary": "secondary",
        "Ghost": "ghost",
        "Destructive": "destructive",
      }),
      size: figma.enum("Size", {
        "Small": "sm",
        "Medium": "md",
        "Large": "lg",
      }),
      disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
      onClick: () => console.log("clicked"),
    },
    example: ({ label, variant, size, disabled }) => (
      <Button variant={variant} size={size} disabled={disabled}>
        {label}
      </Button>
    ),
  }
)
```

### Step 3: Register
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__add_code_connect_map` per component
- Then `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__send_code_connect_mappings` to publish to Figma

### Step 4: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map` → confirm mapping registered
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_context_for_code_connect` → confirm designer-facing snippet renders correctly

## Maintenance

### Daily sweep
- Run `get_code_connect_suggestions` to find newly added components without mappings
- For each, generate + register mapping

### Weekly audit
- For each registered mapping, check codebase component prop signature
- If changed: update `.figma.tsx`, re-register

### Breaking change protocol
- Component prop removed (e.g., `variant: 'success'` deleted)
- Update mapping immediately
- Notify Vega + designer working on that component
- If used in active Figma frames, suggest replacement variant

## Common patterns

### Boolean prop
```tsx
disabled: figma.boolean("Disabled"),
```

### Enum / variant
```tsx
variant: figma.enum("Variant", { "Primary": "primary", "Secondary": "secondary" }),
```

### Text content
```tsx
title: figma.string("Title"),
```

### Instance swap (for slots)
```tsx
icon: figma.instance("Icon"),
```

### Children
```tsx
children: figma.children(["Heading", "Description"]),
```

### Nested components
```tsx
header: figma.nestedProps("Header", {
  title: figma.string("Title"),
}),
```

## Anti-patterns
- Never delete a mapping without deprecation notice
- Never let mapping drift > 24h after component prop change
- Never hardcode example component without using the prop variables

---

## Curriculum v1 — Session 5 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** FIG-002, FIG-004 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-5-changelog.md`

### Naming Convention — Co-Located (FIG-002)
**Pattern:** `[component].figma.tsx` alongside source

Examples:
- `components/button.tsx` + `components/button.figma.tsx`
- `components/product-card.tsx` + `components/product-card.figma.tsx`

**Why:**
- Easier to find when editing component (same dir)
- Git diff shows component + mapping changes together
- Standard Figma Code Connect doc convention
- Pod frontends grep `*.figma.tsx` to validate coverage

NOT: separate `__figma__/` dir, NOT subdir per component, NOT `.ts` extension.

### Breaking Change Protocol — 24h SLA (FIG-004)
When pod frontend changes/removes a prop on a Code-Connect-mapped component:

**Same-day actions (within 24h of weekly drift detection):**
1. Auto-update `.figma.tsx` mapping to remove deleted prop
2. Slack-notify vega
3. Query Figma file API for frames using affected component
4. Add in-Figma comment on each affected frame: "Component prop `X` deprecated. Update before next deploy. — figma-synth"
5. Log to `~/.claude/memory/design/sync-reports/breaking-changes-[YYYY-MM-DD].md`

**SLA:** 24h from drift detection to all designers notified. Don't accumulate breaking changes; resolve as detected.

## Shopify + Hydrogen-specific pipeline additions

### Server Component vs Client Component distinction
Hydrogen uses React Server Components. Figma-synth must know the split:
- **Server Components** (e.g., `ProductDetails.server.tsx`): no event handlers, no state — map props from Figma static layers
- **Client Components** (e.g., `AddToCartButton.client.tsx`): interactive, have state — map to interactive Figma variants (hover/active/disabled)

When `.server.tsx` suffix absent (standard RSC with `"use client"` directive):
- Check for `"use client"` directive at top of file
- Present → treat as client component for mapping purposes

### Hydrogen loader pattern
Hydrogen uses route loaders for data. Do NOT try to map loader data to Figma props.
Map the DISPLAY component, not the loader/action. Example:
```
// ✅ Map this — the display component
components/ProductCard.tsx  →  ProductCard.figma.tsx

// ✗ Don't map these — data shapes, not UI
app/routes/products.$handle.tsx  (route file, no Figma equivalent)
app/lib/cart.ts  (utility, no Figma equivalent)
```

### Metafield display components
Hydrogen PDPs enrich from Shopify metafields. When a component renders metafield data:
- `figma.string("Metafield")` → map to text override in Figma
- Example: `<IngredientsList metafield={product.metafield} />` → `ingredients: figma.string("Ingredients Text")`

### Shopify Figma UI Kit
- Shopify publishes official Figma library with Polaris Web Components
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_libraries` → check if Shopify UI Kit is linked to project
- **Admin components** should reference Polaris frames from Shopify UI Kit
- **Storefront components** are brand-custom — create in project file, do NOT reference Polaris

### File naming for Hydrogen projects
Hydrogen `app/` routes ≠ components. Only create `.figma.tsx` files for:
- `components/` — all shared UI
- `app/components/` — app-specific UI atoms
- Never for `app/routes/`, `app/lib/`, `app/graphql/`

## Coordination
- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)
- Hydrogen `@shopify/hydrogen` version bumps require prop signature re-audit

## Shopify + Hydrogen-specific pipeline additions

### Server Component vs Client Component distinction
Hydrogen uses React Server Components. Figma-synth must know the split:
- **Server Components** (e.g., `ProductDetails.server.tsx`): no event handlers, no state — map props from Figma static layers
- **Client Components** (e.g., `AddToCartButton.client.tsx`): interactive, have state — map to interactive Figma variants (hover/active/disabled)

When `.server.tsx` suffix absent (standard RSC with `"use client"` directive):
- Check for `"use client"` directive at top of file
- Present → treat as client component for mapping purposes

### Hydrogen loader pattern
Hydrogen uses route loaders for data. Do NOT try to map loader data to Figma props.
Map the DISPLAY component, not the loader/action. Example:
```
// ✅ Map this — the display component
components/ProductCard.tsx  →  ProductCard.figma.tsx

// ✗ Don't map these — data shapes, not UI
app/routes/products.$handle.tsx  (route file, no Figma equivalent)
app/lib/cart.ts  (utility, no Figma equivalent)
```

### Metafield display components
Hydrogen PDPs enrich from Shopify metafields. When a component renders metafield data:
- `figma.string("Metafield")` → map to text override in Figma
- Example: `<IngredientsList metafield={product.metafield} />` → `ingredients: figma.string("Ingredients Text")`

### Shopify Figma UI Kit
- Shopify publishes official Figma library with Polaris Web Components
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_libraries` → check if Shopify UI Kit is linked to project
- **Admin components** should reference Polaris frames from Shopify UI Kit
- **Storefront components** are brand-custom — create in project file, do NOT reference Polaris

### File naming for Hydrogen projects
Hydrogen `app/` routes ≠ components. Only create `.figma.tsx` files for:
- `components/` — all shared UI
- `app/components/` — app-specific UI atoms
- Never for `app/routes/`, `app/lib/`, `app/graphql/`

## Coordination
- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)
- Hydrogen `@shopify/hydrogen` version bumps require prop signature re-audit

# JSX→.fig Pipeline

**Owner:** figma-synth
**Scope:** Convert shipped TSX components to Figma `.fig` deliverables.

## Pipeline stages

### Stage 1: TS AST parse
- Read TSX source: `components/[name].tsx`
- Use TypeScript compiler API or `ts-morph` to extract:
  - Component name
  - Prop types (interface or type alias)
  - Variants (often via `cva()` from class-variance-authority)
  - Default values
  - State variants (loading, disabled, error)
  - Responsive breakpoints (Tailwind classes parsed for `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`)

### Stage 2: Render variant matrix
For each variant combination, determine the visual:
- Capture screenshots from a live storybook URL if project has Storybook running
- Or render mentally + use static screenshot for visual reference

### Stage 3: Token mapping
- Pull Token's variable map (`tokens.css` + Tailwind config)
- For each Tailwind class on the component, map to Figma variable
- Example: `bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-md` → Figma fill: `color/primary/default`, text color: `color/primary-foreground/default`, corner-radius: `radius/md`

### Stage 4: Build Figma component spec JSON
```json
{
  "name": "ProductCard",
  "type": "COMPONENT_SET",
  "variants": [
    {
      "props": {"variant": "default"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "borderId": "color/border",
      "radiusId": "radius/lg"
    },
    {
      "props": {"variant": "sale"},
      "fillId": "color/surface",
      "badgeFillId": "color/destructive",
      "borderId": "color/border"
    }
  ],
  "propsPanel": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "price", "type": "TEXT"},
    {"name": "image", "type": "INSTANCE_SWAP"},
    {"name": "variant", "type": "VARIANT", "options": ["default", "sale", "sold-out"]}
  ]
}
```

### Stage 5: Upload via Figma MCP
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__create_new_file` if no project Figma file exists
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__upload_assets` for any imagery referenced
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__use_figma` to write component to file

### Stage 6: Verify
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_design_context` on the new component
- `mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_screenshot` for visual verification
- Compare against codebase render — flag drift

## Edge cases
- Generic types (e.g., `<Button<T>>`) — fall back to heuristic parse, flag for manual review
- Conditional rendering (`{loading && <Spinner/>}`) — represent as variant
- Composition (e.g., `<Card><CardHeader/></Card>`) — represent as instance + slots

## Output deliverable
- One Figma component per JSX component
- Variant matrix complete
- Token-mapped (no hardcoded hex)
- Asset uploads complete

## Coordination
- Token's variable map must be fresh (sync within 7 days)
- Vega owns the project Figma file admin rights
- Pod frontend notifies on component changes (so Figma-Synth can re-sync)

---

## Curriculum v1 — Session 5 Patches (2026-04-27)

**Source:** FIG-001, FIG-006, FIG-007, FIG-008 · changelog: `~/.claude/memory/training/cycle-ecom-v1-session-5-changelog.md`

### Generic Type Heuristic Fallback (FIG-001)
For `<Button<T>>` / `<List<T>>` generic components:
1. Parse codebase usage sites for concrete T instances
2. Extract top 3 concrete types (e.g., `Button<string>`, `Button<User>`, `Button<Product>`)
3. Generate Figma variants for each concrete type
4. Tag component `generic-component-needs-review` in next weekly sync
5. Vega manually reviews flagged components, decides if generic or concrete-only mapping

Don't block pipeline; preserves dev velocity. Manual review catches edge cases.

### Token Drift — Block Upload (FIG-006)
When `tokens.css` drifted from Figma vars at upload time:
1. Block upload, return error to dispatcher
2. Dispatch token agent for emergency sync (4h SLA priority)
3. Token agent runs code→Figma push
4. After sync completes, figma-synth auto-retries upload
5. If sync times out (4h+), escalate to vega + flag deliverable as `pending-token-sync`

NEVER ship with stale tokens. NEVER fall back to inline hex (violates token-system anti-pattern).

### Variant Explosion Split (FIG-007)
Threshold: 30 variants per component-set (well below Figma 50-variant perf cliff).

**Split axis priority:**
1. **STATE** (default/hover/active/disabled) — splits cleanest for stateful components
2. **SIZE** (sm/md/lg/xl) — only if state-axis split insufficient
3. **VARIANT** (primary/secondary/destructive) — last resort

Example: ProductCard with 4 variants × 3 sizes × 2 states = 24 variants. Split into 3 component-sets:
- ProductCardDefault (4 var × 3 size = 12)
- ProductCardHover (4 var × 3 size = 12)
- ProductCardSoldOut (4 var × 3 size = 12)

Each component-set <30 variants. Designers swap between sets via instance swap.

### No Storybook Fallback (FIG-008)
When project lacks Storybook:
1. Auto-generate temp setup: `npx storybook init` + scaffold stories from JSX components
2. Use temp Storybook for figma-synth render captures
3. Log entry in `~/.claude/memory/projects/[project]/tech-debt.md` for project to formalize properly
4. Doesn't block deliverable — figma-synth ships using temp Storybook
5. Pod frontend canonicalizes Storybook config in next sprint

### Focus States
Polaris has opinionated focus rings (`--p-color-border-focus`, `--p-border-width-025`). Storefront uses Tailwind focus utilities.
```css
/* Storefront: override focus ring to match brand */
--color-ring: hsl(var(--color-primary));
--ring-offset: 2px;
```
In admin embed, never override `--p-color-border-focus` — Polaris focus ring is accessibility-required and accessibility-tested by Shopify.

### Full override reference for `polarisTheme.customProperties`
```typescript
export const polarisTheme = {
  colorScheme: 'light' as const,
  customProperties: {
    // Brand color
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand': 'hsl(var(--color-primary))',
    '--p-color-bg-fill-brand-hover': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-hover, var(--color-primary)))',

    '--p-color-text-link': 'hsl(var(--color-primary))',
    '--p-color-text-link-hover': 'hsl(var(--color-primary-hover, var(--color-primary)))',
    // Font (optional — Polaris defaults to Inter, skip if acceptable)
    // '--p-font-family-sans': 'var(--font-sans)',
  },
};
```
**Do NOT** override border, surface, or text colors — Polaris chrome depends on them for accessibility contrast.

| `--p-border-radius-050` | `rounded-sm` (2px) | Direct |

# Polaris ↔ Storefront Token Bridge

**Owner:** token
**Scope:** Stack B challenge — Shopify admin uses Polaris design system; storefront uses custom tokens. Brand must feel unified.

## The problem

Stack B apps embed in Shopify admin (Polaris-styled) AND ship a storefront the merchant's customers see (custom-styled). Two different design systems, same brand expectation.

Without a bridge: admin uses Polaris navy + Inter; storefront uses brand purple + Manrope. Merchants notice immediately.

## Mapping table (categories)

### Color
| Polaris token | Storefront token | Mapping rule |
|---------------|-----------------|--------------|
| `--p-color-bg-surface` | `--color-background` | Direct map (light/dark mode aware) |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` | `--color-primary` | Brand color overrides Polaris default |
| `--p-color-text` | `--color-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-text-secondary` | `--color-muted-foreground` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-border` | `--color-border` | Direct map |
| `--p-color-bg-fill-critical` | `--color-destructive` | Direct map |

### Typography
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-text-heading-2xl` | `text-4xl` | Semantic equivalent |
| `--p-text-heading-xl` | `text-3xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-lg` | `text-2xl` | |
| `--p-text-heading-md` | `text-xl` | |
| `--p-text-body-md` | `text-base` | |
| `--p-text-body-sm` | `text-sm` | |
| `--p-font-family-sans` | `font-sans` | Brand font preferred over Polaris default |

### Spacing
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-space-100` | `space-1` (4px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-200` | `space-2` (8px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-300` | `space-3` (12px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-400` | `space-4` (16px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-500` | `space-5` (20px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-600` | `space-6` (24px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-800` | `space-8` (32px) | Direct |
| `--p-space-1200` | `space-12` (48px) | Direct |

### Motion
| Polaris | Storefront | Mapping |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `--p-motion-duration-100` | `--duration-instant` (100ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-200` | `--duration-fast` (200ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-300` | `--duration-base` (300ms) | Direct |
| `--p-motion-duration-500` | `--duration-slow` (500ms) | Direct |

## Gaps + decisions

### Polaris-only (no storefront equivalent)
- `--p-color-bg-fill-warning-secondary` → No storefront equivalent needed; warning UI lives in admin only
- Action: Accept divergence

### Storefront-only
- Hero gradient tokens (`--gradient-hero-from`, `--gradient-hero-to`) → No Polaris equivalent
- Action: Accept; gradients are storefront-specific

### Brand color override
- Polaris ships its own brand blue. Boldteq apps override with merchant's brand palette.
- Set `--p-color-bg-fill-brand` via Polaris's `AppProvider` theme prop or root CSS override.

## Implementation
- Storefront: ship `tokens.css` with `:root` + `.dark`
- Admin embed: in `App.tsx`, wrap in `<AppProvider i18n={...} theme={polarisTheme}>` where `polarisTheme` overrides brand color tokens
- Two CSS files load on different routes; no collision

## Verification
- Visual diff: open admin embed + storefront side-by-side; brand color should match
- Run contrast validation on both surfaces independently

File location: `apps/[stack-b-app]/lib/polaris-theme.ts`

export const polarisTheme = {
  colorScheme: 'light' as ThemeName,
